candidates.fulltext: IntroductionInterstitial lung disease (ILD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with rheumatic diseases (RDs), including rheumatoid arthritis, systemic sclerosis, inflammatory myopathies, other connective tissue diseases, and systemic vasculitis (1, 2). Acute exacerbation (AE) of RD-associated ILD (AE-RD-ILD) is a severe clinical complication characterised by acute, clinically significant respiratory deterioration, usually within less than 1 month, with new extensive alveolar abnormalities in patients with a known or concurrently diagnosed RD (3). The aetiology and pathogenesis of AE-RD-ILD remain incompletely understood, but potential triggers include infection, mechanical stress, microaspiration, and disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs) (4, 5). Reported mortality after AE-RD-ILD remains high, particularly among patients requiring ventilatory support (6, 7). Even among survivors, persistent impairment in respiratory function and worsening dyspnoea can markedly affect quality of life and long-term survival (6, 7). Optimising treatment for AE-RD-ILD is therefore a pressing clinical need, especially in the setting of post-viral respiratory deterioration after COVID-19 and other respiratory infections (8).High-dose corticosteroids remain the mainstay of acute management for AE-RD-ILD, but the optimal dose and duration and the role of adjunctive immunosuppressive therapy remain uncertain. Current management is largely empirical and may include cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate mofetil, calcineurin inhibitors, and other conventional or targeted synthetic DMARDs. These approaches may be limited by variable efficacy, cumulative toxicity, and infection risk in already immunocompromised patients (3).Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is involved in both acute inflammatory lung injury and fibrotic remodelling. Experimental studies suggest that IL-6 can regulate CD4+ T-cell-mediated responses and contribute to lung injury through effects on inflammatory cell activation, epithelial injury, extracellular matrix deposition, and protease release (9). IL-6 also intersects with JAK/STAT signalling and fibroblast activation pathways, providing a biologically plausible rationale for IL-6 blockade in inflammatory-fibrotic lung disease (10, 11).Clinically, IL-6 receptor inhibition with tocilizumab has shown benefit in chronic ILD stabilisation, particularly in systemic sclerosis-associated ILD, and has been used in rheumatoid arthritis with ILD (12, 13). Tocilizumab also improved outcomes in selected hospitalised patients with severe COVID-19 pneumonia requiring oxygen therapy (14). However, its role in acute-phase AE-RD-ILD remains uncertain. Unlike primary viral pneumonia, AE-RD-ILD often develops on a background of established immune-mediated lung disease and may reflect post-infectious immune dysregulation, uncontrolled inflammation, and early fibrotic repair rather than direct viral cytopathic injury alone.We therefore evaluated the short-term effectiveness and safety of tocilizumab in hospitalised patients with AE-RD-ILD by comparing patients treated with tocilizumab with a contemporaneous control group receiving corticosteroid-based conventional immunosuppressive therapy. We focused on clinically meaningful respiratory recovery, including oxygen requirement, radiological improvement, and successful glucocorticoid tapering.Materials and methodsStudy design and patientsBetween January 2023 and December 2024, this single-centre ambispective observational cohort study included hospitalised adults meeting the diagnostic criteria for AE-RD-ILD, characterised by acute respiratory deterioration with new extensive alveolar abnormalities in patients with a known or concurrently diagnosed RD (3). The tocilizumab cohort was enrolled and followed prospectively, whereas comparator data were assembled retrospectively from the same centre and study period. Common diagnostic eligibility criteria and additional treatment eligibility criteria for the prospective tocilizumab cohort are detailed in Supplementary Data S1. Patients with severe comorbidities or alternative causes of acute respiratory failure, such as heart failure or pulmonary embolism, were excluded.We also retrospectively included patients with AE-RD-ILD treated with prednisone alone, conventional disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (cDMARDs), or targeted synthetic DMARDs (tsDMARDs) without tocilizumab as the control group. Controls were selected from the same study centre and managed by independent clinical teams according to routine practice.The study was conducted under an institutional rheumatology cohort protocol approved by the Ethics Committee of Renji Hospital. Treatment decisions were made by the treating physicians and were not assigned by a trial protocol. Written informed consent was obtained from each participating patient or designated surrogate where required by the approved protocol.Treatment of AE in tocilizumab groupTreatment for AE-RD-ILD

candidates.title: Construction and application of a disease progression model for the placebo group in clinical trials of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study is to quantitatively describe the characteristics of disease progression and its influencing factors in the placebo group of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis clinical trials, and to provide evidence for the optimal design of clinical trials.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase and Cochrane Library were searched for placebo-randomized controlled trials on IPF up to November 12, 2024. We conducted a time-course modeling analysis of the placebo group based on commonly reported evaluation indicators in clinical trials. Using the established model, we simulated the distribution of the placebo effect for each index under various conditions and applied this to provide a quantitative external control.
RESULTS: A total of 32 studies were included. Common evaluation measures in clinical trials include all-cause mortality, forced vital capacity (FVC), 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) and Diffusing Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide (DLCO). Based on the final model, this study simulated typical effect sizes after different times of placebo intervention. Subgroup analysis showed that background treatment and gender also showed consistent trends in the effects on the above efficacy indicators. The potential utility of this model in drug effectiveness evaluation is demonstrated through a preliminary case study.
CONCLUSIONS: This study established a disease progression model for the placebo group based on common evaluation indicators in IPF clinical trials. This model helps conserve valuable clinical resources for rare diseases and promotes the development of new drugs.
STUDY REGISTRATION: The study strictly followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines (Supplementary Material) and was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (registration ID: CRD42024557923).
candidates.fulltext: IntroductionIdiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is an etiologically obscure chronic fibrosing lung disease primarily affecting middle-aged and older men, with an incidence that increases with age [1–2]. The primary symptoms of IPF include persistent pulmonary fibrosis, leading to worsening dyspnea, declining lung function, and reduced exercise tolerance, all of which significantly impair patients’ quality of life and are associated with a generally poor prognosis [3–4]. Studies indicate that untreated patients have a median survival time of approximately 3 to 5 years from diagnosis to death [5]. As IPF is irreversible, it severely impacts patients’ physical and mental health and self-care abilities, imposing significant burdens on families and the healthcare system [6].Pharmacotherapy is the primary treatment modality for IPF. According to the latest clinical practice guidelines by the ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT [7], the primary medications currently recommended are pirfenidone and nintedanib. These drugs have been proven to extend patients’ survival and slow disease progression to some extent. However, to date, IPF remains incurable [8]. Consequently, there is an unmet need for safe and effective therapeutic drugs, making the development of new treatment strategies a matter of urgency.In the development of drugs for IPF, placebo-controlled randomized trials are considered the gold standard for assessing the efficacy of new medications [9]. Thus, a thorough understanding of the disease progression in the placebo groups of IPF clinical trials, including its influencing factors, is crucial for optimizing clinical trial design and evaluating drug efficacy.In IPF clinical trials, the measurement of lung function, particularly Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) and Diffusing Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide (DLCO), is widely regarded as key indicators for assessing treatment response [10–11]. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved pirfenidone and nintedanib primarily based on their effects on FVC. Additionally, all-cause mortality and the Six-Minute Walk Distance (6MWD) are also commonly used as important clinical endpoints in IPF trials [12–13].IPF is classified as a rare disease, and due to limited clinical resources, significant challenges arise in confirming the efficacy of new medications [14]. This situation may prevent many drugs with therapeutic potential from being thoroughly researched, thus limiting their application and development in the treatment of IPF. To alleviate the issue of strained clinical resources, in early clinical trials, it is feasible to consider utilizing historical placebo data from existing IPF clinical trials as an external control group. This approach can help to identify and select drug candidates with potential for further development, allowing them to proceed to subsequent confirmatory clinical trials. This approach not only effectively mitigates the shortage of clinical resources and reduces research costs but also encourages greater patient participation in clinical trials of new drugs. However, it is important to note that due to heterogeneity between trials, significant differences may exist between historical placebo group data and current trial groups, which could impact the accurate assessment of drug efficacy.This study aims to construct a time-course model for the placebo group in IPF clinical trials, based on an extensive review of literature data and selecting key clinical indices such as FVC, DLCO, all-cause mortality, and 6MWD. The model is intended to quantitatively describe the characteristics of disease progression and its influencing factors within the placebo group. This analysis is expected to provide quantitative external controls for the design of IPF clinical trials and the development of new medications, thereby conserving valuable clinical resources for rare diseases and facilitating the development of new treatments in this field.MethodsResearch criteria and eligibilityTo comprehensively collect placebo-controlled randomized trials of drug treatments for IPF, this study conducted a literature search across three databases: PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library. The search covered the period from the inception of each database up to November 12, 2024. To avoid omitting relevant studies, this research also manually searched the references cited in related reviews and systematic evaluations. Search strategy details and inclusion/exclusion criteria are available in the Supplementary.Data extraction and quality assessmentInformation such as literature characteristics, trial design-related characteristics, participants’ characteristics and clinical outcomes were extracted. See the Supplementary for the detailed data extraction.The quality of the included literature was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool 2.0 [15]. The specific information is detailed in the Supplementary.Model establishment and evaluationThis study aimed to establish a time

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Lung Diseases: Screening, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prognosis.
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary diseases currently pose significant threats to global health, spanning common chronic conditions including lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and asthma, as well as infectious and inflammatory diseases like tuberculosis, interstitial lung disease (ILD), and COVID-19. Therefore, accurate diagnosis, effective therapeutic strategies, and reliable assessment of prognosis for pulmonary diseases are essential for improving patient outcomes and safeguarding public health. Despite the increasing availability of medical imaging and pathological data owing to improvements in detection technologies, what is becoming increasingly evident are the limitations of conventional diagnosis, which relies solely on clinicians' subjective judgment based on imaging, pulmonary function, pathology, and clinical experience. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) technology, especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has made significant progress in areas such as image recognition and model construction. Numerous studies have demonstrated the widespread application of AI in the screening and diagnosis of lung diseases, the optimization of treatment strategies, and prognosis assessment, revealing its remarkable ability to process and interpret complex clinical data. Although concerns persist regarding data quality, the "black box" nature of algorithms, clinical practice, and the regulatory landscape, the application of AI in lung disease research and clinical care is more and more promising. In this review, we summarize the latest advances of AI in the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary diseases, analyze the challenges and limitations of current AI technologies ranging from data and algorithms to clinical translation, and highlight directions for future research.

candidates.title: Comparison of Adverse Event Incidence between Japanese and Non-Japanese: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis for Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, and Atrial Fibrillation/Venous Thromboembolism.
candidates.abstract: Enhancing diversity in clinical trial populations is increasingly important, particularly for underrepresented populations. We focused on adverse events (AEs) that have been reported to be more frequent in Japanese than in non-Japanese populations and assessed their plausibility. We conducted a systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 24 multiregional clinical trials (MRCTs): 9 in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), 11 in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and 4 in atrial fibrillation (AF) or venous thromboembolism (VTE). Pooled estimates of the odds ratios (ORs) compared the incidence of targeted AEs between Japanese and non-Japanese participants using a random-effects model. For Janus kinase inhibitors in RA, the OR for the incidence of herpes zoster was 2.50 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.18-5.29, p = 0.0172), suggesting more frequent occurrence in Japanese participants than in non-Japanese participants. The incidence of pneumonia was statistically higher in Japanese in most COPD treatment groups and in the placebo group (OR 4.03 [95% CI: 1.33-12.19, p = 0.0135] for placebo). For direct oral anticoagulants for AF/VTE, the OR for major bleeding was 1.19 (95% CI: 0.91-1.56, p = 0.2105), with no statistically significant difference observed between Japanese and non-Japanese participants. This meta-analysis supported a higher incidence of herpes zoster in Japanese patients with RA, whereas the findings for pneumonia in COPD should be interpreted cautiously, and no statistically significant difference was observed for major bleeding in AF/VTE. Broader inclusion of Japanese participants in MRCTs may improve the interpretability of safety findings and the understanding of population-related differences in drug safety profiles.

candidates.title: Noradrenergic input from sympathetic nerves to fibroblasts regulates lung fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis is a progressive, irreversible condition in which expansion of effector fibroblasts and extracellular matrix obliterates alveolar gas exchange regions of the lung through incompletely understood mechanisms. We found sympathetic nerve fibers in fibrotic alveolar regions enriched for alpha-smooth muscle actin-positive (α-SMA+) effector fibroblasts and noradrenaline by applying optical clearing and whole-lung imaging to the bleomycin mouse model of lung fibrosis and multichannel immunofluorescence to explanted lung tissues from patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) or systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD). Human lung fibroblasts cultured with sympathetic nerves displayed enhanced production of fibrotic markers, and sympathetic nerve-specific deletion of the nerve growth factor receptor neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase 1 mitigated bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis in mice. Pharmacologic inhibition of noradrenaline receptors, including α1-adrenoreceptors, mitigated collagen accumulation and pathologic remodeling in bleomycin-challenged mice and in human precision-cut lung slices. Accumulation of α-SMA+ effector fibroblasts expressing α1-adrenoreceptor subtype D (ADRA1D) was observed in fibrotic mouse lungs and in explanted lung tissues from patients with IPF or SSc-ILD. Therapeutic deletion of Adra1d in α-SMA+ effector fibroblasts suppressed fibrosis in the bleomycin model. Secondary analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from IPF or SSc-ILD lung explants revealed α1-adrenoreceptor antagonist-responsive, disease-specific programs in effector fibroblasts. Together, these studies show that a fibrogenic unit comprising sympathetic nerve-derived noradrenaline and ADRA1D+ effector fibroblasts promotes lung fibrosis in disease-relevant modeling systems. Strategies targeting sympathetic innervation or α1-adrenoreceptors may provide previously unrecognized therapeutic opportunities in IPF, SSc-ILD, and relate

candidates.title: Novel Molecular Mechanisms of Dioctyl Phthalate-Induced Pulmonary Fibrosis: Insights From Network Toxicology, Single-Cell RNA Sequencing, and In Vitro Studies.
candidates.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
candidates.abstract: Phthalate plasticizers have been implicated in respiratory diseases, but their role in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) pathogenesis remains unclear. This study employed an integrative approach combining network toxicology, bioinformatics, and experimental validation to investigate the impact of three common phthalates (PAEs) - diethyl phthalate (DEP), dimethyl phthalate (DMP), and dioctyl phthalate (DOP) - on pulmonary fibrosis pathogenesis. Network toxicology predicted DOP to be the most toxic of the three. By intersecting phthalate-related genes with IPF-associated differentially expressed genes from public datasets and applying bioinformatics analyses, we identified three core biomarkers: ALDH3A1, AVPR1A and GPBAR1, all of which had strong diagnostic value. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed predominant GPBAR1 expression in macrophages and monocytes, with significant downregulation in IPF samples. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations predicted stable binding between DOP and GPBAR1. In vitro experiments confirmed that DOP exposure downregulated GPBAR1 in human alveolar macrophages, promoted the release of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic cytokines, suppressed the expression of ribosomal proteins, and induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in co-cultured alveolar epithelial cells as well as fibroblast activation. Importantly, GPBAR1 overexpression attenuated these DOP-induced effects. This study identified GPBAR1 as the key PAE-associated biomarkers in IPF alveolar macrophages and suggested that DOP may exacerbate pulmonary fibrosis by promoting inflammation, EMT and fibroblast activation, potentially through GPBAR1 downregulation and subsequent ribosomal dysregulation in alveolar macrophages. Further in vivo investigations are required to validate these translational implications.

candidates.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Pulmonary Fibrosis Imaging Research: Knowledge Graph Construction Based on the Web of Science Core Database.
candidates.journal: Malawi medical journal : the journal of Medical Association of Malawi
candidates.abstract:
AIM: To quantify publication trends, map international collaboration networks, and identify dominant and emerging research themes in Pulmonary fibrosis(PF) imaging (2015-2024).
METHODS: A structured Web of Science search combining PF- and imaging-related terms yielded 1,159 English-language original research articles. Analyses employed CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Scimago Graphica for trend assessment, keyword co-occurrence, citation burst detection, and collaboration network visualization.
RESULTS: Annual publication volume showed sustained linear growth (R2 = 0.867). Researchers from 64 countries contributed; the United States led in output (332 publications) and citation impact (9,821 citations), while China ranked second in volume (224 publications) with lower proportional citation impact. The Western Europe-North America axis showed the densest collaborative ties. Keyword co-occurrence revealed close thematic links among idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP), survival, and mortality. Citation burst analysis identified "deep learning" as the strongest and most sustained burst (2021-2024), by which point it had shifted from exploratory method to established domain. Three overlapping research phases emerged: diagnostic framework consolidation (2015-2018), computational computed tomography (CT)-based phenotyping (2016-2022), and therapeutic expansion toward antifibrotics and progressive fibrosing interstitial lung disease (2019-2024).
CONCLUSION: PF imaging research has shifted from diagnostic consensus toward quantitative CT biomarkers and artificial intelligence(AI)-driven phenotyping, driven by the need to reduce interobserver variability and enable individualized risk stratification. Geographic fragmentation and limited multicenter validation remain key barriers to AI generalizability. Future priorities include standardized imaging protocols, prospective multicenter validation cohorts, and int

candidates.title: Therapeutic effects of PolyPHb on bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis: implications for improved oxygenation.
candidates.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive, irreversible, and fatal interstitial lung disease of unknown cause, characterized by severe dyspnea, restrictive lung function, impaired gas exchange, and progressive destruction of pulmonary tissue. While approved drugs can slow disease progression, improving patients' quality of life remains a critical challenge. PolyPHb, a hemoglobin-based oxygen carrier (HBOC) derived from virally inactivated and purified human placental hemoglobin, efficiently transports and releases oxygen. In this study, we show that PolyPHb enhances exercise tolerance and mitigates inflammation and fibrosis in a bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis mouse model. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, we performed transcriptomic analysis of lung tissues following PolyPHb treatment, revealing potential regulatory networks involved in its protective effects. These results provide new insights into potential interventions of PolyPHb in IPF and suggest that it may contribute to improved functional outcomes, though further studies are needed to fully define its impact on exercise capacity and quality of life.

candidates.title: Environmental risk factors in Juvenile dermatomyositis: a systematic review.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) is a rare autoimmune vasculopathy of childhood. Alongside genetic predisposition, environmental exposures are thought to influence when the disease begins and how it progresses. Despite many reports, the evidence base is fragmented, with few studies able to draw firm conclusions.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review according to PRISMA 2020 standards, searching six major databases and conference proceedings (2005-2025). Eligible studies investigated environmental, infectious, chemical, physical, lifestyle, or psychosocial exposures in children with JDM. Two reviewers independently screened articles, extracted data, and assessed study quality using NIH and ROBINS-E tools. Results were summarized by exposure type.
RESULTS: One hundred forty-eight studies were included. Ultraviolet (UV) radiation was the most consistently reported factor, with recent sun exposure often preceding onset or chronic disease, particularly in defined autoantibody subgroups. Infections, especially viral and respiratory, were frequently described as triggers of onset or relapse. Air pollutants and maternal exposures during pregnancy also emerged as significant risks. Psychosocial stress, including early adversity and pandemic-related distress, was linked to flares. By contrast, structured exercise, particularly aquatic therapy, improved fitness and fatigue without worsening disease.
CONCLUSIONS: Multiple modifiable environmental influences appear relevant in JDM. Strategies such as UV protection, minimizing pollutant exposure, and tailored exercise may benefit patients. Well-designed, prospective studies are urgently needed to clarify causal pathways and inform prevention.
PROSPERO: Registration number: CRD42024595442PROSPERO.

candidates.title: Imatinib as a Modulator of Lung Mechanotransduction: Reverting the Fibrotic Feedback Loop.
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis continues to pose a substantial clinical challenge, characterized by relentless progression, limited therapeutic avenues, and poor prognosis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current insights into extracellular matrix remodeling, mechanotransduction pathways, and canonical signaling networks operating in the fibrotic lung, with emphasis on how mechanical cues are translated into enduring pro-fibrotic gene expression programs. The involvement of the tyrosine kinase c-abl is explored as a potential central mediator within fibrotic feedback mechanisms. Additionally, the interplay between aging, cellular senescence, and disease pathogenesis is discussed, focusing on the role of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) in fostering a persistent pro-fibrotic microenvironment. Against this background, the therapeutic potential of imatinib is evaluated for its capacity to modulate c-abl-driven signaling and interrupt self-sustaining fibrotic loops. Taken together, these observations point toward a conceptual model wherein targeting critical integrative signaling hubs may offer a promising approach to counter the self-perpetuating nature of progressive fibrotic lung disease.

candidates.title: Interstitial Lung Disease in Connective Tissue Disease.
candidates.journal: Rheumatic diseases clinics of North America
candidates.abstract: Connective tissue disease, also referred to as collagen vascular disease, encompasses a group of systemic inflammatory disorders characterized by autoimmune-mediated end-organ damage. Connective tissue diseases may result in a variety of interstitial lung disease patterns on computed tomography including usual interstitial pneumonia, nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP), organizing pneumonia and lymphoid interstitial pneumonia, with NSIP being the most common. As interstitial lung disease may be the only manifestation of connective tissue disease or present years before positive serologies, radiologists must be familiar with these patterns to provide diagnostic value.

candidates.title: Mouse Models of Systemic Manifestations in Sjögren's Disease.
candidates.journal: Rheumatic diseases clinics of North America
candidates.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disorder, yet research in mouse models has centered on glandular disease rather than the systemic manifestations driving morbidity and mortality. This article evaluates how well mouse models reproduce the systemic features of SjD, using the organ systems that define disease activity in patients as a benchmark. We focus on pulmonary and renal disease, where data are most developed. No single model captures the heterogeneity of SjD, so individual models may best represent distinct patient endotypes. Advancing the field will require systematically assessing existing models and building new ones for underrepresented manifestations.

candidates.title: Rheumatologic Issues in Women and Rehabilitation.
candidates.journal: Rheumatic diseases clinics of North America
candidates.abstract: This article discusses rheumatologic conditions in women including rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, Sjogren's syndrome, inflammatory myopathies, systemic sclerosis, and polymyalgia rheumatica. These conditions, often affecting muscles, joints, and other organ systems, require early diagnosis and multidisciplinary management. Treatment includes medications, braces, therapy services, education, and lifestyle modifications including energy conservation techniques. These conditions can also impact pregnancy and require close monitoring and careful disease control. It also highlights the benefits of pulmonary rehabilitation that can be helpful for patients with chronic respiratory disease secondary to their rheumatologic conditions.

candidates.title: Long-Term Prognosis and Transition Period until Progression in Fibrotic Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.
candidates.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP) is an interstitial lung disease that may present as fibrotic (fHP) or non-fibrotic (nfHP). Fibrosis is associated with progression and poor outcomes; however, the transition to progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) and its predictors remain unclear.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adult patients diagnosed with HP at a tertiary hospital (2010 and 2022). Patients were classified as having fHP or nfHP and were followed up for at least 1 year. Clinical, functional, radiological, and histological variables were analyzed. PPF was defined according to the 2022 clinical practice guideline of the American Thoracic Society (ATS), European Respiratory Society (ERS), Japanese Respiratory Society (JRS), and Asociación Latinoamericana de Tórax (ALAT).
RESULTS: Of 298 HP patients, 191 were included (153 fHP and 38 nfHP). Among patients with fHP, 76 (49.7%) developed PPF after a median of 3.2 years. Median survival was 4.8 years in fHP with PPF versus 6.3 years without, with 1.6 years from PPF onset to death or transplantation. The independent predictors of PPF and survival were lower forced vital capacity, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, fibroblastic foci, and microscopic honeycombing.
CONCLUSION: Nearly half of fHP patients progressed to PPF within a few years, with markedly reduced survival. Early recognition of high-risk patients may support timely antifibrotic treatment and improve outcomes.

candidates.title: Quantitative CT Phenotypes and Prognosis in Combined Pulmonary Fibrosis and Emphysema.
candidates.abstract: Background Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema (CPFE) has heterogeneous outcomes, and visual assessment or separate measurement of emphysema and fibrosis does not directly identify which structural component predominates in an individual patient. Purpose To determine whether quantitative CT enables objective stratification of CPFE into fibrosis-dominant and emphysema-dominant phenotypes and to evaluate their distinct clinical trajectories and prognostic implications. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis of a prospective multicenter observational study included patients with CPFE enrolled between January 2017 and December 2024. A fixed commercial artificial intelligence workstation automatically segmented the lungs and quantified emphysema and fibrosis on high-resolution CT scans. Participants were classified as having the fibrosis-dominant phenotype when the fibrosis percentage was equal to or greater than the emphysema percentage, and as having the emphysema-dominant phenotype otherwise. Group comparisons used the t test, Wilcoxon rank-sum test, χ2 test, or Fisher exact test. Cox models were used to assess all-cause mortality; C index and calibration were used to assess model performance. Results The study population included 1583 participants (median age, 65 years [IQR, 58-71 years]; 1186 men); 823 (52%) had the fibrosis-dominant phenotype, and 760 (48%) had the emphysema-dominant phenotype. The fibrosis-dominant group had a higher fibrosis percentage than the emphysema-dominant group (median, 18% vs 10%; P < .001), whereas the emphysema-dominant group had a higher emphysema percentage (median, 7% vs 6%; P < .001). During a median follow-up of 2.59 years, 513 deaths occurred. The fibrosis-dominant phenotype was associated with higher mortality after adjustment (hazard ratio, 1.36 [95% CI: 1.13, 1.62]; P < .001). Conclusion Quantitative CT helped identify emphysema- and fibrosis-dominant CPFE phenotypes with different prognoses. The fibrosis-dominant

candidates.title: Endothelial Activation and Stress Index and Radiation Pneumonitis Risk After Thoracic Radiotherapy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
candidates.abstract: Radiation pneumonitis (RP) is a clinically important toxicity after thoracic radiotherapy, and risk assessment should account for treatment dose, systemic therapy, and host response. This retrospective single-center study evaluated whether the endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) adds predictive information for Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v5.0 grade ≥2 RP within 6 months after completion of radiotherapy. Clinical, laboratory, treatment, and dosimetric data from 242 patients with non-small cell lung cancer were analyzed. Model A was the clinical-treatment-dosimetric model and included tumor stage, mean lung dose, radiotherapy technique, concurrent chemoradiotherapy, and immune checkpoint inhibitor exposure; Model B was the clinical-treatment-dosimetric model plus EASIX. Discrimination, calibration, repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation, and 1,000-resample bootstrap validation were assessed. Grade ≥2 RP occurred in 59 patients (grade 2, n=35; grade 3, n=20; grade 4, n=4). Model A achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.826 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.766-0.887), whereas Model B achieved an AUC of 0.903 (95% CI, 0.855-0.951; DeLong p = 0.003). Bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC was 0.886, and the corrected calibration slope was 0.870. The final Youden cutoff was 2.005; EASIX alone had 52.5% sensitivity and therefore should not be used as a standalone test. EASIX may complement established clinical and dosimetric factors for RP risk stratification, but external validation is required.

candidates.title: 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT: a new horizon for evaluating pulmonary involvement in MDA5+ dermatomyositis.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: MDA5+ dermatomyositis (MDA5+DM) frequently complicates interstitial lung disease (ILD), especially rapidly progressive ILD (RP-ILD), which worsens prognosis. Traditional assessments cannot directly reflect fibroblast activation status, a key driver of pulmonary fibrosis. 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT targets fibroblast activation protein (FAP), but its value in MDA5+DM remains understudied.
METHODS: Fourteen MDA5+DM patients and 5 controls were enrolled. 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT was performed to obtain SUVmax of lungs, muscles, and other organs. Clinical data, pulmonary function tests, and deep learning-quantified HRCT indices were collected. Follow-ups for pulmonary function and HRCT were conducted. Correlations between SUVmax, clinical features, and follow-up outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: Whole-lung SUVmax was significantly higher in MDA5+DM patients (3.32 vs. 0.67, p < 0.0001), with left lower lobe showing the most prominent difference (p = 0.0003). SUVmax strongly correlated with HRCT inflammation/fibrosis indices (e.g., left lower lobe vs. PII at 3 months: r = 0.9863, p < 0.0001) and small-to-medium airway function (lung vs. MMEF 75/25: r=-0.8168, p = 0.0133). Baseline SUVmax predicted 3-12-month lesion progression and lung function changes, with deceased patients having higher baseline whole-lung SUVmax (p = 0.008).
CONCLUSION: This exploratory study suggests that 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT may reflect fibroblast activation and the active inflammatory-fibrotic process, assesses early pulmonary impairments and monitoring lesion progression in MDA5+DM. It provides a valuable hypothesis-generating tool for clinical evaluation, warranting further validation.

candidates.title: Echo pattern characteristics on radial endobronchial ultrasonography and their diagnostic implications.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Visual assessment using radial endobronchial ultrasonography (R-EBUS) remains subjective. The current study aimed to examine characteristic echo patterns-including heterogeneity, hyperechoic areas, and vascular visibility-and to validate their diagnostic implications for differentiating malignant from benign peripheral pulmonary lesions.
METHODS: Sixty-eight peripheral pulmonary lesions were retrospectively analyzed. From representative R-EBUS images, three rectangular regions of interest were placed at proximal (near the probe) and distal (deeper within the lesion) locations. The mean and standard deviation (SD) of grayscale intensity were calculated, and visual findings such as hyperechoic areas and vessel patency were evaluated by two independent observers. Discrepancies were resolved by a third reviewer. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of malignancy.
RESULTS: Malignant lesions had a significantly higher SD of grayscale intensity in the proximal region than benign ones (11.14 ± 0.19 vs 10.18 ± 0.33, p = 0.015). Grayscale intensity remained an independent predictor of malignancy in the multivariate analysis (adjusted odds ratio: 1.91, 95% confidence interval: 1.20-3.33, p = 0.006). Based on an analysis across diagnostic subtypes, malignant lesions generally had a higher proximal SD. Meanwhile, both malignant and benign lesions exhibited substantial variability in terms of grayscale intensity and internal echo patterns. Hyperechoic structures were common in adenocarcinoma and organizing pneumonia. However, they were rarely observed in metastatic lesions and small-cell carcinoma. Vessels were frequently found in organizing pneumonia but were absent in fungal/mycobacterial infections.
CONCLUSIONS: Distinct echo pattern characteristics on R-EBUS reflect the internal architecture of pulmonary lesions. Further, they provide diagnostic implications for differentiating malignant from be

candidates.title: Homozygous NOP10 variant presenting with severe pulmonary fibrosis and multisystem involvement: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Genetic factors play an important role in the pathogenesis of interstitial lung diseases. Recent studies have shown that approximately 30% of familial interstitial lung diseases are associated with mutations in telomere-related genes. Herein, we present a young patient with severe pulmonary fibrosis and multisystem involvement in whom a homozygous NOP10 variant was identified.
CASE REPORT: A 29-year-old man presented with progressive exertional dyspnea, cough, and fever. Thoracic computed tomography demonstrated a probable usual interstitial pneumonia pattern. Laboratory investigations showed anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, and elevated lactate dehydrogenase levels, while hematological evaluation revealed a hypocellular bone marrow. Abdominal imaging demonstrated findings compatible with chronic liver disease. Due to parental consanguinity and a positive family history, alpha-1 antitrypsin analysis and whole-exome sequencing (WES) were performed. Despite treatment, his clinical condition continued to deteriorate, with progression to multiorgan failure, and he died on the 21st day of hospitalization. Genetic results obtained after the patient's death revealed the presence of the alpha-1 antitrypsin Pi*M/P Lowell variant and the homozygous NOP10 variant.
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, to the best of our knowledge, this case is the first to describe a patient with a homozygous NOP10 p.Arg34Trp variant who presented with severe pulmonary fibrosis and multisystem involvement in the absence of the classic mucocutaneous triad of dyskeratosis congenita (nail dystrophy, reticular skin pigmentation, and oral leukoplakia).

candidates.title: Determinants of Torque teno virus Replication Across Early and Long-Term Post-Transplant Periods in a Large Multiorgan Transplant Population.
candidates.abstract: Torque teno virus (TTV) viral load is a promising biomarker for immune monitoring in solid organ transplantation, but interindividual variability limits its clinical interpretation. This study aimed to identify TTV viral load (TTV VL) determinants to improve its applicability. In this single-center cross-sectional study, TTV VL was measured between 2013 and 2021, in 477 kidney (KTR) and 240 lung transplant recipients (LTR). Factors associated with high TTV viral load, defined using the third-quartile cutoff (≥ 5.7 log10 copies/mL), were analyzed separately in KTRs and LTRs and in the pooled cohort. Mean TTV VL was 4.64 (1.94) log10 copies/mL, higher in LTR than KTR (5.04 vs. 4.44, p < 0.001). Female sex, an eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, and shorter time since transplantation were independently associated with high TTV VL in both KTRs and LTRs. Additional independent associations in KTRs included tacrolimus, steroid, and rituximab exposure, a leukocyte count < 5.25 × 109/L and no history of cardiovascular event; in LTRs, they included greater immunosuppressive intensity, fibrosing interstitial lung disease, and a neutrophil count < 3 × 109/L. TTV VL reflects both immunosuppressive exposure and host-related determinants. Recognizing both is essential for interpreting TTV dynamics and defining individualized immunosuppression thresholds.

candidates.title: Differentiation arrest of transitional alveolar epithelial cells drives pulmonary fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Alveolar epithelial type 2 cells (AEC2) serve as facultative stem cells of the lung, differentiating into type 1 cells (AEC1) to restore barrier integrity after injury. Recent single-cell studies have identified a transient Krt8+ transitional state as an essential intermediate in this process. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), however, this program is disrupted, leading to the persistence of cells trapped in a differentiation block. These maladaptive cells act not only as markers of failed regeneration but also as active profibrotic signaling hubs that amplify disease progression. Here, we synthesize current evidence on the molecular mechanisms underlying this arrest, including dysregulated signaling pathways (Wnt, YAP/TAZ, Notch), metabolic reprogramming, and epigenetic constraints. We further discuss how these cells remodel the microenvironment and interact with stromal compartments to sustain a self-reinforcing profibrotic niche. Targeting this upstream epithelial arrest may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for pulmonary fibrosis.

candidates.title: Clinical and prognostic implications of honeycombing in patients diagnosed with NSIP.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical, radiological and treatment characteristics of patients diagnosed with nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) between 2012 and 2017. In addition, we investigated the association of these findings with survival outcomes in the context of contemporary treatment strategies.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective cohort study included 79 patients with NSIP. Demographic data, comorbidities, modified Medical Research Council dyspnoea scores, high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) findings, pulmonary function test results, administered immunosuppressive agents and clinical course data were recorded.
RESULTS: The mean age of the cohort was 66.3 ± 10.3 (range: 41-87) years, and 45.6% and 54.4% of them were female and male, respectively. At least one comorbidity was present in 78.5% of patients, cardiovascular disease being the most frequent. Ground-glass opacity was the most common thoracic HRCT finding (91.1%). A honeycombing pattern was present in 40.5% of patients and was associated with mortality (log-rank p = 0.009; univariable Cox HR 3.49, 95% CI 1.29-9.46). Immunosuppressive therapy was administered to 74.6% of patients. There was no significant difference in the survival of the treated and untreated groups (log-rank p = 0.320). Overall survival was calculated as 66.1 months (95% CI: 58.7-73.5).
CONCLUSION: The results suggest that a honeycombing pattern may be associated with a worse prognosis in NSIP. The width of the confidence interval and the modest number of events mean this should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating observation requiring prospective confirmation. No significant survival difference was observed between treated and untreated patients, although the small number of events in the untreated group limits the interpretation of this comparison. These findings support the individualisation of treatment decisions in NSIP based on clinical and radiological prognostic features.

candidates.title: LitGene: an interpretable transformer model integrating text and ontology for gene representation learning.
candidates.abstract: Representation learning in genomics often relies on sequence, expression, and network data, thereby overlooking a wealth of insights in the scientific literature. Here, we present LitGene, an interpretable transformer-based model that refines gene representations by integrating unstructured textual information with Gene Ontology annotations through contrastive learning. In evaluations across eight benchmark tasks for protein properties, LitGene achieves competitive accuracy and exhibits zero-shot prediction of GO terms, KEGG pathways, and gene-disease associations. LitGene identified ANGPTL6 as a potential candidate gene for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), supported by its differential expression in independent IPF samples, illustrating LitGene's utility for hypothesis generation. A SHAP-based interpretability tool highlights text features influencing predictions, while an automated literature-grounding framework provides corroborating support where available. Our results suggest that integrating textual and genetic information may help reduce biases associated with under-studied genes. The model is released as open-source code, along with a publicly accessible web interface at https://litgene.cs.unm.edu/ , which allows users to submit gene names, disease names, drug names, or custom text (e.g., publication abstracts) to obtain evidence-based predictions of related biomedical entities.

candidates.title: Association of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis with TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C: a retrospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accumulating evidence suggests a significant link between dyslipidaemia-characterized by an imbalance in circulating lipids and lipoproteins-and the pathogenesis and progression of various chronic respiratory conditions. However, their mechanistic role in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) pathogenesis has yet to be fully elucidated. This study aimed to explore the associations of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) with TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C in Chinese adults.
METHODS: This study included 129 patients in the stable phase of IPF, 85 patients with acute exacerbation (AE-IPF), and 130 non-IPF controls. The evaluation included routine blood tests (encompassing the lipid profile) and pulmonary function assessments. Additionally, a follow-up with a median duration of 5.84 months was conducted in 183 IPF patients.
RESULTS: Compared with values observed in stable cases or control subjects, the levels of both TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C were markedly elevated in subjects with AE-IPF. Following adjustment for potential confounders, logistic regression models revealed that both TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C were independent factors positively correlated with the presence of AE-IPF. In assessing the predictive power for AE-IPF, the area under the ROC curve corresponding to TG/HDL-C exceeded that of TC/HDL-C and all other conventional lipid levels. During a median follow-up of 5.84 months, 81 IPF patients passed away. Nonsurvivors had higher baseline TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C levels than survivors did. Multivariate Cox regression analysis adjusted for age, sex, and oxygenation index revealed that the adjusted hazard ratios for overall survival with each 1-SD increase in TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C were 1.809 (95% CI: 1.497-2.184, P < 0.001) and 1.486 (95% CI: 1.183-1.867, P = 0.001), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Elevated TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C ratios are independently associated with acute exacerbation and poor short-term survival in IPF patients. The TG/HDL-C ratio, in particular, represents

candidates.title: Nucleic Acid-Driven Immunopathology in Sjögren's Disease.
candidates.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by epithelial dysfunction and pathological lymphocyte homing. Clinically, it manifests with xerostomia, xerophthalmia, and fatigue and may involve systemic features such as arthralgia, cryoglobulinemia, interstitial lung disease, and peripheral neuropathy. Emerging evidence highlights the pivotal role of nucleic acids and their associated receptors in the pathogenesis of SjD. Aberrant nucleic acids can activate type I interferon (IFN-I), the inflammasome, and proinflammatory signaling pathways. This cascade promotes the activation of immune cells and the release of cytokines, thereby exacerbating chronic inflammation. This review article elucidates the mechanisms of nucleic acid-mediated immunopathology in SjD and discusses potential therapeutic strategies.

candidates.title: From local control to systemic management: radiotherapy and sequential methotrexate therapy in an adult BRAF-negative hypothalamic-pituitary Langerhans cell histiocytosis - a case report with 15-month follow-up.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare clonal neoplastic disorder characterized by the proliferation of CD1a+/Langerin+ dendritic cells. Hypothalamic-pituitary region (HPR) involvement in adults-particularly when followed by multisystem progression after local therapy-remains poorly characterized. We report a 35-year-old female with HPR-LCH who achieved durable local metabolic remission after radiotherapy but later developed systemic progression, which was successfully managed with systemic chemotherapy.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 35-year-old woman presented with progressive memory decline, polydipsia, polyuria, 15-kg weight gain over six months, and one year of amenorrhea. Endocrine evaluation revealed central diabetes insipidus (CDI) and hyperprolactinemia (prolactin 94.19 ng/mL). Pituitary MRI demonstrated a 2.0 × 1.4 cm enhancing hypothalamic mass with pituitary stalk thickening. A pterional craniotomy was performed for histopathological sampling, and immunohistochemistry confirmed LCH (CD1a+/Langerin+/S100+); BRAF V600E mutation was negative by quantitative PCR. The patient received involved-field intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT, 22 Gy/11 fractions) targeting the HPR lesion. At 15-month follow-up, 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-computed tomography (18 F-FDG PET-CT) demonstrated complete metabolic remission of the hypothalamic lesion, with resolution of memory and mood symptoms. However, new progressive skull bone destruction, skin ulcers, and pulmonary nodules emerged. She was subsequently treated with a full initial course of high-dose methotrexate (MTX 9 g IV weekly for 3 weeks, 12 g weekly for 2 weeks, and 16 g weekly for 2 weeks) at a Peking Union Medical College Hospital-affiliated institution, achieving significant improvement in skin ulcers, bone pain, and galactorrhea. A second consolidation course is scheduled.
CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that involved-field IMRT can achieve durable local control of HPR-L

candidates.title: Dual-database pharmacovigilance analysis based on FAERS and JADER combined with network pharmacology to explore fulvestrant-associated respiratory toxicity.
candidates.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fulvestrant serves as cornerstone endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive (HR-positive) advanced breast cancer. Recent reports indicate safety concerns regarding respiratory toxicity. This study systematically characterized fulvestrant-related respiratory adverse events (adverse events, AEs) using two independent spontaneous reporting databases (FAERS and JADER) for cross-verification and investigated underlying mechanisms.
METHODS: Disproportionality analysis utilized two post-marketing surveillance databases, the United States Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER), applying reporting odds ratio (ROR) and Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN) methods for respiratory adverse event signal detection. Fulvestrant targets were predicted using SwissTargetPrediction, TargetNet, and Therapeutic Target Database (TTD). Lung disease-related genes were identified from GeneCards and Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM). Overlapping targets underwent Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed with STRING and Cytoscape, core genes identified by maximum clique centrality (MCC) algorithm. CB-Dock2 platform performed molecular docking between fulvestrant and key targets.
RESULTS: A total of 6988 fulvestrant-related reports were included from FAERS with 896 respiratory toxicity cases, while 1582 fulvestrant-associated adverse event reports were retrieved from JADER, covering 154 respiratory toxicity cases. Twenty-two respiratory adverse event signals were detected in FAERS, among which nine consistent positive signals were replicated in JADER, including pleural effusion (ROR = 5.38), interstitial lung disease (ROR = 3.94), and dyspnea (ROR = 1.50). candidates.title: Myokines as Support Mechanisms for Lung Maintenance and Repair: Implications for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
candidates.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
candidates.abstract: Skeletal muscle is increasingly recognized as an active endocrine organ capable of exerting protective effects on distal tissue homeostasis through the secretion of bioactive factors, including myokines. While inter-tissue communication of skeletal muscle has been described for various tissues, its role in lung biology has remained largely unexplored, though evidence for this interaction is now emerging. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a chronic condition characterized by both pulmonary dysfunction and systemic manifestations such as skeletal muscle wasting, provides a strong rationale to explore the role of the muscle secretome in lung health and pathology. In this review, we explore the concept of skeletal muscle-lung crosstalk with a focus on myokines as key mediators. Through literature search, we selected a subset of myokines for which published studies have specifically investigated their effects on lung disease. We highlight four myokines-irisin, apelin, MG53, and Metrnl-that have demonstrated protective effects on lung tissue across a range of experimental models. These factors exert anti-inflammatory, antioxidative, antifibrotic, and cytoprotective effects by modulating key signaling pathways. Through these mechanisms, myokines contribute to the preservation of lung tissue integrity, regulation of inflammation in the lungs, maintenance of lung mitochondrial function, and support of lung tissue repair processes. Collectively, these findings support a paradigm in which skeletal muscle actively contributes to lung health. Elucidating this crosstalk may reveal novel strategies to enhance pulmonary resilience and repair, particularly through interventions that deploy the muscle secretome.

candidates.title: PCSK6 in Pathophysiology and Its Potential Involvement in Pulmonary Fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 6 (PCSK6) is a proteolytic enzyme that may act on a broad spectrum of substrates, including growth factors, extracellular proteases, adhesion molecules, protease activated receptor 1, the prorenin receptor, and Corin. As a consequence of its broad-spectrum substrate activity, PCSK6 is implicated in a wide range of pathophysiological processes such as cardiovascular disease, neurological disorders, arthritis and cancer. Of special interest, PCSK6 has recently been shown to be highly expressed in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and PCSK6 has been associated with reduced survival of IPF patients, linking PCSK6 to pulmonary fibrosis for the first time. Of note however, PCSK6 levels in plasma were not associated with respiratory outcomes in IPF patients and higher PCSK6 levels were even associated with a lower hazard of 10% FVC decline in non-IPF ILD patients. In this review, we summarize the molecular biology of PCSK6, including its structural features and its major (potential) substrates, and outline its pathophysiological roles across various diseases. Furthermore, we propose and discuss the potential involvement of PCSK6 in pulmonary fibrosis to guide future research.

candidates.title: Pulmonary Fibroblast Heterogeneity and Functional Remodeling in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: State Persistence and Reversibility.
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis is a common pathological endpoint of several interstitial lung diseases. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), in particular, has an unknown cause, produces progressive scarring of the lung parenchyma, and carries a poor prognosis. Single-cell and spatial omics studies have shown that lung fibroblasts comprise multiple populations with distinct anatomical locations and functional states. However, how these states are established, interconverted, and maintained in the injured microenvironment remains incompletely understood and has not been directly validated. This review uses IPF as the primary clinical context and draws complementary mechanistic evidence from other fibrotic lung diseases and animal models. It examines fibroblast origins and state heterogeneity; signaling networks involving transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β), Wnt, and Yes-associated protein (YAP); interactions among epithelial cells, immune cells, and fibroblasts; and epigenetic and metabolic remodeling. On this basis, we propose a two-layer stability model of epigenetic maintenance and signaling feedback as a working framework for understanding the persistence of profibrotic states. We also discuss how treatment might move from nonselective inhibition toward restricting pathological states, eliminating pathogenic subpopulations, and preserving reparative function. The causal sequence proposed by this model, the necessity of its components, and the thresholds for state reversal remain unresolved and require testing through lineage tracing, assessment of phenotypic stability after stimulus withdrawal, and sequential combination interventions.

candidates.title: IL-6-Mediated Macrophage-Fibroblast Communication in Pathological Lung Remodeling.
candidates.abstract: Fibrosis is a pathological form of tissue remodeling driven by excessive deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM). Unlike physiological tissue repair, fibrosis arises from persistent myofibroblast activation and unresolved inflammation. Chronic inflammation can both initiate fibrotic remodeling and be sustained by the resulting tissue alterations, supporting the view of fibrosis as an immune-mediated process. Fibrogenesis is fundamentally shaped by interactions between macrophages and fibroblasts. Polarized macrophages can modulate fibroblast activity and promote their differentiation into myofibroblasts. IL-6 is an important mediator of macrophage-fibroblast communication and has been implicated in fibrotic diseases affecting multiple organs. Notably, the effects of IL-6 are highly context-dependent. During acute injury, IL-6 can promote tissue repair by stimulating epithelial proliferation and angiogenesis, whereas persistent IL-6 signaling in chronic inflammation can become a major driver of fibrosis. IL-6 is also a prominent component of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), providing a mechanistic link between fibrosis, cellular senescence, and inflammaging. In this review, we provide an integrated overview of the role of IL-6 in macrophage-fibroblast interactions during pulmonary fibrogenesis, with particular emphasis on its context-dependent functions at the interface between tissue repair and pathological tissue remodeling. We also discuss current therapeutic strategies aimed at targeting IL-6 signaling.

candidates.title: Angiotensin II-Induced Cardiac Fibrosis: Genomic and Molecular Drivers, Emerging Biomarkers and Therapeutic Perspectives.
candidates.abstract: Chronically elevated angiotensin II (Ang II) drives adverse cardiac remodelling, converting a reparative response into progressive interstitial and perivascular fibrosis that stiffens the ventricle and precedes overt heart failure. Acting through the angiotensin II type 1 receptor, Ang II generates reactive oxygen species, recruits and polarises immune cells and activates resident fibroblasts, converging on transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-dependent and mechanotransductive programmes that drive myofibroblast differentiation and excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. The magnitude of this response varies between patients: germline variation in renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) genes, loci for heart failure and imaging-defined fibrosis, epigenomic reprogramming of the fibroblast, non-coding RNA networks and metabolic rewiring of collagen-producing cells all modulate the transition from compensated hypertrophy to fibrotic failure. This review integrates these genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic and metabolomic layers with the signalling architecture of Ang II-induced fibrosis, and reviews the circulating biomarkers-collagen turnover peptides, matricellular and immune mediators, non-coding RNAs and cell-free DNA methylation signatures-that could detect fibrotic activity before remodelling becomes irreversible. We then consider why fibrosis regression under RAAS blockade appears heterogeneous, which emerging targets are mechanistically credible, and how genotype-biomarker-imaging phenotyping could enrich antifibrotic trials. Priorities for ancestrally diverse cohorts and standardised biomarker methodology are identified.

candidates.title: Emerging Therapies in Pulmonary Fibrosis: A Common Pathway for the Action of Diverse Pharmacologic Agents.
candidates.abstract: Fibrotic lung diseases are a heterogeneous set of disorders characterized by progressive infiltration of the pulmonary interstitium by inflammatory cells and fibroblasts, leading to destruction of normal pulmonary tissue and increased extracellular matrix deposition. Fibrotic lung disease can be initiated by numerous triggers-genetic, immunologic, pharmacologic, environmental, infectious-that share many downstream effectors, leading to injury patterns with substantial pathologic and clinical overlap. Recent preclinical studies have expanded our knowledge of the mechanisms of lung inflammation and implicated the key role of specific cytokines in the pathogenesis of lung inflammation. They reinforce the concept that inflammation is a key precursor of lung fibrosis. They have also identified specific intracellular signaling pathways that are modulated, at least in part, by cytokine signaling and that have been shown to be emerging targets for drugs that target inflammation in the lung. Recent advances in therapeutics have yielded two new drugs active in pulmonary fibrosis, the PDE4-selective inhibitor nerandomilast and the prostacyclin analog treprostinil. There is now compelling evidence that, despite their structural differences, these two drugs act through a common mechanism, the cAMP signaling pathway. The new clinical trial results have provided critical confirmation that these targets are indeed key regulators of lung fibrosis and inflammation and, in turn, have provided well-validated clinical evidence that these agents have therapeutic value in patients.

candidates.title: Vitamin K3 (Menadione) Targets TBK1 to Enhance the Efficacy of Pirfenidone in a Mouse Model of Bleomycin-Induced Pulmonary Fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and irreversible interstitial lung disease. Current antifibrotic drugs, exemplified by pirfenidone (PFD), only slow disease progression with limited efficacy and adverse effects, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic strategies. By integrating single-cell transcriptomics with the Drug2Cell algorithm, we performed drug prioritization at single-cell resolution and identified menadione (vitamin K3, VK3), a synthetic naphthoquinone and the minimal core of naturally occurring vitamin K, as a candidate preferentially active in alveolar epithelial cells. In bleomycin (BLM)-stimulated A549 cells and a mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis, therapeutic co-administration of low-dose VK3 and PFD reduced vimentin expression by 44.8% and collagen deposition by 50.3%, and decreased fibroblast abundance by 36.7%, thereby attenuating histopathological damage and restoring BLM-disrupted alveolar epithelial homeostasis. Experiments with VK3 alone further demonstrated that its antifibrotic activity is independent of conversion to vitamin K2. Mechanistically, thermal proteome profiling identified TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1) as the principal candidate target; molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations predicted a stable binding mode, independently confirmed by biolayer interferometry and differential scanning fluorimetry, demonstrating direct binding of VK3 to TBK1 with nanomolar affinity. TBK1 knockdown suppressed BLM-induced fibrotic responses, establishing TBK1 as a positive regulator of pulmonary fibrosis. In vitro signaling analysis revealed that VK3 plus PFD inhibits phosphorylation of TBK1 and STAT3, whereas PFD alone reduces phosphorylation of JAK1 and STAT3, suggesting that both agents converge on STAT3 through distinct upstream nodes. Although VK3 exhibits dose-dependent cytotoxicity precluding direct clinical use as monotherapy, its validated high-affinity target TBK1 and privileged naphthoquinone scaffold lay

candidates.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Translation/RBP-Related Fibroblast Signature for Drug Repurposing in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by persistent fibroblast activation and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. However, transcriptional heterogeneity associated with translation- and RNA-binding protein (RBP)-related processes within IPF fibroblasts remains incompletely characterized. Here, we analyzed two independent human IPF single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts to identify fibroblast states that differed in Translation/RBP-related transcriptional programs while sharing high fibrotic output. Donor-paired pseudobulk analysis in GSE136831 identified a transcriptional signature distinguishing these states, and genes showing consistent directional changes in the independent GSE135893 cohort were retained to derive a cross-cohort signature. Reverse-connectivity analysis across CLUE, L1000CDS2, and iLINCS was then used to prioritize compounds predicted to transcriptionally oppose this signature. Candidate compounds were subsequently evaluated in transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-stimulated human fetal lung fibroblasts (HFL-1), with cell viability, α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), and collagen I used for initial phenotypic assessment. PP-1, PK-11195, dabrafenib, GSK-1059615, and dasatinib reduced both profibrotic markers within the tested concentration ranges, identifying them as candidates for further investigation. Together, these findings define a cross-cohort Translation/RBP-related fibroblast signature in IPF and support its use as a transcriptome-guided strategy for prioritizing compounds with antifibrotic phenotypic activity.

candidates.title: Comparison of whole-lung, physical-dose, and BED3-guided subregional multi-omics for predicting 3-month symptomatic radiation pneumonitis after lung cancer radiotherapy: a dual-center study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Region definition may influence radiation pneumonitis (RP) prediction, particularly when treatment schedules differ. We compared whole-lung, physical-dose subregional, and voxelwise biologically effective dose with α/β = 3 Gy (BED3)-guided strategies. The target outcome was grade ≥ 2 symptomatic RP within 3 months after lung cancer radiotherapy.
METHODS: This retrospective dual-center study included 246 patients between March 2023 and December 2025: 171 in a hospital-defined development cohort and 75 in the center-2 assessment cohort. The outcome was any grade ≥ 2 symptomatic RP recorded within 3 months after radiotherapy. Seven clinical, DVH, radiomic, dosiomic, and combined model specifications were evaluated within each region-design strategy. Development used repeated stratified 5 × 5 nested cross-validation and optimism correction based on 1000 bootstrap samples. All candidate models used the same outer and corresponding inner partitions and bootstrap resamples. Center 2 was excluded from model development and optimism correction and was used for center-specific out-of-sample performance assessment.
RESULTS: Forty-three patients developed grade ≥ 2 symptomatic RP (27/171 in development; 16/75 in center 2). Under shared resampling, center-2 AUCs for the complete whole-lung, physical-dose, and BED3 models were 0.676, 0.669, and 0.684, respectively. The differences were small, with overlapping confidence intervals. Across five intervals per representation, the highest point estimates were observed for physical dose 10-20 Gy (AUC 0.745) and BED3 ≥ 70 Gy3 (AUC 0.720). These interval rankings are exploratory and subject to selection optimism. Center-2 Brier scores for the complete models ranged from 0.184 to 0.260, compared with 0.168 for a constant-probability reference based on the center-2 event rate; calibration was inadequate for clinical use.
CONCLUSIONS: The paired analysis did not identify a clearly superior region design. Complete-model center-2

candidates.title: The risk and economic burden of interstitial lung disease in patients with non-small cell lung cancer treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors and targeted therapies.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite improved survival with targeted therapies and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), evidence regarding the risk and economic burden of drug-induced interstitial lung disease (DI-ILD)-a potentially fatal adverse event-remains limited. We evaluated drug- and generation-specific risks of DI-ILD and its associated economic burden.
METHODS: Using the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service (HIRA) claims database (January 1, 2012-May 31, 2023), we identified patients treated with ICIs, epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitors (EGFRis), or anaplastic lymphoma kinase inhibitors (ALKis). Incidence rates (IRs) and hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for ILD were estimated using stabilized generalized propensity scores weighting and Cox proportional hazards models. After 1:4 propensity score matching, healthcare costs and resource utilization during ILD treatment period were compared between patients with and without ILD.
RESULTS: Among 12,744 ICI users, 44,689 EGFR and 5,655 ALK prescription records, 111, 178, and 33 cases of ILD were identified, respectively. Compared with nivolumab, pembrolizumab (HR, 2.14; 95% CI, 1.12-4.11) and atezolizumab (HR, 1.80; 95% CI, 0.96-3.38) showed higher ILD risk. First- (HR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.44-1.00) and third-generation EGFRis (HR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.22-0.89) had significantly lower risks than second-generation EGFRis. Compared with third-generation ALKis, first-generation (HR, 0.15; 95% CI, 0.03-0.70) and second-generation ALKis (HR, 0.20; 95% CI, 0.04-0.89) showed significantly lower risks of ILD. ILD was associated with higher healthcare costs and utilization, including hospitalization costs (2.11-5.24 times), infection and respiratory medication costs (2.72-13.88 times), hospitalization admissions (1.69-3.84 times), length of stay (1.66-2.57 times), and emergency room visits (1.21-5.58 times).
