candidates.title: Early recognition of a macrophage activation-associated hyperinflammatory state in anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5) antibody-positive dermatomyositis is frequently complicated by rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD) and is associated with poor prognosis. In some cases, excessive systemic inflammation related to macrophage activation may occur and contribute to disease severity.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 59-year-old Japanese woman with anti-MDA5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis complicated by RP-ILD. She initially presented with skin rash and dyspnea, followed by declining vital capacity and progressive proximal muscle weakness. Laboratory evaluation revealed cytopenia and hyperferritinemia. Bone marrow examination performed because of leukopenia demonstrated hemophagocytosis by activated macrophages. Although the diagnostic criteria for macrophage activation syndrome were not fully met, these findings suggested a macrophage activation-associated hyperinflammatory state. In view of the progressive interstitial lung disease and suspected hyperinflammation, therapeutic intensification was undertaken by adding plasma exchange and intravenous cyclophosphamide to corticosteroids and tacrolimus. Following treatment escalation, cytopenia, pulmonary function, and muscle strength gradually improved.
CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the importance of recognizing macrophage activation-associated hyperinflammation in anti-MDA5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis. Early recognition and prompt therapeutic intensification may contribute to improved clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: Five trials to watch.
candidates.abstract: For a decade, treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) relied on two antifibrotic drugs that slow down lung function decline. Positive phase 3 trials for nerandomilast and inhaled treprostinil are now changing this landscape. Additionally, new therapies are in mid- and late-stage clinical development, each targeting fibrosis in a different way. In this Trial Watch, we focus on five of these emerging approaches.

candidates.title: The role of 18F-FDG PET-CT in predicting progressive pulmonary fibrosis in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy associated interstitial lung disease.
candidates.abstract:
AIM: This study aims to investigate the role of 18F-FDG PET-CT in the development of progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) in patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD) and to develop a predictive nomogram model.
METHODS: This study retrospectively included patients diagnosed with IIM-ILD who underwent 18F-FDG PET-CT at Ruijin Hospital between 2018 and 2024. The baseline characteristics, IIM types, myositis antibodies, laboratory tests, pulmonary function, ILD subtypes, 18F-FDG PET-CT findings, and treatment were collected. Enrolled patients were divided into PPF and non-PPF groups according to diagnostic criteria. Clinical features were compared between the two groups, and logistic regression analysis was performed to identify risk factors for PPF. All identified risk factors were combined to construct the predictive nomogram. Receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration plot, and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate the accuracy and efficiency of this predictive model. Additionally, we drew the survival curve of PPF and non-PPF, and compared the maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) between short-term death and long-term survival.
RESULTS: A total of 71 eligible IIM-ILD patients were included, of whom 29 developed PPF within one year of follow-up. Multivariate analysis revealed that bilateral lung SUVmax and FVC%pred were associated with the occurrence of PPF. The calibration plot demonstrated excellent agreement between the predicted and actual observed probability of PPF (Hosmer-Lemeshow test: P = 0.143). The predictive nomogram achieved an area under the curve of 0.887 (95% CI: 0.805-0.969). The SUVmax in the lungs was significantly higher in the PPF group than in the non-PPF group (P < 0.001). Moreover, lung SUVmax was significantly higher in patients who died within one year than in those who survived for more than five years (P = 0.014). In addition, patients with PPF had a significantly

candidates.title: Integrated Multi-Omics Identifies SLIT2 as a Regulator of Senescence-Associated Fibroblast Remodeling in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive interstitial lung disease that is strongly associated with aging. How aging contributes to fibroblast state remodeling and intercellular signaling dysregulation in IPF remains poorly defined. We integrated bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and DNA methylation data from human IPF lungs to characterize fibroblast heterogeneity, trajectory dynamics, intercellular communication, and epigenetic aging. SLIT2 downregulation and senescence-associated changes were then examined in a bleomycin (BLM)-induced mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis. The effects of SLIT2 on fibroblast senescence and paracrine pro-fibrotic activity were assessed in BLM-treated MRC-5 fibroblasts using recombinant SLIT2 supplementation and siRNA-mediated knockdown. In an independent DNA methylation cohort, epigenetic aging clocks and mediation analyses in both directions were used to examine statistical relationships among epigenetic age acceleration, SLIT2 expression, and IPF risk. These analyses identified five fibroblast subtypes, with TCF21⁺ fibroblasts predominating in normal lung and CTHRC1⁺ fibroblasts markedly enriched in IPF. Trajectory analyses inferred a potential fibroblast state trajectory from homeostatic TCF21⁺ toward pathological CTHRC1⁺ fibroblast states, along which a senescent TCF21⁺ subpopulation showed preferential trajectory bias toward the CTHRC1⁺ endpoint. SLIT2 was preferentially expressed in TCF21⁺ fibroblasts, which represented an important predicted sender population within the SLIT-ROBO communication network. In a BLM-induced mouse model, fibrotic remodeling was accompanied by increased senescent cell burden and SLIT2 downregulation, consistent with the observations in human IPF. In vitro, rhSLIT2 attenuated BLM-induced senescence and pro-fibrotic paracrine activation, whereas SLIT2 knockdown exacerbated both. SLIT2 manipulation also altered NF-κB signaling and SASP-associated respon

candidates.title: Imaging in Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma).
candidates.journal: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) or scleroderma is a multisystem autoimmune disorder characterized by a variable pattern of skin thickening and involvement of visceral organs. The pathophysiology is similar across all organs, which is chronic low-grade inflammation, with vasculopathy and eventual fibrosis. Diagnosis is primarily clinical, particularly in patients with established disease comprising characteristic skin and visceral manifestations, with a supportive role of laboratory and imaging findings. The presence of radiologic signs such as hidebound bowel or a combination of patulous lower esophageal sphincter, pulmonary fibrosis, skin thickening, and Raynaud phenomenon is relatively specific for SSc. Nevertheless, imaging in SSc is primarily used to determine the pattern, severity, and complications of visceral organ involvement, rather than for diagnosis of SSc. Radiologic evaluation in SSc employs a wide gamut of investigations, depending on the organ of interest. For example, US is used for the skin and superficial tissues; fluoroscopy, CT, or MR enterography for the gastrointestinal tract; endoanal US or MRI for the internal anal sphincter; high-resolution CT for the lungs; echocardiography and cardiac MRI for SSc-related pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and cardiac disease; and radiography, CT, or MRI for musculoskeletal involvement. Early diagnosis of treatable features, such as PAH and gastroesophageal reflux, can help reduce the morbidity and mortality associated with SSc. Imaging is additionally useful to prognosticate and monitor the disease. The authors focus on the multisystem, multimodality imaging manifestations of SSc with relevant differential diagnoses to bridge the gaps in knowledge about SSc. ©RSNA, 2026.

candidates.title: Enhanced Pulmonary Fibrosis Treatment by Self-Assembling Peptide Nanofibers via Improved Pulmonary Delivery and Retention.
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a life-threatening interstitial lung disease, which progressively impairs pulmonary function, with limited therapeutic options available. In this study, we designed CQ7, a self-assembling peptide that integrates a therapeutic peptide with a self-assembly motif. CQ7 monomers spontaneously form supramolecular nanofibers under physiological conditions, both extracellularly and intracellularly. This nanofiber structure promotes efficient lung retention and targeted pulmonary delivery, leading to enhanced anti-fibrotic efficacy. We evaluated the anti-fibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects of CQ7 in a murine PF model via both intraperitoneal and inhalation administrations. Transcriptomic sequencing and experimental validation further revealed that CQ7 may act through the regulation of mitochondrial function, reducing cellular oxidative stress and thereby regulating the apoptosis process. Collectively, this work demonstrates a novel peptide-based strategy with significant potential for improving PF outcomes and clinical translation.

candidates.title: Design, Synthesis, and Antifibrotic Evaluation of Silicon-Incorporated Alkyl Hydrazide Analogs of Tubastatin A: HDAC3 Selective Inhibitor for Ameliorating Liver Fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Liver fibrosis remains a significant therapeutic challenge, with limited effective treatments and few clinically viable HDAC inhibitors despite their antifibrotic potential. Here, we report the design of silicon-incorporated alkyl hydrazide analogs of tubastatin-A to develop selective HDAC3 inhibitors via cap and zinc-binding motif optimization. These compounds were evaluated for HDAC-selectivity and antifibrotic activity in TGF-β-induced HSC-LX2 and HHSEC models, where 6b exhibited potent and selective HDAC3 inhibition (IC50-22 nM) with respect to HDAC5, HDAC6, HDAC8 along with robust antifibrotic activity, supported by molecular docking. ADMET studies indicated a favourable pharmacokinetic profile, permeability, microsomal stability, and a promising safety profile. Further validation in a CCl4-induced hepatic-fibrosis model, 6b demonstrated significant in-vivo efficacy by reducing AST/ALT levels, fibrotic marker expression and improving histopathology, outperforming tubastatin-A and nintedanib. Mechanistically, 6b significantly inhibited TGF-β/Smad signaling, likely through modulation of histone-acetylation patterns. Collectively, these findings identify 6b as a promising lead candidate for hepatic fibrosis.

candidates.title: Discovery of YKS-34, a Highly Selective PDE4B Inhibitor for the Treatment of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains a progressive and fatal lung disease with a substantial unmet need for safe and effective therapies. Highly selective inhibition of phosphodiesterase 4B (PDE4B) represents a promising therapeutic strategy for IPF while avoiding nausea and vomiting associated with PDE4D inhibition. However, achieving pronounced subtype selectivity remains particularly challenging; notably, the only approved PDE4B-preferential inhibitor, nerandomilast, exhibits only approximately 9-fold selectivity for PDE4B over PDE4D. Herein, we report the identification of YKS-34, a potent PDE4B inhibitor (IC50 = 1.71 nM) exhibiting >1000-fold selectivity over PDE4A, PDE4C, and PDE4D. YKS-34 effectively suppressed TGF-β-induced fibroblast activation and LPS-induced TNF-α release in vitro. In vivo, YKS-34 showed favorable pharmacokinetic properties, lung tissue accumulation, and reduced emetic potential at tested conditions while dose-dependently improving pulmonary dysfunction and fibrotic remodeling in a bleomycin-induced IPF mouse model. Consequently, YKS-34 emerges as a highly promising, next-generation candidate for the treatment of IPF.

candidates.title: Lung-Tailored Pyrrolo-pyrimidine DDR Inhibitors Designed for Optimized Local Delivery.
candidates.abstract: Preclinical studies highlighted the key role of Discoidin Domain Receptors (DDRs) in fibrotic processes, making them promising targets for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) treatment. In this work, we describe the design of a novel class of DDR inhibitors and their subsequent optimization toward inhaled delivery. Following a structure-based approach, we identified two chemical series based on 5:6 heterocyclic cores showing nanomolar affinity for DDR1 and DDR2 and a promising kinome selectivity profile. An inhaled-by-design medchem strategy was then applied to optimize potency, phys-chem, and in vitro ADME properties, tailored to achieve lung-restricted compounds. This effort resulted in the discovery of compound 25, a novel and highly potent DDR inhibitor that combined antifibrotic activity in a TGFβ-induced in vitro fibrosis model with an outstanding pharmacokinetic profile and the desired lung-targeted behavior following inhaled administration.

candidates.title: Successful treatment of anti-glomerular basement membrane antibody disease combined with membranous nephropathy using rituximab: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Anti‑glomerular basement membrane (anti‑GBM) disease is a rare autoimmune disorder that classically manifests as rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage. The coexistence of anti-GBM disease and membranous nephropathy (MN) was first reported in 1976. Although such cases are rare, many reported patients develop progressive kidney injury and poor renal outcomes. We report a young man with sequential-onset dual glomerulopathy. He initially presented with MN alone and achieved partial remission following glucocorticoid and cyclosporine therapy. Three years later, he developed rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, and kidney biopsy confirmed anti-GBM disease superimposed on pre-existing MN. This sequential pattern differs from the simultaneous onset of both lesions reported in many previous cases. To minimize gonadal toxicity, he received individualized therapy consisting of glucocorticoids, dose-adjusted cyclophosphamide, rituximab, and plasma exchange. He ultimately recovered normal kidney function and had a favorable renal outcome. This case expands the clinical spectrum of overlapping anti-GBM disease and MN and suggests that patients with MN in remission require long-term serial monitoring for early detection of superimposed autoimmune kidney injury. Individualized immunosuppressive strategies tailored to each patient's clinical characteristics are essential to optimize kidney outcomes in such complex glomerular diseases.

candidates.title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome after risperidone therapy in a critically ill patient with mixed connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease:A case report.
candidates.journal: The journal of medical investigation : JMI
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is a rare but life-threatening adverse reaction to dopamine-blocking agents. Although atypical antipsychotics are generally considered to carry a lower risk than typical agents, NMS may occur even at therapeutic doses, particularly in critically ill patients. Critically ill individuals with systemic inflammatory diseases may present with diagnostic challenges because the clinical features of NMS overlap with those of infection or disease exacerbation.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 47-year-old woman with mixed connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (MCTD-ILD) developed acute respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation and high-dose corticosteroid therapy. During sedation weaning, risperidone was initiated at 3 mg/day to manage agitation. Within 48 hours, she developed a high-grade fever, tachypnea, and a marked creatine kinase elevation without muscle rigidity, fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for NMS. Discontinuation of risperidone and a single administration of dantrolene led to a clinical improvement. However, recurrent NMS occurred after initial stabilization, necessitating reintubation and the reinstitution of dantrolene. The patient ultimately recovered and was discharged without recurrence.
CONCLUSION: NMS can occur and recur after therapeutic-dose atypical antipsychotic use in critically ill patients with systemic inflammatory conditions. Early recognition and close biochemical monitoring are essential when prescribing dopamine antagonists in the ICU setting. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 558-560, August, 2026.

candidates.title: Demystifying Autoimmune/Autoinflammatory Lung Disease.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Lung diseases in systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARD) and autoinflammatory diseases may be the initial manifestation of underlying immune dysregulation and are significant contributors of morbidity and mortality in these conditions. This review describes the spectrum of lung diseases across SARD and autoinflammatory diagnoses, summarizing the key distinguishing features within these disorders.
RECENT FINDINGS: SARDs and autoinflammatory diseases may involve the airways, lung parenchyma, pleura, and pulmonary vasculature. Bronchiolar disorders such as bronchiectasis and bronchiolitis may complicate many different SARDs leading to chronic mucus production, pulmonary infection, and recurrent exacerbations. Diffuse parenchymal involvement most commonly presents as interstitial lung disease (ILD) which can involve SARDs such as rheumatoid arthritis, Sjogren's syndrome, and mixed connective tissue disease as well as inborn errors of immunity including monogenic autoinflammatory disorders and interferonopathies. Pleural involvement may manifest as serositis or pleural effusions and chronic involvement may lead to complications such as pleural thickening and lung entrapment. Pulmonary hypertension may develop due to the underlying disorder, such as in systemic sclerosis, but may also develop as a complication of advanced lung disease. Early recognition and treatment of pulmonary involvement in SARD and autoinflammatory diseases is key and emerging therapies beyond anti-inflammatory therapy may be required in the treatment of these conditions. candidates.title: Effects of different durations of exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation intervention in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a chronic and fatal lung disease causing progressive scarring, severely impairs respiratory function and quality of life. Although pulmonary rehabilitation is an important supportive intervention, the effects of different intervention durations remain uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the effects of exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation at approximately 3 months/12 weeks, 6 months/26 weeks, and 9 to 12 months/52 weeks in patients with IPF.
METHODS: Systematic literature searches were conducted in the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, Chinese Science and Technology Journal Database, and CBM databases up until May 2024. Included studies assessed the impact of exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation on patients with IPF, with outcomes measuring six-minute walk distance (6MWD), St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) or its IPF-specific version IPF-specific St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ-I), percent-predicted diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLco%), and dyspnea scores using the modified Medical Research Council Dyspnoea Scale. Only studies published in English or Chinese were included.
RESULTS: Eight studies with 358 participants were analyzed. For 6MWD, pooled effects favored pulmonary rehabilitation at 3 months/12 weeks (mean difference [MD] = 35.98 m, 95% confidence interval [CI] 18.05-53.92), 6 months/26 weeks (MD = 36.53 m, 95% CI 19.62-53.44), and 9 to12 months/52 weeks (MD = 50.98 m, 95% CI 25.94-76.03). SGRQ/SGRQ-I improved at 6 months (MD = -8.16, 95% CI - 12.33-- 4.00) and 9 to 12 months (MD = -8.76, 95% CI - 13.06-4.46), but not clearly at 3 months (MD = -4.08, 95% CI - 9.61-1.45). DLco% improved only at 9 to12 months (MD = 7.85, 95% CI 2.80-12.90). mMRC data were available from 1 study at 12 weeks and 1 study at 6 months and were therefore not pooled within either intervention-duration ca

candidates.title: Anti-SRP and anti-HMGCR co-positivity in immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy with interstitial lung disease: A rare case report.
candidates.abstract:
RATIONALE: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare inflammatory myopathy. Coexisting anti-signal recognition particle (anti-SRP) and anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (anti-HMGCR) antibodies in statin-naïve patients with interstitial lung disease are exceptionally uncommon.
PATIENT CONCERNS: A 55-year-old statin-naïve man presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness, dysphagia, myalgia, significant weight loss, and exertional dyspnea.
DIAGNOSES: Serum creatine kinase was 8000 U/L. Anti-SRP, anti-HMGCR, and anti-Ro52 antibodies were positive. Chest computed tomography showed bilateral consolidations and ground-glass opacities suggestive of organizing pneumonia. Pulmonary function tests revealed reduced forced vital capacity (52%) and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (48%). Electromyography and muscle biopsy findings supported IMNM.
INTERVENTIONS: Treatment included high-dose corticosteroids, mycophenolate mofetil, nutritional support, and rehabilitation.
OUTCOMES: After 3 months, muscle strength improved from 3/5 to 4+/5, dysphagia resolved, and weight increased by 5 kg. Creatine kinase decreased to 350 U/L, forced vital capacity improved to 74%, and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide to 65%. Follow-up high-resolution computed tomography showed pulmonary improvement without fibrosis.
LESSONS: This case highlights the rare coexistence of anti-SRP and anti-HMGCR antibodies in statin-naïve IMNM with interstitial lung disease. Early immunosuppression, nutritional support, and rehabilitation may improve muscular and pulmonary outcomes. Comprehensive respiratory assessment and longitudinal monitoring are essential.

candidates.title: Dual-scaffold imageable embolic system with microenvironment normalization enhances hypoxia-activated chemoembolization for HCC.
candidates.abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by the post-embolization tumor microenvironment (pE-TME), which drives revascularization and fibrosis, thereby narrowing the hypoxic window and restricting drug penetration for hypoxia-activated prodrugs like tirapazamine (TPZ). To overcome this challenge, we developed a dual-scaffold theranostic platform integrating an iodinated thermosensitive PNIPAM hydrogel with genipin-crosslinked albumin microspheres for the coordinated co-delivery of nintedanib (NIB) and TPZ. This platform provides intrinsic X-ray visibility, rapid in situ gelation, enhanced mechanical strength, and sustained drug release with excellent hemocompatibility. In vitro, released NIB inhibited fibroblast proliferation, while TPZ potently induced apoptosis in hypoxic HCC cells. In vivo, the platform enabled stable vascular occlusion and prolonged tumor retention. In an orthotopic HCC model, the dual-drug combination achieved 91% tumor inhibition, significantly outperforming embolization alone and single-drug groups, without systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, TPZ promoted apoptosis (Caspase-3/Ki-67), whereas NIB suppressed compensatory angiogenesis (VEGF/CD31) and collagen deposition (α-SMA), thereby remodeling the pE-TME to stabilize hypoxia. By converting the therapy-limiting hypoxic microenvironment into a therapeutic asset, this dual-scaffold strategy offers a new paradigm for amplifying TACE efficacy.

candidates.title: Fc N-glycosylation heterogeneity of anti-MDA5 IgG is associated with interstitial lung disease severity via regulating FcγR/C1q signaling in MDA5 + dermatomyositis: a cross‑sectional study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To characterize Fc N-glycosylation patterns of disease-specific IgG (DSIgG) in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis (MDA5 + DM) and evaluate their associations with interstitial lung disease (ILD) severity.
METHODS: Eighty-four patients with MDA5 + DM and 60 healthy controls were enrolled. Disease-specific anti-MDA5 IgG glycopeptides were analyzed by UPLC-MS/MS. Associations between glycoform features and ILD severity were assessed using correlation analysis, ROC analysis, and logistic regression. Surface plasmon resonance and in vitro functional assays were used to compare glycoform-dependent engagement of FcγRIIa, FcγRIIIa, and C1q, as well as downstream ADCP, ADCC, CDC, and endothelial inflammatory responses.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, DSIgG1 from patients with MDA5 + DM showed higher fucosylation and lower sialylation. Severe ILD was associated with increased DSIgG1F and decreased DSIgG1S. In multivariable analysis, lower DSIgG1S remained independently associated with severe ILD (OR = 0.07, p = 0.0065), and DSIgG1S showed strong discriminatory performance for severe ILD (AUC = 0.9133). Functionally, G1S exhibited stronger FcγRIIa-related binding and phagocytic activity, whereas G1F displayed stronger FcγRIIIa and C1q binding, together with increased ADCC and CDC. In endothelial-cell experiments, the two glycoforms induced distinct inflammatory response patterns.
CONCLUSION: Anti-MDA5 DSIgG Fc glycosylation is associated with ILD severity in MDA5 + DM. Distinct glycoforms exhibit differential FcγR/C1q-related effector profiles, supporting a potential role for Fc glycosylation heterogeneity in disease stratification and pathogenesis.

candidates.title: Skeletal muscle quality as an independent associated factor of oxygen utilization efficiency in interstitial lung disease: a cardiopulmonary exercise testing study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reduced exercise capacity in patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) is associated with poor prognosis. Oxygen pulse (O2 pulse) reflects exercise circulatory efficiency, but its determinants at submaximal exercise remain unclear. Phase angle (PhA) has recently emerged as a surrogate marker of muscle quality.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between lower-limb PhA and submaximal O2 pulse at the ventilatory threshold (VT), which reflects daily physical activity independent of maximal volitional effort, in patients with ILD.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 111 patients with ILD enrolled in an educational hospitalization program (April 2024-March 2026). Among these, 35 patients completed cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Lower-limb PhA was assessed via bioelectrical impedance analysis. The association between PhA and O2 pulse at VT was evaluated using Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis adjusted for age, %FVC, and tricuspid regurgitation velocity (TRV).
RESULTS: The analyzed CPET sub-cohort (n = 35) had a mean age of 69.0 ± 8.4 years, 74.2% male, and %FVC of 85.3 ± 18.1%. Lower-limb PhA was significantly correlated with O2 pulse at VT (r = 0.629, p < 0.001). In multiple regression analysis, PhA remained independently associated with O2 pulse (β = 0.748, p = 0.001), with a model R2 of 0.433.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower-limb PhA is an independent associated factor of O2 pulse in patients with mild-to-moderate ILD. Given the cross-sectional and retrospective nature of this study, these findings do not establish causality but suggest that muscle quality may be a relevant clinical indicator that warrants further prospective and interventional investigation.

candidates.title: Effectiveness of tuberculosis treatment in individuals exposed to silica or with silicosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) is a global problem affecting large numbers of workers exposed to respirable crystalline silica. Both silicosis and exposure to silica without silicosis increase the risk of active TB. While some studies have suggested that silicotuberculosis (silicosis plus TB) or silica exposure on its own are associated with unsuccessful TB treatment outcomes, the evidence is inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare TB treatment outcomes in individuals with silicotuberculosis to those with TB alone, and similarly in those with TB plus silica exposure to those with TB alone.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review of randomized and nonrandomized trials, and cohort and case-control studies published 1970-2024. Studies were sought which investigated TB treatment outcomes for silicotuberculosis or silica exposure alone via PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus. We conducted risk of bias assessments using ROBINS-E for observational studies of TB treatment (silicosis or silica as the "exposure") and ROB 2 for randomized trials of different TB drug regimens. GRADE was used to assess overall certainty of evidence.
RESULTS: Seven studies met the inclusion criteria, all restricted to comparing silicotuberculosis with TB alone or different drug regimens among those with silicotuberculosis. High/very high risk of bias or "some concerns" were noted in six - due to confounding, loss to follow-up, missing data, and/or concerns about exposure or outcome measurement. The pooled odds ratio (OR) for treatment failure/delayed conversion for individuals with silicotuberculosis versus those with TB alone was 1.79 (95% CI 0.54, 5.99; N = 4, very low certainty); for mortality OR 2.45 (95% CI 0.58, 10.39; N = 2, very low certainty); and for TB recurrence OR 1.20 (95% CI 0.01, 134.89; N = 2, very low certainty). The relative risk ratio of recurrence for use of a six versus eight-month TB treatment regimen was 3.29 (95% CI: 0.77, 14.15; N = 1, very

candidates.title: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) represents the common end-stage outcome of a broad range of interstitial lung diseases. The shared pathophysiologic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify two phenotypically distinct neutrophil subsets in PF: a pro-inflammatory subset characterized by CD54 (human) or iNOS (mouse) expression, and an alternative subset marked by Arg1 expression. Notably, CD54+ and iNOS+ neutrophils were markedly expanded in PF patients and mice with bleomycin-induced PF, respectively. Adoptive transfer of iNOS+ neutrophils exacerbated fibrosis in bleomycin-induced PF, whereas transfer of Arg1+ neutrophils had no significant effect. Further, the expression of PIEZO1, a mechanically activated ion channel, is predominantly upregulated in CD54+ neutrophils from PF patients or iNOS+ neutrophils from PF mice. Piezo1 ablation in neutrophils selectively impairs iNOS+ neutrophil differentiation, thereby attenuating fibrosis progression. Mechanistically, PIEZO1 promotes the differentiation of these pro-inflammatory subsets through the transcription factor IRF4 in a calcium-dependent manner. We further identify the JAK/STAT pathway as an upstream regulator of PIEZO1 expression in neutrophils. Consequently, PIEZO1 expression and CD54+ neutrophils are markedly decreased in patients treated with JAK inhibitor baricitinib. Importantly, combined inhibition of JAK/STAT and calcium signaling exerts synergistic suppression on the iNOS+ neutrophil expansion and PF progression. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism in which PIEZO1 promotes PF by specifically driving the expansion of CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophils.

candidates.title: Extracellular vesicles presenting "don't eat me" signal limit the efferocytic capacity in lung fibrosis.
candidates.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
candidates.abstract: Efferocytosis is essential for tissue homeostasis and resolution of inflammation, yet its direct contribution to resolve organ fibrosis remains poorly understood. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive age-driven lung disease, we found profound suppression of efferocytosis coupled with robust production and release of extracellular vesicles presenting functional receptor CD47, a canonical "don't eat me" mediator. Restoration of efferocytosis contributes to the natural resolution of fibrosis, which is accelerated by CD47 deficiency or alterations in macrophage metabolic responses. In turn, pharmacologic disruption of efferocytic receptors or signaling results in lung fibrosis development and its persistence. While sustained reduction of efferocytic capacity align with fibrosis persistence in aged mice, AMPK activation promotes fibrosis resolution via reducing inflammaging and CD47 bioavailability, thus restoring clearance of apoptotic fibroblast. Importantly, AMPK activation also reprograms macrophages engaging apoptotic fibroblasts toward a fibrosis pro-resolving phenotype by suppressing TGF-β1 and promoting secretion of pro-regenerative hepatocyte growth factor (HGF). Together, these findings link metabolism and immune efferocytic fitness in lung fibrosis resolution and suggest that an AMPK senomorphic pathway has broad therapeutic relevance for fibrotic diseases.

candidates.title: Novel ZNFX1 Variants Associated With Refractory Anemia and Interstitial Lung Disease.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ZNFX1 deficiency is a rare inborn error of immunity characterized by recurrent infections, hyperinflammation, cytopenias, and multiorgan involvement. Owing to the limited number of reported cases, its clinical and molecular spectrum remains incompletely defined.
METHODS: Clinical evaluation, whole-exome sequencing (WES) of the proband, Sanger sequencing for variant validation and segregation analysis, RNA sequencing, AlphaFold-based structural modeling, and interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) expression analysis were performed. Variants were interpreted according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines.
RESULTS: A Chinese girl presented with refractory anemia, hyperinflammation, digital clubbing, developmental delay, and interstitial lung disease (ILD). WES of the proband identified three previously unreported ZNFX1 variants. Subsequent Sanger sequencing and segregation analysis confirmed that c.981dupA (p.Asp328Argfs*4) was paternally inherited, whereas c.1605_1630delinsGGGAATATCGTGGA (p.Asn535_Val543delinsLysGlyIleSerTrp) and c.2893G>A (p.Glu965Lys) were maternally inherited. According to ACMG criteria, one variant was classified as likely pathogenic and the other two as variants of uncertain significance. RNA sequencing demonstrated reduced ZNFX1 expression, while AlphaFold-based modeling suggested local structural alterations. ISG expression analysis indicated activation of Type I interferon signaling.
CONCLUSION: We report a child with ZNFX1 deficiency carrying three previously unreported ZNFX1 variants associated with refractory anemia and ILD. These findings expand both the molecular and phenotypic spectrum of ZNFX1 deficiency and highlight the value of integrating genomic, transcriptomic, structural modeling, and ISG expression analyses for molecular diagnosis.

candidates.title: Associations of ECG-derived markers with clinical and biological characteristics in systemic sclerosis: preliminary findings from the SCAR-SSc study.
candidates.abstract: Cardiac involvement in systemic sclerosis (SSc) is often subclinical in its early stages. Electrocardiographic markers have been associated with arrhythmias and myocardial remodeling and may provide insight into cardiac involvement in SSc. This pilot single-center cross-sectional study explored associations between ECG-derived parameters and clinical and biological features in patients with SSc without overt cardiovascular disease. Thirty-four patients meeting the 2013 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology classification criteria were included. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity troponin I were measured, standard 12-lead ECGs were analyzed for interatrial block (IAB), morphology-voltage-P-wave duration (MVP) score and fragmented QRS (fQRS), and 24-hour Holter monitoring was used to quantify arrhythmias. Participants were 85.3% women, with a median (IQR) age of 53.6 (46-61) years and disease duration of 7.95 (1.5-14.8) years; 76.5% had limited cutaneous SSc. Fragmented QRS was present in 7 of 32 patients with evaluable fQRS data (21.9%), and its presence was associated with a higher premature ventricular contraction count on Holter monitoring after adjustment for age and sex (OR = 1.0022; 95% CI, 1.0001-1.0044; P = 0.044). Partial IAB was present in 4 of 8 patients (50%) with diffuse cutaneous SSc. The modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS) differed between patients with and without IAB (9 ± 9 versus 3 ± 4, P = 0.040). Higher MVP scores were associated with mRSS (β = 0.422, P = 0.026), C-reactive protein (β = 0.412, P = 0.028) and NT-proBNP (β = 0.557, P = 0.003). ECG-derived markers were associated with measures of disease severity, ventricular ectopy and NT-proBNP levels. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies.

candidates.title: Real-World Progression Patterns and Potential Prognostic Factors for Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Related Interstitial Lung Disease in Japanese Patients With Breast or Gastric Cancer.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis is a safety concern with trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd). We characterized post-onset changes in ILD severity and imaging patterns, and explored potential prognostic factors for fatal T-DXd-related ILD in Japanese patients with breast or gastric cancer.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis included 381 independently adjudicated T-DXd-related ILD cases from two Japanese all-patient post-marketing surveillance studies. We described transitions from onset to worst Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade and imaging pattern changes. Exploratory tumor type-stratified Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess factors associated with time to fatal (Grade 5) ILD. The variable with the highest hazard ratio (HR) and each of the remaining significant univariate factors (p < 0.05 or a 95% confidence interval excluding 1) meeting the criteria were included in two-covariate multivariable models.
RESULTS: At ILD onset, 60.1% of patients had Grade 1 ILD. Overall, 30 of the 381 adjudicated ILD cases (7.9%) progressed to fatal Grade 5, initially presenting with Grade 1 (n = 9), 2 (n = 5), or 3 (n = 16); time to death was 3-173 days. Of 24 cases with imaging pattern changes, 14 transitioned from nondiffuse alveolar damage (non-DAD) to DAD (10 were fatal). Abnormal C-reactive protein (CRP) at onset had the highest HR in univariate analyses. In separate CRP-adjusted two-covariate multivariable models, preexisting ILD and several onset factors (dyspnea; abnormal SpO2/lactate dehydrogenase/Krebs von den Lungen-6; pleural/cardiac effusion; DAD pattern; traction bronchiectasis) were associated with fatal ILD. An organizing pneumonia pattern was associated with a lower hazard.
CONCLUSIONS: T-DXd-related ILD may progress rapidly to fatal outcomes, even from low-grade or non-DAD presentations, and several onset factors (e.g., elevated CRP, decreased SpO2, and DAD pattern) were associated with fatal ILD outcomes. These fin

candidates.title: Occult lung adenocarcinoma diagnosed by EBUS-TBNA after pneumothorax resolution in an RA-ILD patient with respiratory failure.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: RA-ILD is a serious complication of RA. Patients are prone to spontaneous pneumothorax and have a higher risk of lung cancer.Given poor lung function and high risk of pneumothorax recurrence, conventional biopsy is challenging, making diagnosis difficult.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 67-year-old male with a history of smoking and well-controlled rheumatoid arthritis presented with chest tightness and pleuritic chest pain. On admission, he was found to have respiratory failure (PaO₂ 58.9mmHg). Chest CT revealed left-sided pneumothorax with interstitial lung disease.Following closed thoracic drainage, the pneumothorax resolved, which was confirmed by follow-up chest X-ray.But the persistence of the patient's chest pain despite resolution of the pneumothorax prompted further investigation.CT pulmonary angiography identified a suspicious mass in the left lower lobe with adjacent rib destruction and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Given the high risk of recurrent pneumothorax from percutaneous biopsy in a patient with recent pneumothorax and pre-existing respiratory failure, a multidisciplinary team recommended Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration(EBUS-TBNA) as a safer alternative. EBUS of enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes (stations 7 and 11L) confirmed poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinoma.The patient subsequently received first-line chemotherapy with pemetrexed, cisplatin, and bevacizumab, after which his condition gradually stabilized.
CONCLUSION: Both pneumothorax and interstitial lung disease can mask an occult malignancy, underscoring the need for clinical vigilance. EBUS-TBNA is a safe and effective diagnostic option in such high-risk cases.

candidates.title: Rheumatoid factor positivity in ANCA-negative eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: cardiac mimicry, mononeuritis multiplex, and long-term outcome in a case-based systematic review.
candidates.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare small- to medium-vessel vasculitis characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and multisystem involvement. Diagnosis is challenging in ANCA-negative disease, particularly when misleading serology is present. We describe a 42-year-old woman with long-standing asthma and a rheumatoid factor (RF) of 322 IU/mL, who initially presented with myocardial infarction-like cardiac involvement with non-obstructive coronary arteries. Over the subsequent seven months, progressive eosinophilia, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, and mononeuritis multiplex emerged. ANCA-negative EGPA was diagnosed after connective tissue disease, infection, malignancy, and other causes of hypereosinophilia were excluded. She was treated with prednisolone and azathioprine and subsequently remained off immunosuppressive therapy for more than nine years without reported relapse. On later clinical reassessment, she remained stable apart from mild residual neuropathic symptoms. We also conducted a case-based review following the CABARET standards, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science up to 15 August 2026. We identified 38 published cases of ANCA-negative, RF-positive EGPA, 36 of them without pre-existing rheumatoid arthritis. In these 36, the median age was 53 years and 69% were female. Peripheral neuropathy was reported in 72% and cardiac involvement in 47%; with both occurring in 25%; two patients died of cardiac causes. Among 12 cases with sufficient data to standardize RF relative to the assay upper limit of normal, 75% had RF levels > 3 × ULN. Reporting was often incomplete: both MPO- and PR3-ANCA were documented in only 42% of cases and anti-CCP in 11%. No included published case reported prolonged treatment-free remission, although follow-up and treatment status were incompletely reported in several cases. Based on these gaps, the authors propose a reporting checklist for future EGPA case reports. RF posi

candidates.title: Pulmonary involvement in Gaucher disease patients receiving enzyme replacement therapy: a cross-sectional analysis of radiological and functional lung abnormalities.
candidates.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Pulmonary involvement in Gaucher disease (GD) is underrecognized and may range from asymptomatic radiological abnormalities to respiratory impairment. This study assessed pulmonary involvement and its associations with disease phenotype, genotype, and pulmonary function in patients receiving long-term enzyme replacement therapy (ERT). In this single-center cross-sectional study, 52 genetically confirmed patients with GD receiving ERT underwent clinical assessment and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT). Spirometry was performed in 34 cooperative patients aged ≥ 6 years. Clinical characteristics, genotype, baseline glucosylsphingosine (lyso-GL1), and disease phenotype were analyzed in relation to pulmonary findings. Respiratory symptoms were present in 19/52 (36.5%) patients. HRCT demonstrated interstitial abnormalities suggestive of interstitial lung disease (ILD) in 24/52 (46.2%), predominantly ground-glass opacities and interstitial thickening. These abnormalities were more frequent in type 3 than type 1 GD (P = 0.001). Homozygous L483P was associated with HRCT abnormalities suggestive of ILD in univariable analysis (P = 0.013). Among 34 patients undergoing spirometry, 11 (32.4%) had abnormal results, including obstructive (8.8%), restrictive (11.8%), and mixed (11.8%) patterns. Abnormal spirometry was associated with HRCT abnormalities (P < 0.001), while three patients had radiological abnormalities despite preserved spirometry. On multivariable analysis, higher baseline lyso-GL1, type 3 phenotype, and kyphoscoliosis were independently associated with HRCT abnormalities suggestive of ILD.
CONCLUSION: Pulmonary abnormalities remained common despite long-term ERT, particularly in type 3 GD. HRCT detected interstitial abnormalities in some patients with preserved spirometry, suggesting that structural pulmonary involvement may precede functional impairment. candidates.title: Colorectal cancer-derived IGFBP2 promotes liver metastasis by driving intrahepatic fibrotic pre-metastatic niche formation.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC) liver metastasis (LM) is a leading cause of cancer-related death, with pre-metastatic niche (PMN) formation being critical for metastasis. Insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2 (IGFBP2) is overexpressed in metastatic CRC, but its role in intrahepatic fibrotic PMN formation and CRC-LM remains unclear.
METHODS: Bioinformatics analyses and tissue microarray samples were conducted to assess the expression level and prognostic significance of IGFBP2 in CRC patients. After overexpression of IGFBP2, its in vivo metastatic-promoting ability was evaluated by establishing a splenic injection liver metastasis model, while its in vitro malignant properties were assessed via colony formation, proliferation assay, flow cytometry, wound-healing assay and transwell assay. Furthermore, flow cytometry, RT-qPCR and ELISA were used to evaluate the effect of IGFBP2 overexpression on the polarization of intrahepatic macrophages. In addition, Western blot and immunofluorescence were performed to detect the effect of M2-polarized macrophages on hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). Finally, the splenic injection liver metastasis model was treated with CWI1-2 (IGFBP2 inhibitor) or pirfenidone (PFD, a TGF-β signaling modulator), and the therapeutic effects were observed.
RESULTS: We found that IGFBP2 is overexpressed in CRC tissues, correlating with poor prognosis. Meanwhile, IGFBP2 overexpression significantly promotes CRC-LM progression in vivo. Mechanistically, it drives M2 polarization of intrahepatic macrophages to boost TGF-β secretion. Subsequently, TGF-β activates HSCs, elevates the deposition of extracellular matrix (α-SMA, COL1, FN), and ultimately contributes to the development of intrahepatic fibrotic PMN. Notably, CWI-2 or PFD could suppress CRC-LM, with combined treatment showing synergistic effects both in vitro and in vivo.
CONCLUSIONS: IGFBP2 is highly expressed in CRC and correlated with patient prognosis. CRC-derived IGFBP2 drives intrah

candidates.title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based diagnostic prediction model for adult eosinophilic asthma.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult eosinophilic asthma (EA) is a predominant phenotype of severe asthma. Induced sputum cytology, the diagnostic gold standard, is limited by complex procedures and poor feasibility. Non-invasive type 2 markers perform unsatisfactorily, and existing machine learning models lack interpretability and clinical accessibility.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to construct a machine learning (ML)-based prediction model for EA to enable accurate phenotyping and personalized precision treatment of asthma.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective study was performed at a tertiary hospital in China. A total of 734 asthmatic patients who underwent induced sputum cytology were screened, and 503 were ultimately included. Data preprocessing, missing value imputation, and feature normalization were conducted within the training set to avoid data leakage. Ten ML algorithms were developed with hyperparameter tuning and internal cross-validation for model optimization. Model performance was assessed using AUC, calibration curves, DCA, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, and confusion matrix. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was used to improve model interpretability.
RESULTS: Our results showed that the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) model outperformed the other 9 ML algorithms. After feature selection, an interpretable final KNN model incorporating 6 features was developed, achieving the following performance metrics: AUC = 0.814, accuracy = 0.780, sensitivity = 0.845, specificity = 0.697, precision = 0.780, and F1-score = 0.811. Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO50) was the most important predictor, followed by blood eosinophil count (bEOS). A web-based prediction tool with a probability threshold of 0.391 was developed for clinical use.
CONCLUSION: The developed ML model holds promise as a non-invasive alternative to induced sputum cytology for EA diagnosis. The corresponding web-based prediction tool is accessible at https://mm-zhou-2026.

candidates.title: [Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder incidentally diagnosed at autopsy in a second relapse of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma after cord blood transplantation].
candidates.journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology
candidates.abstract: A 63-year-old woman presented with a relapse of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATL). At age 56, she was diagnosed with acute ATL and achieved a partial response with induction chemotherapy. She underwent unrelated allogeneic cord blood transplantation with an HLA 2-antigen 1-allele mismatched donor. Five years and seven months after transplantation, she experienced abdominal pain and noticed fecaluria. A mass was identified on the ventral side of the sigmoid colon, accompanied by a sigmoid-vaginal-vesical fistula. Based on a biopsy of the mass protruding into the sigmoid lumen, she was diagnosed with relapsed disease on day 2,072 after transplantation. She received mogamulizumab monotherapy and achieved a complete response. However, the reappearance of ascites led to diagnosis of a second relapse on day 2,370 after transplantation, confirmed by ascitic fluid cytology. Retreatment with mogamulizumab monotherapy was unsuccessful due to refractory disease. The patient died on day 2,409 after transplantation from complications of both ATL and cryptogenic organizing pneumonia. An autopsy was performed, and a diagnosis of post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder was incidentally made from a 15-mm solitary nodular lesion in the right upper lobe of the lung.

candidates.title: Unifocal Frontal Bone Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis Presenting as Persistent Post-Traumatic Swelling in a Child with an Asthma Exacerbation: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare disorder characterized by the clonal proliferation of Langerhans cells, and osseous involvement is the most frequent manifestation in pediatric patients. Although pulmonary involvement is recognized in LCH, respiratory presentations typically reflect direct pulmonary or airway disease rather than reversible obstructive symptoms. We report the case of a 4-year-old child with persistent, painful frontal swelling following minor trauma, which was initially presumed to be a post-traumatic hematoma. During the diagnostic course, the patient developed an asthma exacerbation that improved with bronchodilator and corticosteroid therapy. Imaging revealed a solitary osteolytic lesion of the frontal bone, and histopathological examination confirmed unifocal LCH. No clinical or chest radiographic evidence of pulmonary involvement was identified. This case underscored that persistent post-traumatic cranial swelling warrants imaging and histopathological evaluation, and highlights that the concurrent asthma exacerbation represents a temporal clinical overlap without proven causality.

candidates.title: Composition-driven fibrogenic potential of environmental particles: Complementary roles of iron-mediated redox activity and silica-associated TGF-β adsorption.
candidates.abstract: Respirable mineral particles are compositionally heterogeneous environmental stressors increasingly linked to pulmonary fibrosis, yet how coexisting reactive mineral phases regulate early profibrotic signalling remains unclear. In this study, the fibrogenic potential of respirable mineral particles with distinct silica and iron mineralogy was evaluated using alveolar macrophages (AMs), fibroblasts (FBs), A549 epithelial cells, and a Sprague-Dawley rat model, focusing on transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-associated signalling. At equivalent particle burdens, silica-bearing particles promoted profibrotic responses partly by enhancing TGF-β adsorption and associated fibroblast activation, leading to stronger α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) expression in FBs. In parallel, bioavailable iron (BAI) released from reduced iron-bearing phases induced stronger early reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation in AMs, enhanced CD206-associated responses among surviving AMs, and increased TGF-β production, indicating macrophage-mediated amplification of fibrogenic signalling. Under a focused high-dose in vivo challenge using a single selected BAI-rich particle sample (PM 2), the PM 2-silica mixture exhibited significantly greater collagen deposition than either individual particle group at day 42, providing supportive tissue-level evidence for a composition-associated mixed-particle response. These findings support an adverse outcome pathway relevant framework in which silica and BAI regulate distinct but complementary early events converging on pulmonary fibrosis.

candidates.title: Efficacy and Safety of Datopotamab Deruxtecan From a Single-Institution Experience in Hormone Receptor-Positive, HER2-Negative Metastatic Breast Cancer After Multiple Prior Therapies Including Antibody-Drug Conjugates.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) is a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) with a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload and was approved by the Japan Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency in 2025 for patients with unresectable or recurrent hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) breast cancer previously treated with chemotherapy. In the pivotal TROPION-Breast01 trial, most patients had received 1 or 2 prior systemic regimens. However, in routine clinical practice, Dato-DXd is often used in heavily pretreated patients, including those with prior ADC exposure. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of Dato-DXd in this population.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 18 patients with HR+/HER2- metastatic or recurrent breast cancer who received Dato-DXd at our institution between May and December 2025. Clinical data from electronic medical records were reviewed to assess treatment efficacy and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs).
RESULTS: All patients were female, with a median age of 56 years (range, 48-81). Patients were heavily pretreated, with a median of seven prior systemic treatment lines (range, 2-11); 72.2% had previously received trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd). Median real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) was 3.2 months. Patients with prior T-DXd exposure had significantly shorter rwPFS than T-DXd-naïve patients (2.8 vs. 6.4 months, p < 0.01). TRAEs were generally mild and manageable. The most common TRAEs included alopecia, fatigue, constipation, stomatitis, nausea, and elevated liver transaminases. Five patients required dose reductions, but no treatment discontinuations or fatal events occurred. No cases of interstitial lung disease occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of heavily pretreated HR+/HER2- metastatic or recurrent breast cancer, Dato-DXd showed limited clinical activity compared with clinical trials, particularly among patients p

candidates.title: The Latest Progress in the Application of Tofacitinib in Rheumatic Diseases--A Narrative Review.
candidates.abstract: Tofacitinib is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that modulates cytokine-dependent JAK/STAT signaling and has been extensively investigated in rheumatic diseases. This narrative review provides an updated synthesis of the pharmacological characteristics, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, drug-drug interactions and dosing considerations of tofacitinib in special populations. The relevant literature published from January 2013 through December 2025 was identified through searches of MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. After screening and eligibility assessment, 89 clinical publications were included in the disease-specific evidence synthesis, and the strength of clinical evidence across disease indications was evaluated qualitatively. The most robust evidence is available for rheumatoid arthritis, with randomized trials, long-term extension studies, and real-world investigations demonstrating improvements in disease activity and physical function and inhibition of radiographic progression. Clinical evidence also supports therapeutic benefit in psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis, whereas evidence for Takayasu arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, systemic lupus erythematosus, and anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease remains limited or exploratory. Long-term integrated safety analyses in RA have reported incidence rates of serious adverse events of approximately 9.0-9.4 per 100 patient-years and serious infections of approximately 2.5-2.7 per 100 patient-years, while herpes zoster, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism, and malignancy remain clinically important safety considerations. Potential drug-drug interactions and dose adjustment in patients with renal or hepatic impairment and other special populations further require individualized assessment. Overall, tofacitinib has a we

candidates.title: An FCN1+ macrophage-associated SEMA3C-NRP1 axis is linked to fibroblast reprogramming in RA-ILD.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD) is a major extra-articular complication of rheumatoid arthritis and a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. Unlike idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), RA-ILD develops in the context of systemic immune activation, but the cellular basis linking inflammation to fibroblast-state changes remains incompletely understood.
METHODS: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on lung tissues from healthy donors, patients with RA-ILD, and patients with IPF, complemented by spatial validation and in vitro experiments.
RESULTS: In this cohort, RA-ILD lungs showed an increased proportion of FCN1⁺ inflammatory macrophages within the macrophage compartment, whereas IPF lungs were dominated by SPP1⁺ macrophages. Trajectory and cell-cell communication analyses identified an RA-ILD-enriched matrix-fibroblast-to-CXCR4⁺ lipofibroblast program and a predicted SEMA3C-NRP1 interaction between inflammatory macrophage populations and fibroblasts; these patterns were not detected in the IPF or healthy-control samples analyzed here. Multiplex immunofluorescence showed macrophage-associated SEMA3C signal in spatial proximity to NRP1⁺ fibroblasts within fibrotic regions. A flow-sorted inflammatory monocyte/macrophage-enriched population from RA-ILD lungs had higher supernatant SEMA3C levels and was associated with shifts in MRC-5 fibroblast markers from EBF1/PDGFRA toward APOE/CXCR4. Recombinant SEMA3C reproduced this marker-defined shift, whereas pharmacological NRP1 inhibition attenuated it; an orthogonal THP-1 overexpression model produced concordant results.
DISCUSSION: These data support an association between an inflammatory macrophage-SEMA3C-NRP1 axis and fibroblast-state remodeling in the studied RA-ILD samples. Because the RA-ILD cohort was small and did not include other CTD-ILD subtypes, the findings should not be interpreted as establishing RA-ILD specificity or a fully profibrotic functional phenotyp

candidates.title: Carbonic anhydrase 4 restrains dual TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 innate immune signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in methotrexate-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Methotrexate (MTX)-induced pulmonary fibrosis (MTX-PF) is the most severe and frequently irreversible manifestation of MTX pulmonary toxicity, yet the molecular target and signaling circuitry linking drug exposure to fibrosis remain undefined, hampering diagnosis and targeted intervention.
METHODS: We integrated network toxicology, an ensemble of 112 machine-learning classifiers and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) with six GEO cohorts to nominate fibrotic-lung genes, which were intersected with predicted MTX targets to prioritize candidates relevant to MTX-PF. Lead candidates were validated by molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation, MM-PBSA binding free energy calculation and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). In vivo MTX-induced mouse models and in vitro BEAS-2B assays, including the Transwell migration/invasion, EdU proliferation, immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, CA4 and TLR4 overexpression, and a CA4/TLR4 co-overexpression rescue experiment, were performed to assess the regulatory role of the top-ranked gene.
RESULTS: Carbonic anhydrase 4 (CA4) ranked first by SHAP importance (0.120) and diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.879); the Ridge model discriminated training and validation cohorts (AUC = 0.930, 0.897 and 0.864). MTX bound stably to CA4 in silico (Vina -7.078 kcal/mol; MM-PBSA ΔGbind -76.5 kJ/mol), and SPR detected concentration-dependent binding to recombinant CA4 (KD = 6.25 μM), identifying CA4 as a candidate direct binding partner. In MTX-treated mice, CA4 was downregulated while TLR4, collagen deposition and serum TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IFN-α and IFN-β were elevated. In BEAS-2B cells, CA4 overexpression suppressed migration, invasion and proliferation, reversed MTX-induced upregulation of TLR4, NF-κB, IRF3, VIM, FN1 and COL1A1, and restored E-cadherin. Forced TLR4 overexpression reversed the protective effect of CA4 and re-established the inflammatory and mesenchymal phenotype.
