candidates.title: Species distribution and antifungal susceptibility profiles of Trichosporon species: a multicenter study of 223 clinical isolates from South China.
candidates.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trichosporon species have emerged as opportunistic pathogens, causing life-threatening invasive infections. However, epidemiological data from South China remain limited. This multicenter study investigates the species distribution, genotypic characteristics, and antifungal susceptibility profiles of clinical Trichosporon isolates from this region.
METHODS: A total of 223 unique clinical Trichosporon isolates were collected from 18 centers in five South China provinces. These isolates were identified using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) and sequencing of the intergenic spacer 1 (IGS1) region. The Trichosporon asahii isolates were further analyzed through IGS1 sequence analysis for genotyping. The minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of six antifungal agents were determined using the broth microdilution method outlined by the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI). Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on isolates with high fluconazole MICs and on randomly selected low-MIC isolates to characterize ERG11 mutations.
RESULTS: IGS1 sequencing identified 220 of the 223 isolates to the species level, representing eight species, with T. asahii predominating (171, 77.7%). The species-level concordance between MALDI-TOF MS and IGS1 sequencing was 85.5% (188/220), with substantial interspecies variation. Genotypes 1 (32.7%) and 3 (32.2%) co-predominated among T. asahii isolates, with no significant association found between genotype and specimen source (P = 0.663). Voriconazole was the most active agent, with a MIC90 of 0.125 μg/mL and a geometric mean (GM) of 0.06 μg/mL. High fluconazole MICs were consistently associated with specific ERG11 substitutions: Y133F in T. dohaense and L229I, V132A, and Y133F in T. asteroides.
CONCLUSIONS: T. asahii is the predominant clinical Trichosporon species in South China. Voriconazole is the most effective antifungal agent against Trichosporon. Sp

candidates.title: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis: Clinical Paradigm Evolution, Immune-Driven Mechanisms, and Fibrotic Progression.
candidates.abstract: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP) is a complex immune-mediated interstitial lung disease (ILD) triggered by inhaled antigens in genetically susceptible individuals. Recent diagnostic paradigms have shifted from exposure-centric empiricism to fibrosis-based stratification and, most recently, separation of etiology from morphology, with fibrotic HP (FHP) now recognized as a progressive fibrotic phenotype distinct from yet overlapping with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Mechanistically, HP progression reflects a sequential cascade involving gene-environment interactions, dysregulated innate and adaptive immunity, and maladaptive repair. Early disease is characterized by Th1/Th17-driven granulomatous inflammation, whereas chronic FHP exhibits Th2/M2 polarization, tertiary lymphoid structures, B-cell dysregulation, cellular senescence, lung microbiome dysbiosis, and persistent fibroblast activation, ultimately leading to progressively less reversible remodeling. Despite shared terminal pathways with IPF (e.g., extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, EndoMT, and SASP), FHP may be conceptualized as predominantly inflammation-driven or "top-down," whereas IPF is often viewed as predominantly epithelial injury-driven or "bottom-up"; however, these heuristic models are not mutually exclusive and do not establish a discrete mechanistic transition or a uniform therapeutic window. Antigen avoidance remains the cornerstone of management; immunomodulatory treatment may be considered in selected inflammation-predominant phenotypes, whereas antifibrotic treatment may be considered when FHP meets criteria for progressive pulmonary fibrosis. The role of combined therapy remains uncertain, and strategies targeting IL-17, IL-6, or JAK-STAT remain investigational in HP. Early diagnosis is hindered by occult antigens and nonspecific presentations. Future advances will depend on multiomics integration, novel antigen-detection tools, and biomarkers that may help characterize the propos

candidates.title: [Cone beam CT-guided bronchoscopic navigation: step by step].
candidates.abstract: The assessment of peripheral lung lesions (PPH) is gaining increasing importance with the introduction of lung cancer screening using low-dose CT. Bronchoscopic navigation techniques, such as electromagnetic or virtual navigation bronchoscopy or robot-assisted bronchoscopy, are used for histological evaluation and have improved diagnostic accuracy. Navigation to the lesion using a preoperative chest CT scan can be inaccurate, particularly for small lesions or those in the lower lobe, due to CT-to-body divergence. Intraoperative 3D imaging using cone beam CT (CBCT) can significantly improve diagnostic accuracy. The combination of modern navigation techniques and CBCT is non-inferior to CT-guided transthoracic biopsy in terms of diagnostic accuracy and has a significantly more favorable risk profile. This article provides a detailed step-by-step description of how to perform CBCT-guided bronchoscopy.

candidates.title: Deep learning reconstruction for low-dose thoracic CT of calcification inserts: A phantom study of CNR, noise magnitude, and noise texture.
candidates.journal: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare filtered back projection (FBP), 50% Adaptive Statistical Iterative Reconstruction-Veo (ASiR), and medium-strength deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) for hydroxyapatite calcification inserts under different dose, tube-voltage, and phantom-size conditions using contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), background noise magnitude, and noise power spectrum (NPS) analysis.
METHODS: A QRM-Thorax containing a QRM-CCI D100 cardiac calcification insert was scanned on a GE Revolution Apex CT system using institution-defined routine and low-dose protocols at 80, 100, 120, and 140 kVp, with and without an Extension Ring L. Images were reconstructed at 2.5-mm thickness using FBP, ASiR, and DLIR. CNR was evaluated for 3- and 5-mm inserts at 200, 400, and 800 mg HA/cm3. Background noise was assessed from a calcification-excluded mask. For NPS analysis, 10 calcification-free images were analyzed for each acquisition condition. Total two-dimensional NPS power, power-weighted normalized radial NPS, and power-weighted mean spatial frequency were calculated.
RESULTS: DLIR reduced background noise magnitude and increased CNR relative to FBP across the evaluated conditions, whereas differences relative to ASiR varied with insert size, density, tube voltage, and phantom size. Across all 16 protocol, phantom-size, and tube-voltage combinations, ASiR and DLIR reduced total 2D NPS power by 58.1% and 75.8%, respectively, relative to FBP; DLIR reduced total power by 41.9% relative to ASiR. ASiR produced a more consistent shift toward lower power-weighted mean spatial frequencies, averaging 12.4% below FBP, whereas the shift with DLIR was smaller and more condition dependent, averaging 3.2% below FBP.
CONCLUSIONS: In this controlled phantom study, DLIR reduced total noise power and improved CNR relative to FBP, but its incremental difference from ASiR was task and protocol dependent. CNR and noise magnitude should be interpreted together with NPS because nonlinear reconstruction

candidates.title: Asymptomatic tuberculosis among people detected by community-wide active versus passive case finding in Vietnam.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A substantial proportion of people with tuberculosis (TB) do not experience or report typical symptoms. We aimed to describe the characteristics of people with asymptomatic TB disease (aTB) and compare its proportion among people diagnosed with TB during community-wide active case finding (ACF) and passive case finding (PCF) in Vietnam.
METHODS: We undertook a cohort study in Ca Mau Province, Vietnam, comparing people with pulmonary TB detected through community-wide ACF using rapid molecular testing irrespective of symptoms, and those diagnosed through routine care at district health facilities (PCF) over the same period. We defined aTB as TB disease without symptoms, based on a post-diagnosis questionnaire. Secondary analyses applied alternative aTB definitions: absence of WHO 4-symptoms and cough for ≥2 weeks. We used modified Poisson regression with robust sandwich variance to quantify the prevalence ratio for aTB in ACF versus PCF.
RESULTS: Asymptomatic disease was present in 0.9% (PCF) and 12.9% (ACF) of people diagnosed with TB. People with aTB showed lower culture positivity and Xpert Mycobacterium tuberculosis/rifampicin semi-quantitative levels. However, >70% had chest X-ray findings consistent with TB. Compared to PCF, ACF-detected cases were more likely to lack symptoms under each definition: adjusted prevalence ratios for aTB were 13.7 [95%CI 3.2-58.7] for asymptomatic, 2.6 [95%CI 1.6-4.5] for WHO 4-symptoms, and 1.9 [95%CI 1.3-2.8] for cough ≥2 weeks.
CONCLUSION: Community-wide ACF detected a significantly higher proportion of aTB than PCF. Screening strategies that require symptoms as a prerequisite are likely to miss a substantial proportion of people with TB.

candidates.title: Development of a lung nodule volumetry tool for quality assurance assessment of low-dose lung cancer screening CT protocols.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-dose CT (LDCT) is the preferred modality for lung nodule detection and follow-up, yet standardized quality-control criteria are lacking. Volumetric accuracy is clinically important but strongly dependent on segmentation and reconstruction settings, particularly for small, low-contrast subsolid nodules, and frameworks for optimizing LDCT protocols based on volumetric performance remain limited.
PURPOSE: To develop a lung nodule segmentation and volumetry tool that evaluates volumetric accuracy across CT reconstruction settings and to demonstrate how accuracy and repeatability metrics can support protocol comparison as a quality-assurance assessment.
METHODS: A custom semi-automatic tool was developed in Python and evaluated using the QRM Thorax phantom on a GE Revolution Apex CT system. Fifteen artificial nodules were analyzed, combining five diameters (3-12 mm) and three attenuation levels (100, -630, -800 HU). Reconstruction parameters were systematically varied, including kernel (STANDARD, LUNG), slice thickness (0.625-2.5 mm), spacing (0.625, 1.25 mm), algorithm (DLIR-H and ASiR-V at 80%), and field of view (18, 36 cm). Performance was assessed using mean relative volume error (target within ± 20%), repeatability coefficient (RC), and size-specific RMSE; the best-performing configuration per nodule type served as reference. Reconstruction effects were evaluated using factorial ANOVA, Levene's test, Welch's t-test, and bootstrap analysis with false-discovery-rate correction.
RESULTS: Overall mean relative volume errors ranged from -7.1% to 6.7% for solid nodules and -14.7% to 5.8% for type 1 subsolid nodules ≥ 5  mm; type 2 subsolid nodules showed larger deviations (-27.1% to -12.1%). Nodule size and reconstruction kernel were the dominant contributors to mean volume error, while slice thickness and spacing mainly influenced variability. Significant differences from the reference were found for four solid-nodule settings, none for type 1, and one f

candidates.title: An integrated radiomics-pathomics approach for predicting efficacy and prognosis of immunotherapy in advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a multimodal model for predicting progression-free survival (PFS) and survival probability of immunotherapy in patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 182 inoperable NSCLC patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors. The primary endpoint was defined as durable clinical benefit (DCB, PFS ≥ 6 months) and non-durable clinical benefit (NDB, PFS < 6 months). Overall survival (OS) was the secondary endpoint for long-term efficacy. Clinical characteristics were selected using univariate and multivariate regression analyses. Radiomics features were extracted from pre-treatment computed tomography (CT) images, and pathomics features were extracted from whole slide images. A multimodal integrated model was constructed by combining clinical characteristics, radiomics-pathomics features, and utilizing multiple machine learning classifiers. The performance of the model was evaluated by plotting the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and calculating the area under the curves (AUC). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox regression analysis were applied to analyze OS.
RESULTS: The multimodal model using Logistic regression classifier demonstrated better predictive performance in distinguishing DCB from NDB than any unimodal models (including the clinical, radiomics and pathomics model), with AUC of 0.90 (95%CI: 0.82-0.98) in the test cohort. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression analysis revealed significant survival differences between DCB and NDB groups stratified by the multimodal model. Two nomograms were developed to predict DCB and survival probabilities, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: The combination of radiomics and pathomics features showed complementary value in predicting the efficacy and prognosis of immunotherapy, potentially improving individualized treatment in NSCLC.

candidates.title: PET/CT radiomics-based prognostic model with exploratory deep learning features in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (LA-NSCLC) is characterized by substantial heterogeneity, and the traditional TNM staging system has limited capacity for individualized prognostic assessment. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a comprehensive prognostic model integrating clinical characteristics, tumor burden, and PET/CT-based radiomics with exploratory deep learning features, and to assess model interpretability using machine-learning techniques.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included patients with LA-NSCLC who underwent pretreatment 18F-FDG PET/CT and were divided into training and internal test cohorts. Radiomic features were extracted separately from PET and CT images, and endpoint-specific radiomics risk scores were constructed using elastic-net Cox regression. A dual-branch 3D CNN-Transformer framework generated deep-learning risk scores. Clinical variables, radiomics, and deep-learning features were integrated to establish multimodal prognostic models for overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). All feature selection, model fitting, hyperparameter tuning, and cutoff definition were restricted to the training cohort. Model performance was evaluated in the locked test cohort using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration, decision curve analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analysis. SHAP analysis was used to describe contributions to model predictions.
RESULTS: A total of 221 patients were included (training cohort, n = 176; internal test cohort, n = 45). Radiomics and deep-learning risk scores were associated with survival outcomes. The integrated model yielded OS C-indices of 0.731 and 0.743 in the training and test cohorts, respectively; the gain over the radiomics model was modest. In the test cohort, AUCs for predicting 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS were 0.658, 0.820, and 0.874, respectively. For PFS, the deep-learning model had a higher test C-inde

candidates.title: [Research Progress of Active Surveillance Strategies, Psychological Distress and Behavioral Decision-making in Patients with Pulmonary Subsolid Nodules].
candidates.journal: Zhongguo fei ai za zhi = Chinese journal of lung cancer
candidates.abstract: With the widespread use of low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) in lung cancer screening, pulmonary subsolid nodules (SSNs) are being detected with increasing frequency. Persistent SSNs have malignant potential, but their natural history varies, with most lesions growing slowly and some remaining stable for prolonged periods. For SSNs with a low risk of progression, early surgical intervention may lead to overtreatment. Therefore, avoiding overtreatment while identifying the lesions with progression risk in a timely manner and determining the appropriate timing of intervention has become an important challenge in the clinical management of SSNs. Based on their imaging characteristics and natural history, active surveillance has gradually become an important management strategy for low-risk SSNs. Active surveillance appears clinically feasible in appropriately selected patients who can adhere to regular follow-up. However, during long-term surveillance, perceived illness uncertainty, risk perception, anxiety, and patient-clinician communication may influence patients' adherence to follow-up and treatment decisions. Patient education, risk communication and psychological support may help alleviate psychological distress and improve patients' understanding of their condition, although direct evidence supporting these interventions in patients undergoing long-term active surveillance for SSNs remains limited. This review summarizes the clinical evidence and implementation strategies for active surveillance of SSNs, and research on patients' psychological changes and behavioral decision-making during surveillance, with the aim of providing insights into individualized long-term management of SSNs. .

candidates.title: [Research Advances in Exhaled Breath Condensate Multi-omics for the Diagnosis and Clinical Translation of Non-small Cell Lung Cancer].
candidates.journal: Zhongguo fei ai za zhi = Chinese journal of lung cancer
candidates.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the predominant histological subtype of lung cancer and it is characterized by high incidence, insidious onset, and poor prognosis. Early diagnosis remains challenging, as low-dose spiral computed tomography (LDCT) screening has a high false-positive rate, highlighting the need for more specific adjunctive diagnostic approaches. As a lung-proximal, non-invasive liquid biopsy, exhaled breath condensate (EBC) can directly reflect alterations in the local airway microenvironment and is increasingly emerging as an important complement to conventional liquid biopsy approaches. In recent years, EBC research has evolved from single-omics biomarker screening toward integrated multi-omics analyses encompassing genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics. Meanwhile, the introduction of technologies such as microfluidics, nanosensing, and artificial intelligence algorithms has helped overcome key challenges associated with the high dilution of EBC samples and the trace abundance of target molecules. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in EBC research, including the standardization of sample collection, multi-omics biomarker discovery, innovations in detection technologies, and clinical translation. Particular emphasis is placed on the clinical value of EBC in the early screening, molecular subtyping, therapeutic response monitoring, and early warning of drug resistance in NSCLC. Current challenges and future directions are also discussed, with the aim of providing a reference for advancing EBC-based multi-omics technologies toward precision diagnosis and treatment in clinical practice. .

candidates.title: Novel risk models based on screening history results and timing of lung cancer diagnosis: Post hoc analysis of the National Lung Cancer Screening Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Our group previously reported that lung cancer (LC) screening history results and subsequent timing of diagnosis are associated with significant differences in survival outcomes. As a follow-up study, we sought to develop novel personalized risk models that considered screening history for incidence cancers, interval LCs, and prevalence LCs.
METHODS: Using data from the CT-arm of the NLST, four independent case-control analyses were conducted to develop parsimonious risk models. Controls (n = 26,038) were those never diagnosed with LC. The four LC case groups were 270 prevalence LCs, 44 interval LCs, 206 screen-detected LCs (SDLCs) that had a baseline positive screen, and 164 SDLCs that had a baseline negative screen. For each case-control analysis, univariable analyses identified statistically significant covariates from 48 variables and then significant covariates were included into a stepwise backward selection approach to identify a model with the most informative covariates. Model discrimination was quantified by the area under the curve (AUC). Internal validation was performed using 500 bootstrap replications in which the entire variable-selection procedure was repeated, yielding optimism-corrected AUCs, and calibration was assessed using calibration slope and calibration-in-the-large. LASSO logistic regression was applied to all 48 covariates as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: For prevalence LCs, the model (AUC = 0.711) included age, pack-years smoked, BMI, smoking status, smoking onset age, personal history of cancer, family history of LC, alcohol consumption, and milling occupation. For interval LCs, the model (AUC = 0.734) included age, smoking status, smoking onset age, cigar smoking, marital status, and asbestos occupation. For baseline positive SDLCs, the model (AUC = 0.685) included age, pack-years smoked, BMI, emphysema, chemicals/plastics exposure, and milling occupation. For baseline negative SDLCs, the model (AUC = 0.701) included age,

candidates.title: Screening for lung cancer with low-dose computed tomography: systematic reviews on effectiveness and patient preferences.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: We synthesized evidence for three questions on screening for lung cancer with computed tomography (CT): benefits (from randomized trials) and harms of screening versus no screening/minimal intervention or alternative screening approaches (e.g., selection criteria, screening intervals); relative importance that informed patients place on the potential benefits and harms of screening (patient preferences); and comparative effects from observational studies of different CT screening selection criteria (using risk prediction models) or nodule classification systems compared with those used in the screening trials.
METHODS: An expert working group provided input on eligibility criteria and potential effect moderators, rated outcomes, and developed decision thresholds for assessing certainty of the evidence and making conclusions. Critical outcomes of screening effects included all-cause mortality, lung-cancer mortality, and overdiagnosis; important outcomes included false positives (FPs), incidental findings, major complications, and psychosocial harms. For patient preferences, we sought data on (i) disutilities of relevant health states, (ii) direct preference-based data, such as outcome trade-offs, and (iii) relative importance of benefits versus harms inferred from attitudes, intentions, and behaviors towards screening among informed patients. For screening benefits and harms and for patient preferences, we searched three databases (MEDLINE, Embase, and Central and MEDLINE, Scopus, and EconLit, respectively) to July 2025. For screening studies published prior to 2015, we relied on other reviews, and for patient preferences our search was limited to 2012 onwards. For comparative effects, we searched MEDLINE and Embase from 2019 to September 2025, relying on other reviews for studies published 2012-2018. Reference lists were scanned and trial registries searched. Two independent reviewers screened titles and abstracts then full texts. Data extraction and analys

candidates.title: Association between A Body Shape Index (ABSI) and lung cancer risk among never-smoking women in Northern China: a population-based prospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal obesity, particularly visceral fat accumulation, increases the risk of lung cancer. As a novel anthropometric metric, A Body Shape Index (ABSI) offers improved quantification of abdominal obesity. This study aimed to investigate the association between ABSI and lung cancer risk among never-smoking women in Northern China.
METHODS: This study included never-smoking women from the Hebei Lung Cancer Screening Cohort (2016-2024). Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used to evaluate the association between ABSI and lung cancer risk and characterize the dose-response relationship. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess the discriminative ability of ABSI. Subgroup analyses were performed to identify high-risk populations and examine potential interaction effects, and sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess the robustness of the results.
RESULTS: A total of 148,395 never-smoking women were included in this study, with 632 incident lung cancer cases diagnosed during the study period. After adjusting for covariates, higher ABSI quartiles were significantly associated with increased lung cancer risk (Q1 as reference; Q3: OR = 1.31, 95% CI: 1.05-1.65; Q4: OR = 1.32, 95% CI: 1.05-1.65; P for trend = 0.004). RCS analysis showed a significant overall association between ABSI and lung cancer risk (P-overall = 0.018), while the test for nonlinearity was not statistically significant (P-nonlinear = 0.054). Subgroup analyses identified a significant interaction by age (P-interaction = 0.001), with a stronger positive association observed among women aged < 60 years (OR = 1.48, 95% CI: 1.05-2.08, P = 0.027). ROC curve analysis demonstrated that ABSI outperformed other conventional anthropometric measures in discriminating lung cancer risk, with the highest area under the curve (AUC) of 0.624 (95% CI: 0.602-0.645, P = 0.032).
CONCLUSION: Elevated ABSI was significantly associated with in

candidates.title: The effect of pulmonary nodule presence on disease severity and course in ANCA-associated vasculitis: a multicenter cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary nodules are common in ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV), but their clinical relevance remains unclear. This study assessed the influence of pulmonary nodules and radiological features on clinical characteristics and outcomes in AAV.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort, clinical features and outcomes were compared between nodule-positive and nodule-negative AAV patients. Pulmonary nodules were classified as cavitary or non-cavitary, and their morphology and regression were evaluated on serial CT scans at diagnosis, 6 months, and last follow-up. Among patients with pulmonary nodules, radiological regression rates were compared according to cavitary and non-cavitary nodule status. Associations between radiological parameters, inflammatory markers, and radiological outcomes were evaluated using correlation analyses.
RESULTS: Among 342 patients, 100 had pulmonary nodules at diagnosis (51 cavitary, 49 non-cavitary). Patients presenting with pulmonary nodules at diagnosis more likely to have lower baseline proteinuria, a higher prevalence of pleural effusion, and an increased risk of pulmonary nodule relapse (p = 0.043, p = 0.022, and p < 0.001, respectively). Radiological regression rates did not differ between cavitary and non-cavitary nodules at 6 months or last control. Moreover, smaller cavitary nodule diameter, a lower necrosis ratio, and fewer cavitary nodules were associated with a higher rate of complete radiological regression at 6 months (p = 0.016, p < 0.001, and p = 0.046, respectively). Larger cavitary nodule diameter and increased wall thickness correlated with elevated CRP levels (p = 0.001, r = 0.452 and p = 0.018, r = 0.340, respectively).
CONCLUSION: In AAV, cavity size and wall thickness were associated with systemic inflammation. A lower necrosis ratio, smaller cavity diameter, and fewer cavitary nodules were associated with favorable radiological outcomes. These exploratory findings require prospective validation usi

candidates.title: Computed tomography lung tumor dataset for deep learning to facilitate medical image segmentation.
candidates.abstract: In-depth analysis of the morphological characteristics of lung tumors in computed tomography (CT) images is crucial for achieving accurate tumor segmentation. While deep learning models based on artificial intelligence have demonstrated excellent segmentation performance, the lack of high-quality training data limits their reliability and applicability in this field. This study constructed a CT image dataset for lung tumor segmentation, comprising 730 cases of early-stage lung cancer and 449 cases of advanced-stage lung cancer. The data were segmented by experienced radiologists and radiation oncologists, and the patient information was anonymized. We proposed a segmentation model based on Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) with adapter fine-tuning and contrast-awareness. The Dice coefficients on the proposed dataset reached 91.64% and 89.51%, respectively, demonstrating the feasibility of training the segmentation model using the constructed dataset. This dataset can be used for the development, comparison, and validation of lung tumor CT image segmentation methods, contributing to the promotion of reproducible research and application exploration in the field of medical image segmentation.

candidates.title: Independent Validation of the LIONS PREY in Patients Undergoing Navigational Bronchoscopy.
candidates.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Accurate malignancy risk prediction of pulmonary lesions is essential in the context of lung cancer screening and early diagnosis. Widely used risk prediction tools, such as the Brock and Herder models, have shown limited performance in high-risk cohorts referred for bronchoscopic evaluation. The LIONS PREY (lung lesion score predicts malignancy) was specifically developed to provide a simple and reliable estimate of malignancy risk in this clinical setting. This study aimed to externally validate the LIONS PREY model and to compare its predictive performance with the Brock and Herder models in patients undergoing index navigational bronchoscopy for pulmonary lesion evaluation.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed patients who underwent index navigational bronchoscopy for peripheral pulmonary lesions between December 2019 and March 2024 at a tertiary academic centre. Malignancy risk was estimated using the LIONS PREY, Brock, and Herder models. Model performance was assessed via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and classification accuracy.
RESULTS: Among 193 evaluable lesions, 134 (69.4%) were histologically confirmed malignant. Malignant lesions were associated with increased growth dynamics (2.7 ± 4.1 mm vs. 1.0 ± 4.3 mm, p < 0.001) and spiculation (56.0% vs. 23.7%, p < 0.001). The LIONS PREY achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.94, outperforming Herder (AUC 0.72; p < 0.001) and Brock (AUC 0.62; p < 0.001) models. Correct classification rates were highest for LIONS PREY (85.0%) versus Herder (70.3%) and Brock (69.1%) (all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The LIONS PREY demonstrated superior predictive accuracy over Brock and Herder in high-risk patients undergoing navigational bronchoscopy, supporting its clinical utility for malignancy risk stratification.

candidates.title: Radiomics- based biomarkers for immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer: advances, challenges, and future perspectives in biological interpretation and clinical translation.
candidates.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet treatment benefit remains heterogeneous and resistance is common. Genomic alterations, tumor microenvironment (TME) remodeling, and metabolic reprogramming across spatial and temporal scales that are incompletely captured by single-site tissue sampling. Radiomics extracts quantitative features from routine images and offers a framework for investigating macroscopic correlates of these processes. This narrative review critically examines computed tomography (CT) and fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT (¹8F-FDG PET/CT) radiomics in relation to oncogenic alterations, immune and stromal phenotypes, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, tumor mutational burden, and metabolic-immune interactions in NSCLC. It should be highlighted that such observed statistical links only generate plausible biological hypotheses and do not constitute experimental proof of true mechanistic relationships. Rather than merely summarizing predictive model performance, we emphasize evidence boundaries and interpretive caveats for radiomic-TME associations. We further elaborate on key translational bottlenecks including limited reproducibility, technical standardization deficits, and retrospective-model overfitting. We discuss ongoing efforts toward cross-scale multi-omics integration, alongside the promises and inherent limitations of explainable artificial intelligence and federated learning for clinical translation. To move beyond purely predictive tools toward mechanism-aware decision-support systems, future radiomic research requires prospective multicenter validation, rigorous data harmonization, and combined analyses integrating spatial transcriptomics, digital pathology, and circulating biomarkers for precision immuno-oncology.

candidates.title: Development and validation of a parsimonious clinical-texture signature for differentiating primary lung cancer from pulmonary metastases on ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT: a retrospective diagnostic study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distinguishing primary lung cancer (PLC) from pulmonary metastases (PM) is a pivotal yet elusive challenge in thoracic oncology, directly dictating surgical strategy from lobectomy to lung-sparing mastectomy. Conventional CT morphology and standard metabolic parameters (SUVmax) frequently lack the specificity required for accurate characterization, particularly in solitary nodules, leading to potential misclassification and treatment delays.
METHODS: We developed and internally validated a machine learning framework integrating ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT radiomics with clinical variables to non-invasively differentiate PLC from PM. In this retrospective study, 161 multimodal features were extracted from 79 pathologically confirmed lesions (30 PLC, 49 PM). A rigorous two-stage feature selection pipeline (Spearman correlation + Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression) identified the most predictive signature. Ten supervised classifiers were trained and evaluated on the held-out internal test set, with comprehensive assessment via AUC, calibration curves, and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: The final parsimonious signature comprised only four features: age and three higher-order texture features (GLSZM), notably excluding conventional SUV metrics which failed to retain predictive value. Logistic Regression achieved superior discrimination (AUC = 0.90), while XGBoost demonstrated optimal calibration (Brier score = 0.119) and the highest net clinical benefit across relevant threshold probabilities. Feature selection consistently improved model stability and interpretability by reducing redundant variables while preserving diagnostic performance across the evaluated machine-learning algorithms.
CONCLUSIONS: This study validates a concise, biologically meaningful radiomics-clinical model that significantly outperforms conventional metabolic metrics in distinguishing PLC from PM. By delivering accurate, well-calibrated predictions, this fr

candidates.title: Lung Cancer and Thoracic Malignancies: Staging and Treatment Response.
candidates.journal: Magnetic resonance imaging clinics of North America
candidates.abstract: This article reviews the clinical role of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/ computed tomography (CT) in lung cancer and selected thoracic malignancies, focusing on staging and treatment response assessment, while emphasizing major interpretation pitfalls. In lung cancer, emphasis is placed on nodal and metastatic staging, evaluation for recurrence, metabolic response criteria, quantitative PET parameters, and treatment-specific imaging considerations. Selected applications in thymic epithelial tumors and malignant pleural mesothelioma are also discussed. Emerging approaches, including somatostatin receptor PET, fibroblast activation protein inhibitor PET, PET/MR imaging, and artificial intelligence-based PET/CT analysis, are briefly summarized.

candidates.title: Development of a diagnostic biomarker panel for early-stage lung adenocarcinoma using serum-derived small RNAs.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Circulating small RNAs, such as microRNAs (miRNAs) and transfer RNA fragments (tRFs), reportedly reflect the physiological and pathological conditions in various diseases. Herein, we aimed to identify circulating small RNAs for the early diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma.
METHODS: This study included 40 healthy controls and 43 patients with lung adenocarcinoma. We analyzed their serum using small RNA sequencing and identified differentially expressed small RNAs between healthy controls and patients with lung adenocarcinoma. We verified the expression profiles of these small RNAs in 29 patients with lung adenocarcinoma and 27 healthy controls. Finally, we evaluated our current results by performing machine learning-based analysis.
RESULTS: The expressions of two mature miRNAs (miR-193a-5p, miR-423-5p), one miRNA isoform (isomiR) (miR-423-5p(21nt)), and two tRFs (tRF-Gly(CCC)(29nt), tRF-Gly(CCC)(30nt)) were significantly elevated in patients with lung adenocarcinoma than in healthy controls. Moreover, the expressions of one miRNA (miR-20a-5p) and five tRFs (tRF-iMet(CAT)(31nt), tRF-Lys(CTT), tRF-iMet(CAT)(30nt), tRF-iMet(CAT)(29nt), tRF-Val(AAC)) were significantly decreased in patients with lung adenocarcinoma than in healthy controls (area under the curve [AUC] values = 0.71 to 0.85, respectively). Furthermore, a combination of six small RNAs (miR-193a-5p, miR-423-5p(21nt), miR-20a-5p, tRF-Gly(CCC)(29nt), tRF-iMet(CAT)(29nt), and tRF-Val(AAC)) was useful for developing a biomarker panel for the early diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. Discovery screening revealed that the panel demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.954 and a specificity of 0.925 (AUC = 0.974), whereas the validation data demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.690 and a specificity of 0.926 (AUC = 0.924).
CONCLUSION: Serum-derived small RNAs are associated with the status of patients with lung adenocarcinoma, and evaluating small RNAs in serum is a promising non-invasive approach for diagnosing lung aden

candidates.title: Advances in Biomarker Discovery for Early Ovarian Cancer Diagnosis.
candidates.abstract: Ovarian cancer is one of the deadliest gynecological cancers worldwide. One promising therapeutic approach is the use of combined biomarkers. The Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA) which combines CA125 with Human Epididymal Protein 4 (HE4) is an example of combining biomarkers to gain an optimal predictive outcome. Tumor Protein p53 (TP53) is a transcription factor with tumor suppressor properties. Mutations in TP53 constitute the most frequent genetic alterations observed in ovarian cancer. In contrast to conventional markers such as CA125, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) provides information about tumor mutations and insights into treatment response. Analysis of ctDNA enables the identification of tumor-associated mutations. Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) also influence cellular processes and act as effectors in oncogenic pathways by binding to RNA or proteins. One effector is Metastasis-Associated Lung Adenocarcinoma Transcript 1 (MALAT1), whose increased expression is associated with an aggressive tumor phenotype. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are crucial in regulating the expression of genes associated with ovarian cancer development and progression. Exosomes carrying various molecules, including miRNAs and lncRNAs, contribute to ovarian cancer progression. Adipocytokines play an important role in the regulation of metabolic and inflammatory processes. Despite their diagnostic potential, the identified biomarkers require further validation.

candidates.title: 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics for differentiating peripheral tuberculosis from lung cancer: development and validation.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a multidimensional radiomics signature utilizing fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT) and machine learning to accurately differentiate peripheral pulmonary tuberculosis from primary peripheral lung cancer.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 346 patients (144 peripheral pulmonary tuberculosis, 202 lung cancer). Radiomic features were extracted from pretreatment PET/CT scans. Patients were randomly split 7:3 into training (n = 242) and internal validation (n = 104) sets. Due to the short 3-year enrollment period with stable protocols, random splitting was the primary validation method. A temporal split (first 70% vs. most recent 30%) was also performed as a sensitivity analysis to assess temporal robustness. Three classifiers (random forest, support vector machine, gradient boosting machine) were compared. The optimal model was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: The final model incorporated six key predictors: age, maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), metabolic heterogeneity index (CV%), PET skewness, PET gray-level co-occurrence matrix energy (PET-GLCM Energy), and shape sphericity. All were identified as independent predictors via multivariate logistic regression (all P < 0.05). The random forest model demonstrated superior and stable performance, achieving an AUC of 0.861 (95% CI: 0.805-0.917) in training and 0.833 (95% CI: 0.732-0.934) in internal validation set. Calibration curves indicated good agreement between predictions and observations. Furthermore, decision curve analysis confirmed the model's clinical net benefit across a wide threshold probability range.
CONCLUSION: A machine learning model based on multidimensional ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT radiomics features was developed and internally validated. This model demonstrates

candidates.title: Prospective field deployment of Swaasa® AI for community-based screening of tuberculosis and other respiratory diseases in Andhra Pradesh: a feasibility and implementation study.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health problem in India. In the state of Andhra Pradesh (AP), the burden of TB is compounded by a shortage of specialists and the lack of scalable, real-time community screening tools. We prospectively implemented Swaasa® AI, a software as a medical device (SaMD) product, in a real-world community healthcare setting and evaluated its feasibility and user experience for TB screening, with the additional capability to identify individuals at potential risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma. Swaasa® uses machine learning (ML) algorithms to analyze acoustic cough patterns and gather information through guided questions about symptoms. Unlike conventional TB screening, which primarily targets symptomatic individuals, Swaasa® supports symptom-agnostic community screening.
METHODS: The platform was deployed in a pilot screening program and integrated into existing healthcare workflows. Trained frontline health workers collected cough recordings using smartphones, and the platform generated automated risk assessments for TB, COPD, and asthma. Over a 6-week deployment, a total of 7,879 individuals from vulnerable populations were screened. Based on risk stratification (Green, Amber, and Red) from Swaasa®, high-risk individuals were referred for confirmatory testing, specifically using nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) for TB and spirometry for COPD and asthma.
RESULTS: Swaasa® AI identified 780 individuals (~10%) at risk of TB and referred them for confirmatory testing. TB was confirmed in 11 of these individuals, yielding an observed TB yield of 1.41% (11/780). Among symptomatic Swaasa®-positive individuals, 7 of 23 were diagnosed with TB, corresponding to an observed yield of 30.4%. Importantly, 36% of the identified TB cases were asymptomatic. In addition to TB, the platform identified that 6.5-9.5% of the population was at risk of COPD and 1.6-1.9% at risk of asthma. Further evaluation

candidates.title: Deep learning model for automatic detection of incidental adrenal abnormalities on low-dose computed tomography images.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the feasibility of employing deep learning models for automated segmentation and classification of adrenal incidental abnormalities on low-dose CT images.
METHODS: Four distinct CT cohorts were retrospectively collected for deep learning models development (cohort A, n = 2574; cohort B, n = 1205), internal evaluation (cohort C, n = 3681), and external evaluation (cohort D, n = 779). Two experienced uroradiologists independently reviewed the CT images and labeled the adrenal glands as normal or abnormal based on predefined criteria encompassing both density and morphological abnormalities, with any discrepancies resolved through consultation. The model development cohorts were divided into a training set, a validation set, and a test set. Deep learning models for segmentation and classification were trained and evaluated on internal and external sets, with the dice similarity coefficient (DSC), area under precision-recall curves (AUPRC), and area under receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROC) as evaluation metrics. Adrenal descriptions from radiology reports were extracted to compare with the model's performance.
RESULTS: For adrenal gland segmentation, the DSC values for the test set, internal validation cohort, and external validation cohort were 0.839 (IQR: 0.783-0.871), 0.870 (IQR: 0.819-0.902), and 0.799 (IQR: 0.729-0.849), respectively. For adrenal gland classification, the AI model achieved AUPRC values of 0.913, 0.753, and 0.927 in the test set, internal validation cohort, and external validation cohort, respectively, outperforming routine radiology reporting (AUPRC: 0.809, 0.708, 0.591; all P < 0.05). Corresponding AUROC values were 0.956, 0.942, and 0.977 for the AI model, which also outperformed routine radiology reporting (AUROC: 0.889, 0.705, 0.551; all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The deep learning models showed promise in automated adrenal segmentation and classification, highlighting AI's potential to improve detection of

candidates.title: Smoking Cessation Assistance and Lung Cancer Screening Among Latino Patients Following Medicaid Eligibility Amendment to Adults Aged 50 and Older Regardless of Immigration Status.
candidates.journal: Journal of primary care & community health
candidates.abstract: ObjectivesThis study assesses whether expanding Medicaid eligibility to low-income adults aged 50 and older regardless of immigration status improved the prevalence of smoking cessation assistance and lung cancer screening among Latino patients receiving care at community clinics.MethodsThis retrospective study used electronic health record data from clinics in Oregon and California who expanded Medicaid eligibility by 2021. Data included 1,741 Latino and non-Hispanic white patients aged 50-64 uninsured at baseline who were documented as current or former smokers and had visits both pre-amendment (2018-2019) and post-amendment (2021-2023).ResultsFew patients received lung cancer screening during the study period (4% of n=1,242). There was no significant difference in the prevalence of lung cancer screening between groups from pre-to-post period (ATT=-2.29; 95%CI: -4.90, 0.33). Latinos (9.5%) had lower prevalence of smoking cessation assistance than the non-Hispanic White group (16.2%) in the pre-period. There was no significant group difference from pre-to-post eligibility expansion (ATT=-4.92; 95%CI: -11.21, 2.57).ConclusionsMedicaid eligibility expansion regardless of immigration status was not associated with improved up-to-date lung cancer screening or receipt of smoking cessation assistance in Latino patients. Insurance access is not sufficient to improve lung cancer screening uptake and facilitate smoking cessation.

candidates.title: Integrated transcriptomic and clinical prediction model for malignant pulmonary nodules: Model development, external dataset evaluation, and single-center expression validation.
candidates.abstract: Discriminating between benign and malignant pulmonary nodules remains a clinical challenge, complicating treatment decisions. This study developed a predictive model integrating transcriptomic and clinical data to characterize pulmonary nodules. Gene expression profiles and clinical data from GSE108375 were analyzed. Differential expression and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were performed. Patients were randomly split into training and validation sets (7:3). The model was further evaluated using an external dataset (GSE225787), and candidate gene expression was examined in a single-center clinical cohort (n = 30) using blood reverse‑transcription quantitative real‑time PCR and nodule-tissue immunohistochemistry (IHC). WGCNA identified the MEgreen module as significantly associated with malignant nodules. Among 776 differentially expressed genes between malignant and benign nodules, 36 overlapped with the MEgreen module. Last absolute shrinkage and selection operator selected age, lesion size, and 5 genes (RBX1, GZMK, AKR1C3, NDUFA4, CELA1) for model construction. The model achieved AUCs of 85.16% in the training set and 80.23% in the internal validation set, with an AUC of 0.867 in the external dataset. In the single-center clinical cohort, blood CELA1 and NDUFA4 mRNA levels were significantly higher in the malignant group, and tissue IHC measurements of the corresponding proteins also differed significantly between groups. The integrated transcriptomic and clinical model showed potential for estimating malignancy risk in pulmonary nodules. The expression findings for CELA1 and NDUFA4 support further investigation of these candidate markers in larger clinical cohorts.

candidates.title: LDCT Screening Cost-Effectiveness for Familial Lung Cancer Risk in Taiwan.
candidates.journal: The American journal of managed care
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Most economic evaluations of low-dose CT (LDCT) screening focus on heavy smokers, with limited evidence for individuals with a family history of lung cancer (LCFH). This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of LDCT screening for individuals with LCFH using Taiwan epidemiologic data and cost data derived from the Taiwan National Health Insurance program.
STUDY DESIGN: A Markov model simulation evaluated the cost-effectiveness of LDCT screening vs nonscreening using 10,000 iterations in the probabilistic sensitivity analysis, a 1-year cycle, a 20-year time horizon, and a 3% annual discount rate.
METHODS: The analysis adopted the perspective of the Taiwan health care payer and assumed annual LDCT screening with full adherence. The willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was set at $32,440, corresponding to Taiwan's 2024 gross domestic product per capita. We used incremental costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) to calculate the incremental cost-utility ratio (ICUR). Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate parameter uncertainty.
RESULTS: At the specified WTP threshold, LDCT screening yielded an ICUR of $23,786/QALYs, which was below the prespecified WTP threshold. In the simulated cohort, 158,375 LDCT examinations resulted in 609 lung cancer diagnoses over 20 years. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis demonstrated a 61.22% probability of cost-effectiveness. Results were most sensitive to lung cancer incidence in the nonscreening cohort, LDCT positivity rate, and positive predictive value.
CONCLUSIONS: LDCT screening for individuals with LCFH was cost-effective at the selected threshold under modeled assumptions. Targeted implementation in high-risk populations may enhance value-based resource allocation; however, real-world adherence, evolving treatment costs, and program scalability should be considered in coverage and reimbursement decisions.

candidates.title: Low-Dose CT Lung-RADS 2022 for the Management of Screening- and Non-Screening-detected Lung Cancer Associated with Cystic Airspaces.
candidates.abstract: Background Lung cancer associated with cystic airspaces (CA) can be misinterpreted as a benign lesion, leading to missed or delayed diagnosis; however, the effect of the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) 2022 criteria remains unverified. Purpose To retrospectively determine the frequency and outcomes of lung cancer associated with CA during screening and explore the potential effect of Lung-RADS 2022 on earlier diagnosis. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis included participants with lung cancers from three trials: the National Lung Screening Trial (2002-2007); Italian Lung Cancer Screening Trial, or ITALUNG (2004-2010); and German Lung Cancer Screening Intervention trial, or LUSI (2007-2016). Two radiologists jointly reviewed low-dose CT images to identify and morphologically characterize lung cancer associated with CA. Associations with histologic features, stage, and other variables were assessed. Lung cancer-specific survival was analyzed using Fine-Gray regression accounting for the competing risk of non-lung cancer death. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, stage, detection status, and trial. Lung-RADS 2022 criteria for atypical pulmonary cysts were applied. Results Seventy-three cancers associated with CA were identified in 1258 participants (median age, 64 years [IQR, 61-69 years]; 43 male), including 44 of 716 (6.1%) screening-detected and 29 of 542 (5.4%) non-screening-detected cancers. Multilocular morphologic type was associated with a more advanced stage than unilocular morphologic type (12 of 24 vs 15 of 49; P = .02). The 5-year lung cancer-specific survival was 51.4% (95% CI: 39.3, 62.3) for cancers associated with CA and 53.2% (95% CI: 50.1, 56.2) for 1054 participants with noncystic non-small cell lung cancer. No evidence of a difference in survival was observed (subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.15 [95% CI: 0.81, 1.63]; P = .44), and results remained consistent in multivariable models. candidates.title: EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma featuring massive bronchorrhea, a dominant pulmonary nodule, and migratory ground-glass opacities: a case report and literature review.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer exhibits profound clinical, radiological, and biological heterogeneity, which poses significant challenges for early recognition and timely diagnosis in select atypical cases. Among rare manifestations, massive bronchorrhea caused by EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma with radiological findings of a dominant pulmonary nodule and migratory ground-glass opacities (GGOs) remains extremely uncommon.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 67-year-old male patient presented with massive bronchorrhea and progressive dyspnea. Serial chest computed tomography (CT) scans revealed bilateral migratory GGOs and a small nodular lesion in the basal segment of the right lower lobe. Empiric antibiotic therapy and subsequent systemic corticosteroid treatment failed to alleviate his respiratory symptoms. Ultimately, markedly elevated sputum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels, combined with pathological results from transbronchial biopsy of the right lung nodule, confirmed a diagnosis of EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma. Treatment with osimertinib achieved rapid resolution of bronchorrhea, accompanied by complete regression of the pulmonary nodule and GGOs during clinical follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for lung adenocarcinoma in patients with persistent unexplained bronchorrhea. For patients harboring EGFR-sensitive mutations, EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) remain the first-line treatment, yielding favorable therapeutic effects on bronchorrhea control and improving survival outcomes.

candidates.title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based combined model for malignancy risk prediction in pulmonary subsolid nodules: a dual-center study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate characterization of pulmonary subsolid nodules (SSNs) is important for selecting surveillance, biopsy, or surgery. Existing clinical models were developed in broader nodule populations and may not fully reflect the radiological and biological features of SSNs.
METHODS: This dual-center retrospective study included 225 patients with pathologically confirmed SSNs from January 2018 to January 2024. The development center contributed 167 patients, split into internal training (n = 118) and internal validation (n = 49) cohorts, and the external center contributed 58 patients. Ten machine-learning algorithms were compared within the development cohort. The final combined model used four routinely available predictors: spiculation, consolidation-to-tumor ratio (CTR), CYFRA 21 - 1, and nodule diameter. Discrimination, calibration, decision-curve analysis, pairwise model comparison, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: The combined model achieved AUCs of 0.932 (95% CI, 0.887-0.977), 0.954 (95% CI, 0.895-1.000), and 0.930 (95% CI, 0.864-0.995) in the internal training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. In external validation, the corresponding AUCs for the Mayo, VA, Brock, and PKUPH models were 0.750, 0.560, 0.800, and 0.840. Calibration was evaluated in all three cohorts, and decision-curve analysis showed net benefit across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.12-0.68 in external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: A four-variable combined model integrating imaging features and CYFRA 21 - 1 showed consistent discrimination across the internal and external validation cohorts. The web calculator may support research-stage risk estimation, but prospective multicenter validation is needed before clinical implementation.

candidates.title: Active tuberculosis screening incorporated with AI-assisted chest X-ray among the elderly in community settings, a cross-sectional study in China.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults face an elevated risk of tuberculosis (TB), yet they frequently present with atypical or asymptomatic clinical features, leading to major diagnostic delays. This study evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and epidemiological insights of a novel "double X plus AI" active case-finding (ACF) strategy embedded within the routine annual health check-up program for community-dwelling elderly.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted across 14 communities in Jiangsu Province. Local residents aged ≥ 65 years received symptom screening and digital chest X-ray for tuberculosis by annual health examination. Chest X-rays were triaged using a convolutional neural network-based artificial intelligence (AI) system. Participants with tuberculosis-related symptoms or AI-suspected chest X-ray findings provided sputum specimens for molecular analysis using an 8:1 pooling strategy via the Xpert® MTB/RIF Ultra assay. Positive pools were subsequently disaggregated for individual testing.
RESULTS: A total of 14,312 older adults were enrolled, among whom 2,436 presumptive tuberculosis patients were identified, comprising 2,309 AI-suspected individuals and 127 symptomatic individuals with normal chest X-rays. Among the 2,309 AI-suspected individuals, 76 failed to provide qualified sputum specimens. A total of 20 active pulmonary TB cases were disclosed, including 16 microbiological positive and 4 clinical diagnosed tuberculosis patients. The overall age and sex standardized prevalence of pulmonary tuberculosis identified through this active screening strategy was 154.5 per 100,000, which was higher than the registered prevalence among older adults in Jiangsu Province in 2025 derived from passive surveillance (48.9/100,000; P < 0.001). Notably, all the twenty confirmed patients were originated from the AI-suspected group, while none of the symptomatic individuals with normal X-rays were diagnosed with tuberculosis.
