candidates.title: Simultaneous Occurrence of Berlin Nodule and Optic Disc Granuloma: A Rare Case Report.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe a rare case of sarcoidosis presenting with simultaneous anterior segment granuloma (Berlin nodule) and posterior (optic nerve head) granuloma.
METHODS: A 40-year-old male presented with a four-year history of persistent glare in the right eye. Detailed ocular examination, gonioscopy, ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM), spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), laboratory evaluation, chest computed tomography (CT), endobronchial lymph node biopsy, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain and orbits were performed.
RESULTS: The right eye revealed mild granulomatous anterior uveitis, a yellowish-white iris nodule at 6 o'clock, mild vitritis, optic disc granuloma obscuring the cup, and peripheral vitreous snowballs. The left eye showed mild anterior uveitis with peripheral vitreous snowballs. UBM confirmed the Berlin nodule as a hyporeflective trabecular lesion, and SD-OCT demonstrated increased temporal peripapillary thickness. Gonioscopy documented localized angle involvement without significant synechial closure. Laboratory investigations revealed elevated serum angiotensin-converting enzyme, with negative Mantoux and Quantiferon-TB Gold tests. CT chest demonstrated bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with ground-glass opacities, and endobronchial biopsy confirmed non-caseating granulomatous lymphadenitis, establishing systemic sarcoidosis. MRIs of the brain and orbits were normal, excluding neurosarcoidosis. The patient was treated with oral and topical corticosteroids, resulting in complete regression of both granulomas.
DISCUSSION: This case expands the clinical spectrum of ocular sarcoidosis by demonstrating the exceptionally rare coexistence of a Berlin nodule and an optic nerve head granuloma. Recognition of these highly specific granulomatous lesions, supported by multimodal imaging and systemic evaluation, facilitated prompt diagnosis, avoided unnecessary invasive intervention, and resulted in complete resolution with cortic

candidates.title: EGFR mutation prediction in NSCLC from CT images via self-supervised disentangled feature learning and multimodal fusion.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT)-based noninvasive prediction of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation status in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is highly important for advancing precision diagnosis and treatment. Current detection methods that rely on invasive tissue biopsies present several limitations. This study aimed to develop a model that integrated deep learning and multimodal information for the noninvasive prediction of EGFR-sensitizing mutations (exon 19 deletion and L858R point mutation) in NSCLC patients using contrast-enhanced CT (CE-CT) images.
METHODS: We retrospectively included 466 pathologically confirmed NSCLC patients from two centers (413 from our own center for model development and internal validation, and 53 from another center for independent external validation), and proposed a novel paradigm combining disentangled self-supervised learning (D-SSL) with multimodal gated fusion. The D-SSL encoder was pretrained on CT images and tumor ROI masks from the entire 413-patient internal cohort without using EGFR mutation labels and was subsequently fixed for downstream classification. An adaptive gated fusion network was subsequently constructed to dynamically integrate these deep features with traditional radiomics features and clinical information to predict the EGFR-sensitizing mutation status.
RESULTS: In 20 repeated random splits, the D-SSL fusion models achieved mean AUCs of 0.800 (±0.052) and 0.794 (±0.048) on the training set and internal test set, respectively. One-way ANOVA and subsequent Tukey HSD post-hoc test revealed that the performance on the internal test set of the D-SSL fusion models was significantly superior to that of the clinical models, radiomics models, and radiomics-clinical fusion models (all p < 0.001). On the fully independent external validation set, which was not involved in D-SSL pretraining or downstream model development, the D-SSL fusion models maintained robust performance with a mean AUC of 0.6

candidates.title: 18F-FDG PET/CT Habitat Radiomics for Predicting Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Mutation Status in Locally Advanced Non-small Cell Lung Cancer: A Multicenter Study.
candidates.abstract: IntroductionAccurate identification of epidermal growth factor receptor mutation status is essential for treatment planning in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer, but tissue testing may be limited by specimen availability and sampling. We developed and externally validated a fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography habitat radiomics model to estimate mutation probability as an adjunct to molecular testing.MethodsThis retrospective multicenter study included 313 patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer who underwent imaging and tissue-based mutation testing. Center A provided the training cohort (n = 142) and internal validation cohort (n = 61), and Center B provided the external validation cohort (n = 110). Separate Otsu thresholds were applied to positron emission tomography and computed tomography intensities within each segmented tumor. Voxel-wise intersection generated four mutually exclusive habitats. Habitat features were selected in the training cohort and evaluated with six classifiers. Additional analyses examined adenocarcinoma-restricted performance, alternative partitioning, segmentation reproducibility, calibration, decision-curve performance, and selection bias.ResultsThe training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts included 69/73, 31/30, and 64/46 mutation-positive/mutation-negative tumors, respectively. The support vector machine habitat model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.911 (95% confidence interval, 0.869-0.948), 0.898 (0.819-0.967), and 0.884 (0.829-0.933), respectively. With the threshold selected only in the training cohort, external validation sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and negative predictive value were 0.750, 0.739, 0.745, and 0.680. The combined model achieved an external validation area under the curve of 0.904 (0.855-0.949).ConclusionHabitat radiomics showed promising discrimination across two centers, includ

candidates.title: Malignancy yield after resection of incidentally detected solid solitary pulmonary nodules according to lung cancer screening eligibility.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Solid solitary pulmonary nodules (SPNs) detected incidentally may represent a primary pulmonary malignancy, metastatic disease, or benign pathology, and accurate preoperative differentiation remains challenging. The study assessed malignancy yield after surgical resection based on retrospectively determined lung cancer screening eligibility and identified factors associated with malignant pathology in a predefined high-risk surgical cohort.
METHODS: The retrospective single-center study included adults who underwent lung resection for incidentally detected solid SPNs measuring 8-30 mm with no preoperative tissue diagnosis or previous lung cancer between January 2016 and January 2026. The cohort consisted of patients who either fulfilled the study-specific lung cancer screening definition (age and smoking history) or had a first-degree family history of cancer or previous extrathoracic malignancy. Malignancy yield was compared between screening-eligible and non-eligible patients. Factors associated with malignant pathology were explored using multivariable logistic regression. A sensitivity analysis excluding pulmonary metastases evaluated associations with primary pulmonary malignancy.
RESULTS: Among 112 patients, 78 cases (69.6%) had malignant pathology and 34 (30.4%) had benign lesions. Malignant nodules consisted of 58 primary pulmonary malignancies and 20 pulmonary metastases. Seventy-four patients met the screening eligibility criteria, having a higher malignancy yield than non-eligible patients (81.1% vs. 47.4%; P < 0.001). The initial multivariable analysis demonstrated that male sex and previous extrathoracic malignancy were independently associated with malignancy. Increasing age, male sex, and previous extrathoracic malignancy remained associated with primary pulmonary malignancy after exclusion of pulmonary metastases.
CONCLUSIONS: Screening eligibility was associated with higher malignancy yield among patients who had already undergone multid

candidates.title: Tricuspid Valve Vegetations: Diagnosis, Implications, and Management.
candidates.journal: Techniques in vascular and interventional radiology
candidates.abstract: Right-sided infective endocarditis (RSIE) and associated tricuspid vegetations pose treatment challenges due to intercurrent shock, pulmonary embolism, tricuspid regurgitation, and risk of stroke from paradoxical emboli. As rates of intravenous drug use and chronic indwelling intracardiac devices increase, so do rates of RSIE. This condition is associated with significant healthcare costs, prolonged hospitalization, and an increased incidence of multidrug resistant organisms. Percutaneous mechanical aspiration (PMA) of tricuspid vegetations provides a cost-effective and relatively safe method for debulking tricuspid vegetations in patients who are not stable for more invasive therapies, or in which valve replacement is contraindicated. PMA may improve efficacy of antibiotic treatment, reduce severity of embolization and valvular damage, and delay or avoid valve replacement. PMA is associated with high procedural success rates, and relatively low risk of periprocedural clinical deterioration. Still, device selection and periprocedural support are critical to ensure successful treatment. Intra-procedural transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE), and/or intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) is critical for viewing tricuspid vegetations, assessing valvular function after aspiration, and positioning aspiration devices appropriately. Several devices-AngioVac, AlphaVac (both Angiodynamics Inc, Latham, NY), FlowTriever (Inari Medical, Irvine, CA), and Lighting/FLASH systems (Penumbra Inc, Alameda, CA)-are available for off-label use for PMA with documented successful debulking of tricuspid vegetations. These studies demonstrate shortened hospital stays and improved outcomes compared to traditional therapies. This review details periprocedural considerations, procedure steps, and expected clinical outcomes of PMA of tricuspid vegetations.

candidates.title: Current Status of Fetal Cardiac Care in Germany from a Pediatric Cardiology Perspective: A Consensus Statement on Behalf of the Fetal Cardiology Working Group of the German Society of Pediatric Cardiology.
candidates.abstract: Fetal cardiology has become an important subspecialty in Pediatric Cardiology. It includes prenatal detection of congenital heart defects and arrhythmia as well as prenatal therapeutic procedures, planning of perinatal management, and the important part of parental counseling. Currently available methods to diagnose congenital heart disease prenatally, major requirements for parental counseling, available prenatal treatment options, and perinatal care of fetuses and newborns are outlined. A risk-stratified level of care classification system is proposed. This consensus statement of the Fetal Cardiology Working Group of the German Society of Pediatric Cardiology gives an overview about the current status of fetal cardiology in Germany from a Pediatric Cardiology perspective emphasizing that detection rates in Germany stay behind in international comparison due to the minimal requirement of displaying a 4-chamber-view only in screening guidelines according to the "Mutterschaftsrichtlinie." We require mandatory views of the outflow tracts and the 3-vessel-trachea view in the 19 to 22 weeks' examination.

candidates.title: Predicting rapid progression of non-target lesions after PCI using machine learning combining coronary CTA plaque features and clinical inflammatory markers.
candidates.abstract: This study investigates the value of a machine learning method combining coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA plaque features and clinical inflammatory markers for predicting rapid progression of non-target lesions after Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI). A total of 331 post-PCI patients were retrospectively enrolled and divided into rapid progression (n = 78) and non-rapid progression (n = 253) groups based on follow-up CTA. Baseline clinical data, inflammatory markers (hs-CRP, IL-6, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio), and CTA plaque features (low-attenuation plaque, positive remodeling, noncalcified plaque volume) were collected. Patients were randomly split 7:3 into training and validation sets. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression identified predictors. Logistic regression, inflammation-only, CTA-only, and multimodal fusion models were developed and compared. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression selected 8 independent predictors: hs-CRP, IL-6, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, low-attenuation plaque, positive remodeling, noncalcified plaque volume, napkin-ring sign, and diabetes history. In the validation set, the multimodal fusion model achieved an area under the curve of 0.89 (95%CI: 0.83-0.95), outperforming the inflammation-only (0.78), CTA-only (0.83), and Logistic regression (0.72) models (all P < .05). Its accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity were 92.9%, 95.2%, and 92.3%, respectively. The fusion model showed excellent calibration (HL P = .58), the highest net benefit across threshold probabilities of 8% to 35%, and stable performance across subgroups (area under the curve 0.86-0.92). The multimodal fusion machine learning model effectively predicts rapid progression of non-target lesions after PCI, outperforming single-modality models and supporting risk stratification and individualized secondary prevention.

candidates.title: Observed pathogen- and species-specific proportions of diagnosed infective endocarditis among bloodstream infection cases: A 10-year retrospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract: Infective endocarditis (IE) remains associated with high mortality despite advances in diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. The observed proportion of diagnosed IE among bloodstream infection (BSI) cases may vary according to the causative pathogen; however, pathogen- and species-specific data remain limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 5816 cases of true BSI at a tertiary care hospital in Japan between April 2015 and March 2025. Eighty cases were diagnosed with definite IE according to the modified Duke criteria. Echocardiography was performed according to clinical judgment and was not systematically mandated for all BSI cases. Pathogen- and species-specific observed proportions of diagnosed IE and factors associated with in-hospital mortality were evaluated. The overall in-hospital mortality was 17.5% and was higher among cases with Staphylococcus aureus IE (39.1%). In an exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression analysis adjusted for age only, S. aureus infection was associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratios, 5.697; 95% CI, 1.635-19.850), although the estimate was imprecise. The observed proportion of diagnosed IE varied according to pathogen and species. Among streptococci, relatively high proportions were observed for Streptococcus mitis (23.5%, 4/17; 95% confidence intervals (CI), 6.8-49.9), Streptococcus oralis (23.5%, 4/17; 95% CI, 6.8-49.9), and Streptococcus gallolyticus (22.2%, 4/18; 95% CI, 6.4-47.6). The observed proportions were 3.7% for S. aureus and 6.4% for Enterococcus faecalis. The observed proportion of diagnosed IE differed according to the causative pathogen and species. Despite the relatively low observed proportion of diagnosed IE in S. aureus bacteremia, in-hospital mortality among cases with S. aureus IE was high. Because echocardiography was not systematically performed, these estimates may underestimate the underlying frequency of IE. These findings should be considered descriptive and hyp

candidates.title: Maternally inherited PRKAR1A pathogenic variant causing Carney complex with a concomitant LDLR variant resulting in hyperlipidemia: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carney complex (CNC) is an autosomal dominant multisystem tumor syndrome predominantly caused by pathogenic PRKAR1A mutations. Cardiac myxoma, multiple endocrine neoplasms and cutaneous pigmented lesions are its typical clinical manifestations. We report an extremely uncommon case of CNC caused by a PRKAR1A pathogenic variant, with a LDLR variant leading to familial hyperlipidemia and marked phenotypic heterogeneity within the family.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 45-year-old male presented with palpitations was admitted to our hospital. The patient's past medical history included cerebral infarction, myocardial infarction, right monocular blindness, and atrial myxoma. Physical examination revealed typical acromegalic facies, accompanied by markedly elevated serum growth hormone (GH) levels. Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) further identified a pituitary neuroendocrine tumor. Transthoracic echocardiography and contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) demonstrated global cardiac chamber enlargement and ventricular hypertrophy. Coronary CTA revealed diffuse dilatation of the coronary artery. Genetic testing confirmed two maternally inherited pathogenic variants: the splice-donor variant PRKAR1A c.769 + 1G>A responsible for CNC, and LDLR c.1879G>A, which causes familial hypercholesterolemia. One month after discharge from our hospital, the patient received transnasal transsphenoidal resection of sellar pituitary lesion under general anesthesia at the Department of Neurosurgery in another general hospital. Preoperative GH and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) were elevated on repeat testing, and both decreased significantly postoperatively. The sellar lesion was confirmed as a plurihormonal pituitary neuroendocrine tumor of pituitary transcription factor 1 (PIT-1) lineage; immunohistochemistry showed weak GH expression, focal prolactin (PRL) and luteinizing hormone (LH) expression, negative adrenocorticotro

candidates.title: Prevalence of Diastolic Dysfunction Among COPD Patients-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Given the similarity of risk factors and pathophysiological mechanisms, suspecting HFpEF in COPD is challenging because of overlapping clinical features. Echocardiographic assessment of diastolic dysfunction (DD) may help identify patients with abnormal left ventricular filling who warrant further cardiac evaluation, although DD is not equivalent to a clinical diagnosis of HFpEF. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate the pooled prevalence of DD among patients with COPD.
METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to February 5, 2026. Studies reporting the prevalence of DD in COPD using any echocardiographic criteria were included. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed using restricted maximum-likelihood estimation. Heterogeneity was assessed with Cochran's Q, I2, and τ2. Subgroup, sensitivity, and meta-regression analyses were conducted. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale, and the certainty of the evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Forty-eight studies comprising 6845 patients were included. The pooled prevalence of echocardiographic findings consistent with DD was 47% (95% CI: 39%-56%), with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 95.5%; 95% prediction interval, 7%-91%). Prevalence increased across GOLD stages, from 30% (95% CI: 16%-50%) in Stage I to 38% (22%-57%) in Stage II, 58% (39%-75%) in Stage III and 72% (56%-84%) in Stage IV. These stage-specific estimates were interpreted descriptively because several studies contributed data to multiple stages. Sensitivity analyses yielded pooled prevalences of 54% after excluding low-quality studies and 62% after excluding studies with fewer than 50 participants. Multivariable meta-regression explained only a modest proportion of between-study variance. No statistically significant asymmetry was detected by Egger's test, although its interpretation for prevalence outcomes is limited.

candidates.title: Bicuspidization of a severely dysplastic aortic valve in a neonate.
candidates.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
candidates.abstract: Severe congenital aortic valve stenosis in neonates remains a challenging lesion requiring individualized treatment. While balloon aortic valvuloplasty and surgical valvotomy are established treatment options, neonates with severely dysplastic valve morphology may benefit from anatomical valve reconstruction in addition to relief of obstruction. This video tutorial demonstrates our technique of bicuspidization of a severely dysplastic neonatal aortic valve by commissural reconstruction, extensive leaflet shaving and limited free-edge remodelling. Our ultimate goal of tricuspid valve repair was impossible in this scenario.

candidates.title: Type 3 aortopulmonary window: surgical repair technique.
candidates.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
candidates.abstract: A 2-week-old, 3.5 kg neonate presented with congestive heart failure and a cardiac murmur. Echocardiography demonstrated a large type III aortopulmonary window associated with a large secundum atrial septal defect. Biventricular systolic function was normal, the pulmonary valve was competent, and both branch pulmonary arteries were well formed. No coronary artery anomalies were identified. Through a median sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass was established with aortic and bicaval cannulation, and the branch pulmonary arteries were controlled. Following aortic cross-clamping and cardioplegic arrest, the window was exposed, allowing direct visualization of the defect margins, coronary artery origins, branch pulmonary arteries and pulmonary valve. The aortopulmonary septum was reconstructed with a bovine pericardial patch, preserving branch pulmonary artery alignment and avoiding distortion or obstruction. The atrial septal defect was partially closed, leaving an approximately 4 mm fenestration. The patient was weaned from cardiopulmonary bypass. Cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic cross-clamp times were 67 and 49 minutes, respectively, and total operative time was 3 hours. Long-term follow-up was unavailable. This case illustrates patch repair of a large type III aortopulmonary window under direct visualization of adjacent structures, with attention to preserving great vessel geometry and branch pulmonary artery. Long-term outcomes could not be assessed because follow-up data were unavailable.

candidates.title: Predictive Value of Serum Fibrinogen-to-Albumin Ratio in Young Patients With Coronary Heart Disease and its Correlation With Coronary Lesion Severity.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Predictive value of Fibrinogen-to-Albumin Ratio (FAR) in young patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) and its correlation with the severity of coronary artery lesions.
METHODS: We enrolled 472 young patients hospitalized at our hospital from August 2013 to August 2024 who underwent coronary angiography (CAG) and divided into a CHD group (n = 212) and a non-CHD group (n = 260) based on CAG results. Univariate analysis was conducted on all variables. Subsequently, Lasso regression analysis (LASSO) and bidirectional stepwise logistic regression were used to identify the independent risk factors to construct a prediction model. ROC, calibration, and clinical decision curves evaluated model performance. CHD patients were grouped by Gensini tertiles to compare FAR differences, and ROC curve analyzed FAR's predictive value for moderate-to-severe stenosis.
RESULT: Univariate analysis showed statistically significant differences in multiple indicators including FAR (p < 0.05). Finally, seven indicators including FAR were included to establish the model. The results of ROC curve analysis showed that FAR and joint mode had predictive value for CHD (p＜0.05), The AUC of FAR was 0.643, and that of the combined model was 0.847. FAR was positively correlated with Gensini score (rs = 0.215, p < 0.001). FAR was positively correlated with the Gensini score (rs = 0.215, p < 0.001), showed an upward trend with increasing lesion severity (p = 0.046), and yielded an AUC of 0.596 for predicting moderate-to-severe stenosis (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: FAR and the prediction model have predictive value for CHD in young adults; FAR has limited predictive performance for the severity of coronary artery lesions and can serve as an auxiliary reference indicator.

candidates.title: Cardiorenal biomarker‑enhanced model for left ventricular hypertrophy in non-dialysis chronic kidney disease.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) acts as a key factor for determinant of adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Echocardiography is the standard method for LVH assessment. Yet asymptomatic LVH patients are often overlooked or missed in routine screening. Whether a biomarker-enhanced model improves detection of prevalent LVH in non-dialysis CKD remains unclear.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 647 non-dialysis patients with CKD. We developed a clinical model based on female, age, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, estimated glomerular filtration rate, and serum phosphorus. Cardiorenal biomarkers, including urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2), were then added to assess their incremental value. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: LVH was present in 131 patients (20.2%). In multivariable analysis, female, hypertension, serum phosphorus, UACR, and sST2 were independently associated with LVH. NT‑proBNP was associated with LVH in univariable but not multivariable analysis. The clinical model had an AUC of 0.789. Adding three biomarkers improved the AUC to 0.812 (95% CI, 0.769-0.856), with lower Brier score and AIC. Bootstrap internal validation showed an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.790 and Brier score of 0.129. Decision curve analysis suggested higher net benefit for the biomarker-enhanced model across most threshold probabilities.
CONCLUSIONS: A biomarker-enhanced model incorporating UACR, NT-proBNP, and sST2, have potential clinical applications to help prioritize echocardiography referrals for asymptomatic CKD patients who may have prevalent LVH.

candidates.title: Neck-to-height ratio is positively associated with left ventricular mass index in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between fat distribution, specifically visceral adipose tissue and subcutaneous fat, and the parameters of left ventricular structure has shown inconsistent findings. Interestingly, the role of neck circumference, a surrogate for upper-body subcutaneous fat, in these parameters is less explored. This research seeks to evaluate the neck-to-height ratio (NHR) as a potential phenotypic indicator for cardiac structure evaluation in type 2 diabetes patients. It particularly focuses on examining how the NHR correlates with parameters of the left ventricular structure.
METHODS: This observational study encompassed 1074 individuals diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, who were evaluated or treated at the Second Affiliated Hospital of the School of Medicine, Zhejiang University, from January 1, 2019, to December 31, 2020. The participants were categorized into three cohorts according to their NHR levels. Statistical analysis of normally distributed data involved one-way ANOVA, whereas the Kruskal-Wallis test was applied for data not following normal distribution. Further, multivariate linear regression analysis was utilized to explore correlations between NHR and the left ventricular mass index (LVMI). Additionally, subgroup analyses and interaction tests were conducted to further investigate these relationships.
RESULTS: Analysis indicated the association between NHR and various parameters of left ventricular structure. Through multivariate linear regression, a significant positive correlation emerged between NHR and LVMI (LV mass/height².⁷) (β = 39.95, P = 0.003), further regression analysis, adjusting for potential confounders, confirmed a consistent positive trend between NHR and LVMI (P for trend = 0.004). Extensive subgroup analysis demonstrated that age, gender, and varying criteria for obesity assessment did not significantly alter the observed correlation between NHR and LVMI.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of Chinese patients with T2DM, a notab

candidates.title: Cardiorespiratory fitness gap during stable recovery after percutaneous coronary intervention relative to a contemporaneous angiographic reference group: a propensity score overlap-weighted cross-sectional study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) relieves epicardial coronary stenosis, but anatomical treatment does not necessarily indicate recovery of integrated exercise function. We examined whether patients during stable recovery after PCI had lower measured cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) than a contemporaneous angiographic reference group and how much body composition and common clinical and metabolic factors accounted for the difference.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study included 682 patients who underwent coronary angiography, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), and bioelectrical-impedance assessment: 209 in the reference group and 473 in the PCI group. Both groups completed the study assessments 4-6 weeks after the corresponding coronary angiography or planned PCI. Propensity score overlap weighting was used to compare absolute peak oxygen uptake (VO₂peak), body weight-normalized VO₂peak, and percent-predicted VO₂peak (pVO₂). Skeletal muscle mass and body fat mass or their height-indexed measures were aligned with the scale of each outcome. Robustness was assessed using an extended clinical model, cross-fitted reference-group mapping, and sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: The six propensity-score covariates were balanced after overlap weighting. In the primary extended model, the PCI group had lower absolute VO₂peak (difference, - 59.69 mL/min; 95% confidence interval [CI], - 109.65 to - 9.74; P = 0.019), body weight-normalized VO₂peak (- 0.83 mL·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹; 95% CI, - 1.54 to - 0.11; P = 0.023), and pVO₂ (- 4.28% points; 95% CI, - 7.13 to - 1.43; P = 0.003). In cross-fitted reference-group mapping, only the residual difference in pVO₂ remained statistically significant (- 4.16% points; 95% CI, - 7.45 to - 1.00; P = 0.012). Results were generally consistent across sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients during stable recovery after PCI had a CRF gap relative to a contemporaneous angiographic reference group, with th

candidates.title: Heterogeneity in diagnosing heart failure - real world data from electronic health records.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) prevalence is increasing and is relatively well described. Less is known about using tests in diagnosing HF in clinical practice. The aim of this article was to describe the diagnostic practices among incident HF patients in Estonia.
METHODS: Electronic health records and healthcare provision claims from 1st January 2012 to 31st December 2019 for a random sample of 10% of the Estonian population (N = 150 824) were used to retrieve data about newly diagnosed HF patients focusing on natriuretic peptide and echocardiographic testing. The incident HF was defined as the first occurrence of International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision codes I50.x or I11.0, with no occurrence of I50.x or I11.0 during the previous four years. The group differences were analysed using the Wilcoxon rank sum test for continuous variables. For categorical variables, the chi-square test and binary logistic regression, controlled for gender and age, were used.
RESULTS: Within one year before and after the HF diagnosis, 31.0% of patients underwent echocardiography and natriuretic peptide testing, but 40.7% did not receive either investigation. Most diagnostic assessments were performed in three months before HF diagnosis with 41% of patients receiving at least one test. We observed that patients diagnosed with HF in emergency departments were most likely to undergo at least one HF test (81,3%).
CONCLUSION: In clinical practice, HF may be diagnosed in the absence of sufficient diagnostic evidence. By highlighting key shortcomings in the routine clinical diagnosis of HF, this study underscores the potential to enhance patient care (e.g. creating HF pathways).

candidates.title: A composite metabolic profile score combining the atherogenic index of plasma and triglyceride-glucose index is associated with cardiac magnetic resonance-derived structural severity in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a cross-sectional study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic and inflammatory dysregulation have been implicated in the phenotypic heterogeneity of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). A recent study demonstrated that the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is independently associated with left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction in HCM using echocardiography, but the relationship between metabolic and inflammatory biomarkers and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived measures of structural severity and myocardial fibrosis remains unexplored. We aimed to investigate associations between metabolic (atherogenic index of plasma [AIP], TyG index) and inflammatory (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR], platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio [PLR], systemic immune-inflammation index [SII]) biomarkers, individually and as composite profile scores, and CMR-derived structural and functional severity in patients with HCM.
METHODS: In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional analytic study, 63 patients with HCM who underwent CMR were included. A metabolic profile score (z-AIP + z-TyG) and an inflammatory profile score (z-PLR + z-SII) were constructed following collinearity assessment. Associations with LVOT obstruction and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent ≥ 5% were assessed using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.
RESULTS: LVOT obstruction was present in 27 patients (42.9%), and LGE ≥ 5% in 46 (73.0%). AIP, the TyG index, and the metabolic profile score were significantly higher in patients with LVOT obstruction (all P < 0.001). The metabolic profile score remained independently associated with both LVOT obstruction (OR 3.07, 95% CI 1.57-6.01, P = 0.001) and LGE ≥ 5% (OR 1.50, 95% CI 1.04-2.15, P = 0.030) after adjustment, with good discriminatory performance (AUC 0.864 and 0.780, respectively); exploratory analyses indicated that AIP was the principal driver of this performan

candidates.title: Serial echocardiographic changes in left ventricular size and calculated mass after transcatheter aortic valve replacement for predominant native aortic regurgitation without severe aortic stenosis: a retrospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD) is widely available but is one-dimensional and load dependent. We evaluated serial LV size and calculated LV mass after TAVR for predominant native aortic regurgitation (AR) without severe aortic stenosis (AS), using all quantitative and semi-quantitative information available in routine clinical echocardiographic reports.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 62 patients treated between January 2023 and February 2025. Echocardiographic measurements were extracted from contemporaneous clinical reports; original image loops were unavailable for retrospective core-laboratory remeasurement. AR severity, report-derived regurgitant jet area, valve morphology, aortic-root measurements, procedural characteristics, and residual AR were summarized with variable-specific denominators. Linear mixed-effects models assessed serial LVEDD and calculated LV mass. Approximate 1-year paired analyses included one additional 249-day examination recovered during report re-review.
RESULTS: Baseline AR was severe or very severe in 55 patients and moderate-to-severe in 7. Regurgitant jet area was available in 39 patients (median 9.9 (9.3-11.2) cm²). Numeric vena contracta, EROA, and regurgitant volume were not recorded with sufficient consistency for analysis. LVEDD decreased at every postprocedural window in mixed-effects analysis (adjusted approximate 1-year difference, -5.89 mm; 95% CI, -7.67 to -4.11; P < 0.001). Calculated LV mass also decreased (adjusted approximate 1-year difference, -47.8 g; 95% CI, -66.1 to -29.5; P < 0.001). Among 30 patients with approximate 1-year LVEDD, median LVEDD change was - 7.0 (-10.8-2.0) mm (P < 0.001). Calculated LV mass decreased by -47.4 (-90.6-4.0) g (P = 0.002), and LV mass index decreased by -30.2 (-58.4-2.4) g/m² (P = 0.003). candidates.title: Sleeping with the unknown: coronary vasospasm in an anomalous right circumflex artery mimicking in-stent restenosis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary vasospasm represents a transient, reversible constriction of coronary arteries that often goes unrecognised in patients with established coronary artery disease or anomalous coronary anatomy. When combined with prior percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), vasospasm can closely mimic in-stent restenosis, leading to delayed diagnosis and unnecessary repeat interventions.
CASE PRESENTATION: We describe a 55-year-old male with prior PCI to an anomalous right circumflex artery (RCx) who presented with recurrent nocturnal chest pain and asymptomatic transient ST-segment elevation (STE) during sleep. Despite FFR-guided PCI to the left anterior descending artery (LAD) and subsequent repeat intervention for suspected RCx in-stent restenosis, symptoms persisted. A probable diagnosis of nocturnal coronary vasospasm was established based on the clinical presentation, characteristic nocturnal ECG changes, response to diltiazem, and exclusion of alternative structural pathology on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging; however, the diagnosis remains inferential in the absence of invasive provocation testing.
DISCUSSION: This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity of probable coronary vasospasm in a male patient with structural coronary disease and anomalous coronary anatomy. Several factors may have contributed to diagnostic delay, including anchoring toward structural disease, angiographic ambiguity, anomalous anatomy, and the unusual nocturnal presentation. The differential response to calcium channel blocker subclasses in this patient is presented as a clinically relevant, hypothesis-generating observation rather than evidence of therapeutic superiority.
CONCLUSION: Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for probable coronary vasospasm in patients with recurrent nocturnal ST elevation following PCI, particularly when symptoms, telemetry findings, and coronary physiology are discordant with fixed obstructive disease. candidates.title: Blunt anatomical cardiac injury (BACI) - lessons from a single trauma center cohort.
candidates.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with anatomical damage to the heart after blunt trauma are rarely seen in hospital settings due to their elevated prehospital mortality. The aim of this study is to review our center experience with this entity.
METHODS: After institutional research board approval, a local Trauma Databank search (Qatar National Trauma Registry) was performed from 2016 to 2025. Cases presented with blunt trauma and anatomical changes to pericardium or heart, detected in imaging or surgery, in patients above 13 years old were diagnosed as blunt anatomical cardiac injury - BACI and included.
RESULTS: Amongst 17542 blunt trauma cases admitted to our Trauma Center during the study period, 15 patients (0.09% incidence) met the inclusion/exclusion criteria. All patients were males, with average age of 43 years (ranges 26-75), with ISS of 32 (ranges 10-75). The most common mechanism of injury was pedestrian struck (5cases -33%). Hypotension at trauma room assessment was common (8 cases - 53% of patients) and 8 patients (53%) required surgery. FAST, echocardiogram and computed tomography were used as diagnostic tools. The patients presented in 4 anatomical patterns: (a) intracardiac/valve damage; (b) pericardial effusion; (c) pericardial laceration and (d) cardiac rupture. Three patients (20%) died, all during emergent surgery and sustaining cardiac rupture.
CONCLUSION: BACI is uncommonly seen at Emergency Departments and carries elevated early mortality in cases with cardiac rupture, requiring high index of suspicion for diagnosis. Different clinical presentations of BACI were observed and described in this series. Further studies with larger number of patients are needed to further clarify possible differences in severity, surgical requirement and mortality according to the BACI structural presentation.

candidates.title: Stress Echocardiographic Strain-Dyssynchrony Interactions Identify Prognostic Phenotypes in Chagas Cardiomyopathy: A Pilot Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mechanical heterogeneity is a hallmark of advanced cardiomyopathy, although stress echocardiography traditionally focuses on ischemia or global systolic reserve. Exercise stress echocardiography may identify distinct mechanical phenotypes in chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy (CCC) through integrated assessment of strain and dyssynchrony behavior.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the interaction between contractile reserve and intraventricular dyssynchrony (IVD) during exercise stress echocardiography and its association with clinical outcomes in patients with CCC.
METHODS: Forty patients with severe CCC (left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 35%, non-LBBB QRS morphology) underwent symptom-limited treadmill stress echocardiography. Global longitudinal strain (GLS), IVD, and conventional echocardiographic parameters were assessed at rest and immediately after peak exercise. Patients were stratified into four groups according to GLS and IVD variation. The primary endpoint was a composite of death, heart transplantation, or hospitalization for heart failure over a 2-year follow-up. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.
RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 729 days, 20 patients (50%) reached the primary endpoint. Patients without contractile reserve and without dyssynchrony improvement during exercise had significantly lower event-free survival compared with the remaining groups (p < 0.01). When analyzed separately, both absence of contractile reserve and unfavorable dyssynchrony response were associated with adverse outcomes. In multivariable analysis, only right ventricular function remained independently associated with the primary outcome (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% confidence interval 0.71-0.96; p = 0.014).
CONCLUSIONS: Integration of strain-derived contractile reserve and IVD during physiologic stress may help identify prognostic phenotypes beyond ejection fraction in CCC and supports the concept of dynamic mechanical phenotyping in advanced cardiomyopathy.

candidates.title: Regional Left Ventricular Myocardial Strain Alterations in Patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy and Correlation with Electrocardiographic and Motor Function Alterations.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is characterized by progressive degradation of muscle function. Myocardial dysfunction is a major cause of mortality; however, its correlation with skeletal motor function remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess myocardial function and to correlate it with motor function in patients with DMD.
METHODS: This was a cross-sectional observational study of patients with DMD. Evaluations included the Motor Function Measurement (MFM) scale, electrocardiogram (ECG), and echocardiography (Echo) with speckle-tracking (STE) imaging of the left ventricle (LV). The level of significance adopted in the statistical analysis was 5%.
RESULTS: Thirty-three patients with a mean age of 14.30 ± 4.09 years. The average MFM score was 52.30 ± 16.32%. Electrocardiographic abnormalities were observed in 75% of patients. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was preserved (57.80 ± 9.62%). Global longitudinal strain (GLS) was reduced in 70% of the patients (-15.06 ± 2.46%; normal ≤ -18%), global circumferential strain (GCS) was decreased in 76% (-12.99 ± 2.89; normal ≤ -18%), and global radial strain (GRS) was reduced in 80% (20.52 ± 15.72; normal ≥ 40%). Hypokinesia and a significant reduction in regional myocardial strain (REGLSi) were also observed in the inferior and inferolateral segments of the LV. No significant correlation was found between MFM and ECHO variables.
CONCLUSION: Patients with DMD exhibit early compromise in STE parameters (GLS, GRS and GCS) and in REGLSi, particularly in the inferior and inferolateral LV regions, even with preserved LVEF (Central Figure). No significant correlation was observed between motor and cardiac function parameters.

candidates.title: Cost-effectiveness and Budget Impact Analysis of Coronary CT Angiography in the Brazilian Unified Health System.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) represents a major clinical and economic burden for the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS). Although coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has excellent diagnostic accuracy, cost-effectiveness analyses (CEA) based on national data are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness and budget impact of incorporating CCTA as the initial diagnostic strategy for patients with suspected stable CAD from the SUS perspective.
METHODS: A cost-effectiveness analysis (CEA) and a budget impact analysis (BIA) were conducted, comparing CCTA with invasive coronary angiography (ICA) and with a panel of functional tests in patients with suspected stable CAD. A one-year time horizon was adopted for the CEA and five years for the BIA. Effectiveness outcomes included the incidence of acute myocardial infarction (AMI), revascularization rates, and hospitalizations. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: CCTA proved to be cost-effective, reducing costs related to AMI (R$610.18 vs. R$867.80), revascularization (R$1,378.14 vs. R$1,833.84), and hospitalization (R$602.86 vs. R$932.79), resulting in savings of R$329.93 per patient. Compared with functional tests, CCTA also reduced costs associated with AMI (R$610.18 vs. R$658.36), revascularization (R$1,378.14 vs. R$1,659.18), and hospitalization (R$602.86 vs. R$628.16). The BIA projected cumulative savings for SUS ranging from R$34.1 million to R$73 million over five years, depending on the comparator and diffusion scenario.
CONCLUSIONS: The results suggest that using CCTA as the initial diagnostic test for patients with low-to-moderate risk of CAD in SUS may represent an economically favorable strategy, with potential to generate substantial cost savings compared with the evaluated alternatives.

candidates.title: Wearable acoustic cardiography for detection of left ventricular and valvular dysfunction: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative cardiac evaluation based on history and physical examination is subjective, risking delayed diagnosis or excessive echocardiography. Acoustic cardiography (ACG) synchronizes ECG and heart sound analysis for rapid point-of-care cardiac screening. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of wearable ACG for left ventricular dysfunction, significant valvular dysfunction, and the consistency of ACG-aided preoperative risk assessment with expert consensus.
METHODS: This prospective single-center study enrolled consecutive patients undergoing major elective non-cardiac surgery. Echocardiography served as the reference standard; the primary endpoint was LVEF <40%.
RESULTS: Among 262 patients, ACG showed excellent performance for LVEF <40% (AUC=0.979, sensitivity 93.3%, specificity 96.4%). It achieved substantial agreement with echocardiography for significant valvular dysfunction (κ=0.69). Adding ACG improved consistency with expert consensus versus physical examination alone (κ=0.71 vs 0.55).
CONCLUSIONS: Wearable ACG provides high accuracy for preoperative screening of systolic and valvular dysfunction. It facilitates targeted echocardiography referral. Further trials are needed to verify its impact on referral decisions and perioperative outcomes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2300073695.

candidates.title: Coronary Artery Calcium Scoring From Contrast-Enhanced Photon-Counting CT in Pre-TAVI Patients: Intra-Patient Comparison of PURE Calcium and Virtual Non-Contrast Algorithms.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate coronary artery calcium score (CACS) obtained from virtual unenhanced ECG-gated and non-gated photon-counting CT (PCCT) images using PURE Calcium (PC) and Virtual Non-Contrast (VNC) algorithms, compared to unenhanced ECG-gated images as reference standard.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients scheduled for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) were prospectively included. Per patient, CACS was quantified in five datasets: true non-contrast ECG-gated scan (TNC, reference); PC and VNC reconstructions of ECG-gated (PCGATED, VNCGATED) and non-gated contrast-enhanced scans (PCNON-GATED, VNCNON-GATED). Pairwise comparisons with the TNC reference were performed using Bland-Altman analysis, correlation, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and risk-category agreement assessed by linearly weighted Cohen's κ. Additionally, CACS was classified into risk categories (0; 1-10; 11-100; 101-400; >400).
RESULTS: Sixty-one patients were included (59% female; 78±8 years). Median total CACS on TNC was 659 [222-1183]. Agreement with TNC was highest for PCGATED (ICC = 0.99; bias -73), followed by PCNON-GATED (ICC = 0.98; bias -152). In contrast, VNCGATED and VNCNON-GATED demonstrated substantially larger negative biases (-615 and -687, respectively) and lower agreement (ICC = 0.62 and 0.54, respectively). Compared with TNC, significant differences in total CACS were observed for all reconstruction methods except PCGATED (p< 0.001 for all significant comparisons). Agreement in CACS category classification was higher for PC reconstructions (κ = 0.83/0.80 for ECG-gated/non-gated) than VNC reconstructions (κ = 0.41/0.33 for ECG-gated/non-gated). Exploratory vessel-level agreement showed a similar pattern.
CONCLUSION: CACS derived from virtual unenhanced contrast-enhanced PCCT images systematically underestimated the reference CACS. PC substantially outperformed VNC, including non-gated acquisitions, although underestimation persisted and the absolute scores sho

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Echocardiographic Platform for Automated Measurements in Children.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study assessed the accuracy of a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted echocardiographic platform for automated measurements in children.
METHODS: In this prospective, blinded, comparative, single-center pilot study, transthoracic echocardiography was performed in pediatric subjects aged 5 to 18 years using the Siemens Acuson Origin cardiovascular ultrasound system. For spectral Doppler assessments, two echocardiographic acquisitions were required: one using the AI-assisted protocol with automatic spectral Doppler marker placement, and one with manual marker placement. For all other analyses, a single manual acquisition was required for subsequent AI and manual assessments. Images were initially analyzed with the AI-assisted protocol, followed immediately by manual evaluation by a pediatric cardiologist blinded to the AI-derived results. Indices included B-mode, M-mode, Doppler, speckle tracking, and four-dimensional (4D) parameters. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis.
RESULTS: Thirty subjects (23 males; age 12.2±3.8 years) were studied, including 23 with structurally normal heart, six with congenital heart diseases, and one with dilated cardiomyopathy. Feasibility exceeded 90% for 2D AI-assisted assessment and 80% for 4D ventricular volumetry, but was below 35% for 4D atrial volumetry. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was strong for all parameters except septal (ICC 0.2) and left ventricular posterior wall thickness (ICC 0.5). Bland-Altman analysis showed no significant systematic differences.
CONCLUSION: Our pilot findings suggest that a commercially available AI-assisted echocardiographic system may be feasible and reasonably accurate for conventional and advanced quantitative echocardiographic assessment for children in a real-world setting.

candidates.title: Subclinical Left Ventricular Hypertrophy Among Emergency Department Patients With Elevated Blood Pressure.
candidates.journal: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension (HTN) is a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, yet early detection of target organ damage is often missed, particularly in patients with limited access to care. The Emergency Department (ED), a key site of care for underserved populations, may offer an opportunity for risk stratification; we sought to determine the prevalence of LVH-a marker of subclinical disease and increased cardiovascular risk-among ED patients with asymptomatic elevated blood pressure and assess differences by sex, race, and insurance status.
METHODS: We enrolled a convenience sample of adults aged 18-65 years presenting to an academic ED with blood pressure ≥ 140 mmHg systolic or ≥ 90 mmHg diastolic on two measurements. Subjects with prior LVH, active cardiac disease, hypertensive emergency, dialysis dependence, or pregnancy were excluded. LVH was identified using left ventricular mass indexed to height2.7 or body surface area via focused (point-of-care) cardiac ultrasound (parasternal long-axis view). Multivariate logistic regression assessed associations with LVH.
RESULTS: Among 155 subjects, 46 (29.7%, 95% CI 22.5%-36.9%) had LVH. Mean age was 46.9 ± 12.1 years; 53.6% were women. LVH was more prevalent in women (38.6% vs. 19.4%; p = 0.009) and remained independently associated with female sex (OR 2.44, 95% CI 1.14-5.22, p = 0.021) and prior hypertension (OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.14-5.39, p = 0.023). Notably, 18.3% of patients without a prior hypertension diagnosis demonstrated LVH (p = 0.004).
CONCLUSION: Nearly one-third of ED patients with elevated blood pressure had LVH, including many without known hypertension, with a higher prevalence among women.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05730309.

candidates.title: Cardiac imaging biomarkers of heart failure in diabetes for phenotyping, risk stratification, and evaluating therapeutic response.
candidates.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a well-established risk factor for the development of heart failure (HF), yet HF risk within this population is highly heterogeneous. Appropriate biomarker selection and a limited mechanistic understanding of the phenotypic subtypes of HF in T2DM remain barriers to both risk stratification and therapeutic development. Cardiac imaging-based biomarkers are emerging as versatile tools for assessing myocardial dysfunction in T2DM and may enable a shift toward non-invasive, comprehensive, and precise disease assessment. Advances in cardiac MRI, echocardiography, CT, PET, and metabolic imaging have enhanced detection of myocardial fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction, and early functional impairment, as well as assessment of response to contemporary metabolic therapies. This review synthesizes recent imaging evidence to deepen our understanding of HF mechanisms in T2DM and to improve early risk stratification and surveillance strategies. Artificial intelligence-based imaging applications in T2DM with HF and other cardiomyopathies, including radiomics analyses and prediction tasks, will also be discussed with respect to their potential to further refine HF phenotyping and risk assessment.

candidates.title: Bentall procedure in the small aortoannular complex: impact of the implantation plane on prosthesis upsizing and early outcomes-a retrospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proximal conduit geometry may affect prosthesis accommodation during Bentall surgery for severe aortic stenosis and a small aortoannular complex. We compared subannular-supported supra-annular conduit implantation (SSSC) with supra-annular-supported annular conduit implantation (SSAC) for nominal size gain and early outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 402 adults undergoing mechanical Bentall surgery between January 2020 and April 2026 (SSSC, n = 164; SSAC, n = 238). After leaflet excision and annular debridement, the largest manufacturer sizer accepted before suture/pledget placement defined the presuture expected size; repeat sizing after interrupted pledgeted sutures guided final conduit selection. The primary endpoint was implanted nominal size minus presuture expected size. Preoperative computed tomography characterized anatomy without conversion to nominal size, and body-size variables were recalculated from corrected measurements. Routine transthoracic echocardiography on postoperative days 5-7 measured continuity-equation effective orifice area (EOA), indexed EOA (EOAi), prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM), and Doppler gradients. The 24-patient narrow sinotubular junction-proximal ascending aorta subgroup was analyzed separately.
RESULTS: SSSC yielded larger implanted size (23.4 ± 1.4 vs. 22.0 ± 1.1 mm) and nominal size gain (3.3 ± 1.1 vs. 1.9 ± 0.9 mm; both p < 0.001). After adjustment for corrected body size, baseline anatomy, and patient characteristics, SSSC remained associated with 0.99 mm greater gain (95% CI, 0.78-1.19; p < 0.001), higher EOA (+ 0.108 cm²) and EOAi (+ 0.063 cm²/m²), and lower odds of moderate PPM (adjusted odds ratio, 0.15; all p < 0.001). The adjusted mean-gradient difference was nonsignificant and the peak-gradient difference small. Permanent pacemaker implantation was more frequent after SSSC (7.9% vs. 2.1%; p = 0.007), whereas mortality was similar.
CONCLUSIONS: SSSC was associated with approximately 1 m

candidates.title: Polarimetric Characterization of CCTA-Defined High-Risk Coronary Plaques: Linking Morphology to Fibrous Matrix Organization and Lipid Burden.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-risk plaque (HRP) features on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) predict future coronary events, yet the microstructural substrate underlying these radiological signatures remains largely unknown. Polarization-sensitive (PS) optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) quantifies tissue birefringence and depolarization-derived lipid core burden index (LCBI) in vivo. We aimed to investigate the relationship between PS-OFDI-derived polarimetric signals and CCTA-defined HRP features.
METHODS: We retrospectively identified 43 patients from a prospective registry of intracoronary polarimetry with PS-OFDI who had undergone CCTA before hospitalization and subsequently underwent OFDI-guided percutaneous coronary intervention. A total of 70 coronary segments were analyzed. HRP was defined as the presence of ≥2 established CCTA features: positive remodeling, low-attenuation plaque, napkin-ring sign, or spotty calcification. Conventional OFDI metrics and PS-OFDI-derived birefringence and depolarization-derived maximum 4-mm LCBI were evaluated in relation to CCTA-defined HRP. Segment-level comparisons accounted for within-patient clustering, and correlation and discrimination analyses incorporated patient-level bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Among the 70 analyzed segments, 28 (40%) exhibited CCTA-defined HRP. HRP segments showed lower birefringence and higher depolarization-derived maximum 4-mm LCBI than non-HRP segments (both P<0.001). Birefringence was inversely correlated with low-attenuation plaque volume (ρ=-0.350 [95% CI, -0.543 to -0.131]), whereas depolarization-derived maximum 4-mm LCBI correlated with maximum lipid arc (ρ=0.480 [95% CI, 0.277-0.635]), lipid length (ρ=0.463 [95% CI, 0.199-0.654]), and minimum fibrous cap thickness (ρ=-0.466 [95% CI, -0.661 to -0.212]).
