candidates.title: Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement after failed edge-to-edge repair.
candidates.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual or recurrent tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is a growing concern in clinical practice and is associated with inferior outcomes.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the early experience of transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) in patients with failed TEER.
METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing TTVR for recurrent or residual severe TR after TEER. Clinical, echocardiographic, and computed tomography findings were evaluated. The primary outcome was clinical success at 30 days after TTVR.
RESULTS: Of the 28 patients included (age 78.5±6.3 years, 61% female), 20 (72%) had residual TR and 8 (28%) had recurrent TR diagnosed within a median of 182 days after TEER. Patients were severely symptomatic (New York Heart Association [NYHA] III/IV in 97%), and 64% had massive/torrential TR. In 6 patients (21%), a commissural TEER device was evident, enabling direct TTVR (neocommissure strategy). Engagement of TEER devices with single leaflet device attachment during TTVR was carried out in 12 patients (43%), and electrosurgical laceration and stabilisation to facilitate TTVR in 10 patients (36%). Clinical success at 30 days was 93%. NYHA Functional Class improved in 93% of patients, with 85% being in NYHA I/II at 1 month after TTVR. Two patients died from non-cardiac reasons, and during a median follow-up of 69 days, 4 patients suffered a heart failure hospitalisation despite procedural success.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small patient cohort, three different TTVR strategies after failed TEER resulted in significant clinical success at 30 days and led to substantial symptom relief during short-term follow-up.

candidates.title: Acute right ventricular response to transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement.
candidates.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Changes in right ventricular (RV) function are frequent after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR), yet their mechanisms and prognostic implications remain incompletely defined.
AIMS: We sought to characterise acute RV functional changes following TTVR and evaluate their prognostic impact.
METHODS: This multicentre study included consecutive patients treated with TTVR between 2019 and 2025 with complete imaging data. RV function was assessed by echocardiography at baseline, intraprocedurally, and before discharge. RV end-systolic elastance (Ees), effective arterial elastance (Ea), and RV-pulmonary artery coupling (Ees/Ea) were derived from non-invasive single-beat pressure-volume loop analysis. Changes over time were assessed using paired tests, and associations with mortality were investigated using Cox regression analysis with Firth's penalised likelihood.
RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients (median age 78 years; 72% female; EVOQUE n=49; LuX-Valve Plus n=18) were included. At discharge, both cohorts showed declines in absolute RV free-wall longitudinal strain (aRV-FWLS; -10.4%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -10.4%; p=0.001 for LuX-Valve Plus) and fractional area change (FAC; -18.0%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -13.5%; p=0.005 for LuX-Valve Plus). Overall, 58% of patients met the criteria for severe RV dysfunction after TTVR. Over a median follow-up of 19 months, 15 patients died. Device type, acute RV functional changes, Ees, and Ees/Ea were not associated with mortality (allp>0.05). In contrast, computed tomography-derived RV coupling (hazard ratio [HR] 0.02, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.01-0.89) and the coexistence of baseline longitudinal (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion <17 mm and/or aRV-FWLS <23%) and circumferential (RV-FAC ≤35%) RV dysfunction (HR 3.93, 95% CI: 1.10-14.47) were associated with mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: TTVR is associated with an acute decline in RV systolic function. Although common, early postprocedural RV dysfunction was not a

candidates.title: An extreme giant left atrium exceeding 160 mm in rheumatic mitral valve disease: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Giant left atrium is a rare complication of chronic rheumatic mitral valve disease. We report an extreme case to highlight the technical challenges and clinical considerations in the surgical management of this uncommon condition.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 46-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral valve disease, permanent atrial fibrillation, and right heart failure presented with dysphagia and hoarseness. Computed tomography showed a left atrial anteroposterior diameter of 167 mm and a computed volume of 2,225 to 2,411 mL, among the largest ever documented. She underwent mitral valve replacement, tricuspid annuloplasty, and left atrial plication. Surgery was technically successful, with visible intraoperative reduction in atrial size and a subsequent decrease in cardiac silhouette on early postoperative chest radiography, but the patient died on postoperative day 12 from refractory low cardiac output and drug-resistant ventilator-associated pneumonia.
CONCLUSIONS: This case illustrates an extreme presentation of giant left atrium associated with rheumatic mitral valve disease. Although surgical reduction was technically feasible, careful patient selection and preoperative optimization remain crucial in patients with advanced right heart failure and low physiological reserve.

candidates.title: Multimodality Imaging in the Evaluation of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
candidates.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is characterized by pathologic hypertrophy in the absence of a potentially causative disease process and carries increased risk of heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and sudden cardiac death. Synergistic use of multi-modal imaging is pivotal and necessary in the diagnosis and management of patients with, or at risk for, HCM. Echocardiography, cardiac MR, and cardiac computed tomography each have important roles and limitations in assessing the morphologic changes responsible for symptoms and morbidity in HCM. In this article, we will explore these modalities and their roles in evaluating HCM.

candidates.title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy in the Absence of "Hypertrophy": A Precision Medicine Reappraisal.
candidates.abstract: Fixed wall thickness cutoffs have historically defined hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), yet this rigid approach overlooks patients with early, segmental, or morphologically subtle disease. Subthreshold phenotypes-particularly in women, individuals with short stature, and those with apical or focal variants-may not meet conventional criteria despite exhibiting pathologic features. This article examines the limitations of absolute diagnostic thresholds and advocates for a precision medicine framework. Integrating cardiac magnetic resonance imaging with individualized metrics and architectural markers enhances diagnostic accuracy, identifies nonclassical presentations, and facilitates earlier disease recognition, ultimately improving care across the heterogeneous spectrum of HCM.

candidates.title: Redefining Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Ejection Fraction and Global Longitudinal Strain.
candidates.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is an inherited disease characterized by increased myocardial thickness without cardiac, systemic, or metabolic causes to explain the observed left ventricular (LV) hypertrophy. Importantly, LV systolic dysfunction influences symptoms, heart failure, and the risk of SCD in HCM. LV global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) is a sensitive marker for detecting subclinical LV dysfunction and improving risk stratification. Integrating LV-GLS with other imaging biomarkers, such as late gadolinium enhancement and left atrial reservoir strain, may improve risk prediction. Future research should focus on refining LV-GLS cutoffs and exploring its utility for personalized risk assessment in HCM.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cardiomyopathies: From Opportunistic Detection to Decision-Critical Risk Stratification.
candidates.abstract: This article examines the evolving role of artificial intelligence (AI) across the continuum of care in cardiomyopathies, from opportunistic screening to decision-critical risk stratification. AI-enhanced electrocardiography enables scalable early detection, while advanced echocardiographic and cardiac magnetic resonance-based radiomics refine myocardial substrate characterization. Multimodal models integrating imaging, electrical, and clinical data refine risk stratification beyond conventional metrics such as left ventricular ejection fraction. However, clinical translation requires external validation, calibration stability, interpretability, and structured workflow integration. AI emerges not as autonomous diagnosis, but as accountable, clinician-supervised decision support embedded within multidisciplinary cardiovascular care.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence and Computational Methods in Cardiovascular Ultrasound.
candidates.abstract: Cardiovascular ultrasound is particularly suitable for artificial intelligence: it is widely available, information-rich, dynamic, and strongly dependent on acquisition quality and operator interpretation. Contemporary computational methods can guide image acquisition, recognize views, segment chambers, quantify ventricular function, characterize myocardial mechanics, and detect disease signatures. In heart failure, multimodal architectures can combine echocardiographic images and Doppler data with clinical variables, biomarkers, electrocardiograms, and omics to support patient-level phenotyping and prognostic assessment, while emerging foundation models enable adaptation across multiple tasks. The most credible near-term model is augmented echocardiography: automation of repetitive measurements combined with transparent quality control and expert clinical interpretation.

candidates.title: Moving Toward Clinical Cardiac Magnetic Resonance: Full Integration of Imaging Data into Patient Care Pathways.
candidates.abstract: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) provides the greatest clinical value when performed to answer a specific clinical question rather than as a stand-alone imaging test. The significance of CMR findings depends on integration with the patient's clinical history, Electrocardiogram , laboratory data, and other imaging results. Clinical CMR extends beyond image acquisition by integrating tailored imaging, clinical interpretation, and management-oriented reporting. In heart failure, clinical CMR supports etiologic diagnosis, phenotyping, risk stratification, therapeutic decisions, and selected follow-up. Artificial intelligence will streamline CMR workflows, but clinical reasoning will remain essential for translating imaging findings into patient care.

candidates.title: Nuclear Cardiac Imaging.
candidates.journal: Magnetic resonance imaging clinics of North America
candidates.abstract: Nuclear cardiology is a broad topic but is commonly used for evaluation of inducible ischemia in patients with symptoms suggestive of coronary artery disease. Tc-99 m sestamibi and tetrofosmin single-photon emission computed tomography have long been mainstays in the evaluation of reversible perfusion defects indicative of ischemia; however, cardiac PET, including Rb-82 PET, has gained widespread use because it permits quantification of myocardial blood flow and myocardial blood flow reserve. Abnormal myocardial blood flow reserve may indicate epicardial coronary artery disease, diffuse atherosclerosis, and/or coronary microvascular dysfunction even when relative perfusion appears normal, and it can alter risk stratification.

candidates.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Initial Clinical Experience.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), defined as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, remains challenging to treat because of its heterogeneous pathophysiology. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in patients with symptomatic nHCM.
METHODS: Patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory nHCM were prospectively enrolled to undergo transapical beating-heart septal myectomy through a left minithoracotomy. Under real-time transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, septal myectomy was tailored to relieve systolic cavity obliteration and mid-to-apical ventricular obstruction and to enlarge the left ventricular cavity. The primary end point was procedural success at 6 to 12 months postoperatively, defined as fulfillment of all prespecified criteria compared with baseline: ≥1-class improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, ≥10-point increase in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, ≥10-mL increase in stroke volume, and normal or grade I diastolic function.
RESULTS: Between January 2023 and January 2025, 97 consecutive eligible patients with nHCM underwent transapical beating-heart septal myectomy at Tongji Hospital. At postoperative 6 to 12 months, procedural success was achieved in 87.6%. Specifically, New York Heart Association functional class I increased from 0% at baseline to 93.8% at follow-up, the median Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved from 64 (interquartile range, 56-69) to 87 (interquartile range, 82-92; P<0.001), the stroke volume increased from 53.5 mL (interquartile range, 41.0-66.6 mL) to 70.8 mL (interquartile range, 61.3-82.3 mL; P<0.001), and normal or grade I diastolic function increased from 65.6% to 97.9%. Among patients who underwent paired cardiopulmonary exercise testing (n=58), peak oxygen uptake increased by 1.1±2.9 mL/kg/min (P=0.008). In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analy

candidates.title: Diabetes mellitus and the risk of sudden cardiac death in patients with and without coronary artery disease.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes is associated with sudden cardiac death (SCD), but evidence in patients without coronary artery disease (CAD) remains limited. SCD risk may vary by revascularisation strategy in diabetic patients with CAD.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 22,395 consecutive patients undergoing coronary angiography from 2007 to 2018, either electively for suspected or known CAD or for acute coronary syndrome. Follow-up ended 31 December 2022. Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA), SCD and SCD-equivalent events were adjudicated using medical records, death certificates, and nationwide mortality data.
RESULTS: Among 22,395 patients, 5,804 had diabetes. Over a median follow-up of 8.1 years (IQR 5.1-11.6), 1,710 experienced SCA, including 1,046 SCD or SCD-equivalent events. After multivariable adjustment including left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), diabetes showed similar associations with SCD or SCD-equivalent event (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 1.38, 1.21-1.58; P < 0.001) and non-SCD death (SHR 1.37, 1.30-1.44; P < 0.001). Yet, among patients with diabetes, the 10-year cumulative incidence of non-SCA death was more than three times that of SCA. Diabetes was associated with SCD or SCD-equivalent event even without obstructive CAD (SHR 1.53, 1.11-2.12; P = 0.010). In patients with diabetes and CAD, lower SCD risk was observed in revascularized patients than in those receiving medical therapy (SHR 0.77, 0.60-0.99; P = 0.039). The diabetes-SCD association appeared stronger at age < 70 years, with LVEF ≥ 40%, in type 1 diabetes, and with higher HbA1c levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Diabetes was associated with SCD irrespective of obstructive CAD, but the high competing burden of non-SCA death highlights the challenge of SCA prevention and the importance of identifying higher-risk subgroups among patients with diabetes.

candidates.title: Two-dimensional speckle-tracking imaging for assessing cardiac dysfunction in liver cirrhosis: correlation with Child-Pugh score.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging (2D-STI) enables sensitive and quantitative assessment of myocardial deformation, its application in patients with liver cirrhosis (LC) has largely been limited to ventricular function. This study applied 2D-STI to evaluate both ventricular and atrial function in order to identify early myocardial dysfunction in this population.
METHODS: A total of 82 patients with LC were enrolled and stratified according to the Child-Pugh classification into Class A (n = 30), Class B (n = 29), and Class C (n = 23). Thirty healthy individuals served as controls. All 112 participants underwent conventional echocardiography and 2D-STI assessment.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, all LC groups showed reduced left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) and right ventricular free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS) (both P < 0.05), with a progressive decline from Class A to Class C. In contrast, right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RVGLS) was significantly decreased only in Classes B and C (P < 0.05). Left atrial conduit strain (LAScd) was significantly reduced across all LC groups (P < 0.05), whereas left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) and contractile strain (LASct) demonstrated a biphasic pattern -initially increased, then decreased- compared with controls. Overall, 2D-STI detected cardiac dysfunction earlier than conventional echocardiography. Significant negative correlations were observed between Child-Pugh score and LVGLS, RVFWLS, and RVGLS.
CONCLUSION: Cardiac function is impaired in patients with LC and deteriorates with increasing disease severity. Compared with conventional echocardiography, 2D-STI detects cardiac dysfunction at an earlier stage, providing valuable support for early clinical intervention.

candidates.title: Association between periodontitis and coronary plaque composition: can early periodontal treatment influence coronary artery disease progression? A study protocol for a prospective, randomized controlled trial.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The (PERIOdontitis and Coronary Artery Disease) PERIOCAD study aims to investigate the association between periodontitis and coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients undergoing cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and the effectiveness of early versus late periodontitis (PD) treatment on systemic inflammation and CAD progression.
BACKGROUND: PD and CAD are common diseases, sharing underlying molecular mechanisms, like systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Epidemiological and genetic studies suggest a strong link between PD and CAD. Yet, it remains unclear whether treatment of periodontitis may attenuate progression of arteriosclerosis. CCTA enables reproducible quantitative assessment of coronary plaque volumes and composition, providing metrics for both cross-sectional associations and longitudinal changes of plaque burden.
METHODS: PERIOCAD is a prospective, randomized, controlled trial (RCT) aiming to enroll 200 patients who undergo clinically indicated CCTA. All participants will undergo comprehensive periodontal status assessment and patients diagnosed with PD (estimated n = 100) will be randomized 1:1 to either early, systematic PD therapy (intervention arm) or delayed care after 2 years (control arm). CCTA analysis will include quantitative plaque volumes and composition, assessment of high-risk plaque features and evaluation of pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation (PCAT). Cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers will be assessed at baseline and after 24 months. Follow-up evaluations are scheduled at 12 and 24 months to reassess periodontal status. In addition, changes in plaque burden will be longitudinally assessed in case of clinically indicated repeat CCTA scans. The primary endpoint is the influence of periodontal treatment on cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers at 24 months. Secondary endpoints include major adverse cardiovascular events during follow-up, changes in plaque parameters and PCAT on serial CCTA, and associat

candidates.title: Cumulative cardiovascular risk factor burden is independently associated with impaired global longitudinal strain in individuals with preserved ejection fraction: a Vietnamese cross-sectional study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Global longitudinal strain (GLS) and diastolic dysfunction (DD) are sensitive markers of early myocardial remodeling in patients with cardiovascular risk factors (CRFs). This study aimed to evaluate the association of GLS and DD with the burden of CRFs.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 345 patients without known cardiovascular disease who underwent transthoracic echocardiography. Participants were stratified according to the number of CRFs (0, 1, 2, or ≥ 3), including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, chronic kidney disease and smoking. Obesity was evaluated as a covariate in regression analyses. Logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of abnormal GLS and DD.
RESULTS: GLS progressively worsened with increasing CRF burden, from - 21.1% in patients without CRFs to - 17.1% in those with ≥ 3 CRFs (p for trend < 0.001). In univariate analysis, patients with ≥ 3 CRFs were significantly more prevalent in the abnormal GLS group compared with the normal GLS group (38.1% vs. 3.1%, p = 0.001). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that male sex (aOR 4.22, 95% CI 1.22-14.66; p = 0.023), obesity grade II (aOR 6.29, 95% CI 1.22-32.42; p = 0.028), and the presence of ≥ 3 CRFs (aOR 6.18, 95% CI 1.06-35.98; p = 0.043) were independent predictors of abnormal GLS. The prevalence of DD increased from 9.3% in patients without CRFs to 61.1% in those with ≥ 3 CRFs (p for trend < 0.001). However, in multivariate analysis, only age ≥ 60 years (aOR 5.80, 95% CI 2.80-12.01; p = 0.001) and systolic blood pressure (aOR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.05; p = 0.001) were independently associated with DD, whereas CRF burden was not.
CONCLUSION: GLS deteriorates progressively with increasing CRF burden, even in individuals without overt heart disease. While DD was primarily driven by age and systolic blood pressure, impaired GLS reflected the cumulative burden of CRFs. These findings support GLS as a sensitive tool for early detection of subclinic

candidates.title: Atypical CTPA contrast timing revealing a suspected right-to-left shunt in a patient with advanced COPD and concurrent pulmonary malignancy.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoxemia in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) typically arises from ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) mismatch. However, refractory hypoxemia should raise concern for alternative mechanisms, such as intracardiac shunting. This report describes a rare presentation where a catastrophic rise in pulmonary vascular resistance-potentially driven by acute hypoxic vasoconstriction, tumor-related microvascular obstruction, or both-likely unmasked a pre-existing interatrial shunt in a patient with advanced lung disease and a concurrent pulmonary mass.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 66-year-old male with advanced COPD presented with acute dyspnea and was initially treated for an exacerbation. Despite initial improvement, he experienced abrupt, severe refractory hypoxemia 28 h post-admission, necessitating endotracheal intubation. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) excluded pulmonary embolism but revealed near-simultaneous contrast enhancement of the right and left atria before the right ventricle, alongside a left lower lobe mass. Bedside echocardiography indicated severe pulmonary hypertension and a suspected reversed interatrial shunt (Eisenmenger-like physiology). He was successfully extubated in the intensive care unit. Following a shared decision-making process where the family explicitly refused advanced mechanical interventions due to his severe comorbidities, the patient transitioned to palliative care.
CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the importance of recognizing CTPA contrast timing abnormalities ("aortic pre-opacification") as a diagnostic clue for intracardiac shunting.

candidates.title: Value of carotid shear-wave elastography combined with the coronary artery calcium score in assessing three-vessel disease in patients with coronary artery disease.
candidates.journal: The Journal of international medical research
candidates.abstract: ObjectiveThis study evaluated whether carotid elasticity parameters derived from shear-wave elastography, when combined with the coronary artery calcium score, could aid the identification of three-vessel disease.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, participants were divided into three groups according to coronary angiography findings: group A (mild lesions; n = 42; coronary artery stenosis <50%), group B (single- or double-vessel disease; n = 43; ≥50% stenosis in one or two major coronary arteries), and group C (three-vessel disease; n = 42; ≥50% stenosis in all three major coronary arteries). Carotid ultrasonography and shear wave elastography were used to assess arterial parameters and minimum, mean, and maximum elastic moduli (MEmin, MEmean, and MEmax). Coronary artery calcium score was obtained using noncontrast multislice spiral computed tomography. The Gensini score was calculated to assess the severity of coronary artery lesions.ResultsMEmin, MEmean, and MEmax were significantly higher in groups B and C than in group A (all p < 0.05). Compared with group B, group C showed significantly higher MEmin and MEmax (both p < 0.05). No significant difference in MEmean was observed between groups B and C (p > 0.05). Coronary artery calcium score increased progressively across the three groups (p < 0.05). After Bonferroni correction for multiple correlation tests, Spearman correlation analysis showed that MEmin (r = 0.278, adjusted p = 0.006), MEmean (r = 0.322, adjusted p < 0.001), MEmax (r = 0.312, adjusted p = 0.001), and coronary artery calcium score (r = 0.449, adjusted p < 0.001) remained positively correlated with the Gensini score. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that, in a model including age, hypertension, diabetes, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, MEmax, and coronary artery calcium score, both MEmax (odds ratio per 10 kPa increase = 2.325, 95% confidence interval: 1.399-3.863, p = 0.001) and coronary artery calcium score (odds ratio p

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Valvular Heart Disease: Imaging, Quantification, Risk Prediction, and Potential Clinical Decision Support.
candidates.abstract: Valvular heart disease (VHD) affects a substantial proportion of the population and remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite advances in surgical and transcatheter therapies, important challenges persist. VHD remains underdiagnosed, assessment of disease severity is often variable, and the optimal timing of intervention continues to evolve. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool across the spectrum of VHD care. AI-based electrocardiogram analysis can identify both existing and future VHD, while AI-guided point-of-care ultrasound extends screening to nonspecialist settings. Across multimodality imaging, machine learning (ML) and deep learning algorithms enable automated, reproducible assessment of VHD. In echocardiography, AI supports grading of disease severity across the main valvular lesions, including Doppler interpretation and automated report generation. AI-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance facilitates automated assessment of ventricular remodeling and myocardial fibrosis, while AI-assisted cardiac computed tomography improves procedural planning for transcatheter interventions. In parallel, ML has identified distinct patient phenotypes in multiple valvular lesions with differing clinical trajectories and responses to intervention. This review summarizes current applications of AI in detection, multimodality imaging, and potential clinical decision support for VHD and discusses opportunities and challenges for integration into routine practice.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Coronary Artery Disease: From Detection to Precision Management.
candidates.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet the landscape is rapidly evolving as artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to its detection, diagnosis, and management. This review surveys the expanding role of AI across the full spectrum of CAD care. In screening, deep-learning electrocardiography and electronic health record-based digital markers enable earlier identification of clinically significant disease. In noninvasive imaging, AI-driven coronary computed tomography angiography automates calcium scoring, derives fractional flow reserve without invasive wires, and quantifies high-risk plaque features that predict incident adverse events. Within the cardiac catheterization laboratory, angiography-derived physiologic assessment and AI-guided intravascular imaging segmentation support real-time procedural decision-making. Beyond diagnosis, machine-learning models integrating multimodality imaging data improve risk stratification over conventional clinical scores, while pharmacogenomic algorithms and wearable-based digital rehabilitation platforms enable patient-centric secondary prevention. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including limited evidence from randomized trials, algorithmic bias in underrepresented populations, regulatory uncertainty surrounding software-as-a-medical-device frameworks, and the risk of clinician de-skilling. AI has the potential to act as a collaborative tool that augments-rather than replaces-physician judgment. Future directions include foundation models, multiomics integration, agentic AI workflows, and equity-centered deployment strategies to ensure that AI-driven advances benefit all individuals with CAD.

candidates.title: Incidental Ostial Band of the Left Main Coronary Artery.
candidates.abstract: We report an incidental ostial band of the left main coronary artery (LMCA), identified on coronary computed tomography angiography. A thin, linear, noncalcified band was noted within the left coronary sinus, adjacent to the LMCA ostium, confirmed on multiplanar and virtual dissection images, with no associated luminal narrowing. Such bands are exceedingly rare congenital variants, distinct from ostial ridges or atherosclerotic lesions, and may closely mimic a focal dissection flap. This case highlights the importance of recognizing this subtle entity and the value of high-resolution noninvasive imaging in its accurate characterization.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Heart Failure: Early Detection, Phenotyping, and Prognostic Modeling.
candidates.abstract: This review examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) across the heart failure (HF) continuum, with particular emphasis on patient identification and early recognition, AI-enabled electrocardiography and echocardiography, etiologic and phenotypic classification, electronic health record-based staging and risk prediction, advanced HF identification, continuous monitoring, treatment optimization, and emerging applications of agentic AI.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Congenital Heart Disease: A Roadmap.
candidates.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a lifelong condition that requires ongoing monitoring due to its heterogeneous anatomy, physiology, and clinical course. Despite major advances in diagnosis and treatment, challenges remain in early detection, risk stratification, and long-term management. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to enhance CHD care by extracting actionable insights from complex clinical data. This review examines current and emerging applications of AI in three key domains: cardiovascular imaging, wearable technologies, and clinical registries. We highlight opportunities to improve diagnosis, monitoring, and outcome prediction, while discussing important challenges related to data quality, validation, interpretability, and clinical implementation. Together, these areas illustrate both the promise and the barriers to integrating AI into CHD care.

candidates.title: Coronary Vasomotor Disorders: Focus for Internists.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary vasomotor disorders encompass a spectrum of functional and structural abnormalities involving both the epicardial coronary arteries and the coronary microcirculation. Epicardial coronary vasospasm, coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) and microvascular spasm may cause myocardial ischemia in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) and represent an important, under-recognized, diagnostic challenge in internal medicine.
PURPOSE: This review aims to provide a practical, clinically oriented framework for internists to recognize coronary vasomotor disorders in patients presenting with chest pain or myocardial injury in the absence of obstructive CAD.
CONTENT: Coronary vasomotor disorders may manifest as chronic coronary syndromes, including angina with non-obstructive CAD (ANOCA) and ischemia with non-obstructive CAD (INOCA), or as acute coronary syndromes with myocardial injury and non-obstructive CAD (MINOCA). Their clinical presentation is heterogeneous and may differ from the classical pattern of classic, effort-related angina. Rest or nocturnal/early-morning chest pain, prolonged or fluctuating symptoms, incomplete response to nitrates, dyspnea, fatigue, weakness and reduced exercise tolerance should raise suspicion, particularly in women when coronary computed tomography angiography or invasive angiography demonstrate non-obstructive CAD. Non-invasive investigations may provide evidence of ischemia or CMD but may have limited ability to identify transient coronary vasomotor abnormalities, particularly epicardial or microvascular spasm. Accordingly, selected patients should undergo invasive coronary functional assessment combining coronary physiology with acetylcholine provocation testing to identify the underlying endotype.
CONCLUSIONS: Coronary vasomotor disorders, including epicardial vasospasm, coronary microvascular dysfunction and microvascular spasm, are important causes of myocardial ischemia in the absence of obstruc

candidates.title: Etoposide-induced angina in a patient with small cell lung carcinoma: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of cisplatin and etoposide is a standard therapy for small cell lung cancer; however, ischemic heart disease is a known complication. We report a rare case of effort angina pectoris that worsened during initial treatment of small cell lung cancer with etoposide.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 73-year-old Asian male was admitted to our hospital with effort angina. Coronary angiography revealed severe stenosis with significant calcification of the proximal right coronary artery. Computed tomography revealed a 21-mm-sized nodule in the right upper lobe and hilar lymphadenopathy suggestive of lung cancer. The patient underwent thoracoscopic wedge resection before coronary revascularization, and intraoperative findings indicated a small cell carcinoma with hilar lymph node metastases. Early postoperative definitive treatment consisting of chemotherapy with cisplatin plus etoposide and accelerated hyperfractionated radiation was planned. During the first chemotherapy session, on postoperative day 7, the patient complained of chest pain, and an electrocardiogram showed slight ST depression in leads V5 and V6 while receiving etoposide; nitroglycerin improved his symptoms. Although treatment was resumed with the administration of nicorandil the next day, the same symptoms were observed during the infusion of etoposide. Accordingly, chemoradiation therapy was suspended and revascularization of the right coronary artery was performed. Etoposide and cisplatin were readministered 3 days after revascularization, without any chest symptoms.
CONCLUSION: Chemotherapy for malignant tumors carries the risk of progression to coronary artery disease. To prevent serious ischemic events, sufficient discussions between oncologists and cardiologists and careful observation of chest symptoms are needed.

candidates.title: Deep learning denoising and deep learning-augmented contrast enhancement improve ultra-high-resolution photon-counting-detector CCTA image quality.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Ultrahigh-resolution (UHR) coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) using a photon-counting detector (PCD) provides excellent spatial resolution but is limited by increased image noise. We evaluated whether deep learning (DL)-based denoising and contrast enhancement can further improve UHR-CCTA image quality.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: UHR-CCTA scans from 25 patients with coronary artery disease were retrospectively analyzed. Images were reconstructed at 0.2-mm slice thickness without and with quantum iterative reconstruction (QIR, Qoff-Q4), and subsequently processed using a DL tool for denoising and increasing iodine contrast enhancement. Subjective image quality (sharpness, noise, vessel wall delineation, and overall quality) was assessed by three radiologists using a 5-point Likert scale. Objective analysis included signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and coronary wall sharpness. Differences between image sets were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
RESULTS: DL-based CCTA demonstrated significantly superior subjective image quality across all parameters compared to standard reconstructions, with an overall median image quality ([interquartile interval, IQR]: 4 [3-5] versus 2 [2-3], p < 0.001). SNR and CNR were significantly higher for DL-based CCTA across all QIR levels (all p < 0.001). The highest values were observed for DL-based CCTAQ4 versus UHR-CCTAQ4 (SNR: 258.0 ± 147.5 versus 145.2 ± 50.1; CNR: 25.8 ± 17.1 versus 11.1 ± 4.5; both p < 0.001). Coronary wall sharpness was improved for DL-based CCTA for Q1-4 (all p < 0.027).
CONCLUSION: DL-based denoising and iodine contrast enhancement effectively reduce noise and improve anatomic detail in UHR-CCTA, providing incremental value beyond vendor-specific reconstruction, particularly at high QIR strength levels.

candidates.title: [Predictors of naive functional mitral regurgitation progression after isolated correction of chronic aortic regurgitation].
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify predictors of naive functional mitral regurgitation (MR) progression in patients with severe left ventricular dilatation after isolated correction of aortic valve disease.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: The study included 80 patients with left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) ≥ 250 ml due to chronic AI with functional MR. In all patients, AI was the only primary factor of left ventricular remodeling. Surgical treatment of AI was performed using the David and Bentall-DeBono techniques, as well as aortic valve replacement and isolated aortic valve leaflet repair. Functional MR was assessed using transthoracic echocardiography. We evaluated MR and potential predictors 1-10 days before surgery, 7-10 days after surgery, and at least 6 months after surgical treatment.
RESULTS: Preoperative mitral annulus diameter (MAD) ≥ 45 mm is an independent predictor of long-term MR progression with LVEDV ≥ 250 ml in all groups with (OR 1.560, CI 1.033-2.358, p=0.035). The MAD/left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD) ratio ≥ 0.539 before surgery is a significant predictor of postoperative MR progression (AUC=0.734; 95% CI: 0.562-0.905, p=0.011). The MAD/left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVESD) ratio ≥ 0.833 before surgery is a significant predictor of MR progression (AUC=0.698; 95% CI: 0.522-0.875, p=0.031).
CONCLUSION: Functional MR following chronic AI may progress after correction of aortic valve disease in patients with severe mitral annular dilatation.

candidates.title: Clinically suspected acute myocarditis with ST-segment elevation, multiorgan dysfunction, and reversible conduction disturbance in an older patient receiving maintenance hemodialysis: A case report.
candidates.abstract:
RATIONALE: ST-segment elevation and marked myocardial injury require urgent exclusion of coronary occlusion. Maintenance hemodialysis adds metabolic, volume, biomarker, and bleeding-related uncertainty.
PATIENT CONCERNS: A 70-year-old woman receiving thrice-weekly hemodialysis developed chest tightness, dyspnea, and upper abdominal pain during dialysis. She returned with recurrent symptoms, severe metabolic acidosis, lactate 21 mmol/L, ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3, and troponin I that increased from 13,019.45 to >25,000 ng/L.
DIAGNOSES: Coronary angiography showed unobstructed epicardial arteries with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction grade 3 flow. Clinically suspected acute myocarditis remained the leading working diagnosis, but cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and endomyocardial biopsy were not performed and other causes of myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries could not be definitively excluded. The course was complicated by pulmonary congestion, metabolic and volume instability, hepatic injury, suspected pancreatic involvement, gastrointestinal bleeding, and symptomatic sinus arrest.
INTERVENTIONS: Antithrombotic therapy was reassessed after angiography and withheld when bleeding developed. Early continuous venovenous hemofiltration was performed without circuit anticoagulation, with heparin reintroduced later when clinically appropriate. Continuous renal replacement therapy was used for volume, electrolyte, and acid-base support. A temporary transvenous pacemaker was implanted for telemetry-confirmed sinus arrest with a maximum pause of 8.78 seconds.
OUTCOMES: The maximum R-R interval decreased to 1.97 seconds, permitting pacemaker removal. At approximately 3 months, syncope had not recurred, but persistent atrial fibrillation, New York Heart Association class III symptoms, and an left ventricular ejection fraction of 47% indicated incomplete cardiac recovery.

candidates.title: Tirofiban combined with heparin versus heparin alone in acute coronary syndrome patients undergoing emergency PCI: A retrospective study of no-reflow and myocardial perfusion.
candidates.abstract: The no-reflow phenomenon is an important complication of emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute coronary syndrome (ACS). We examined the association between adjunctive tirofiban and in-hospital angiographic and electrocardiographic reperfusion indicators. This single-center retrospective observational study included 186 ACS patients who underwent emergency PCI between January 2021 and December 2024. According to perioperative antithrombotic treatment, patients were divided into a tirofiban plus heparin group (n = 92) and a heparin-alone group (n = 94). Because treatment assignment was nonrandom and determined by the treating interventional cardiologist, the analysis was designed to estimate associations rather than causal treatment effects. For the no-reflow outcome, a parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model adjusted for clinically relevant measured confounders, including diabetes mellitus, symptom-to-balloon time > 6 hours, high thrombus burden, and pre-PCI thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (grade/flow) (TIMI) 0-1 flow. No-reflow was recorded in 8/92 (8.7%) versus 20/94 (21.3%) patients (P = .016). Final TIMI grade 3 flow occurred in 91.3% versus 79.8% (P = .028); myocardial blush grade 2-3 in 84.8% versus 68.1% (P = .008); TIMI myocardial perfusion grade 2-3 in 82.6% versus 66.0% (P = .010); and ST-segment resolution > 70% in 65.2% versus 47.9% (P = .017). The originally reported adjusted odds ratio for no-reflow associated with tirofiban was 0.36 (95% confidence interval 0.14-0.90; P = .029). Bleeding Academic Research Consortium major bleeding occurred in 3/92 (3.3%) versus 2/94 (2.1%; P = .679); Bleeding Academic Research Consortium minor bleeding in 6/92 (6.5%) versus 5/94 (5.3%; P = .733). These small event counts do not establish comparable safety. candidates.title: Non-Invasive Myocardial Work Assessment of Subclinical Left Ventricular Dysfunction in Ankylosing Spondylitis.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease associated with increased cardiovascular risk. This study aimed to evaluate subclinical left ventricular (LV) dysfunction in patients with AS using non-invasive myocardial work analysis.
METHODS: 50 patients with AS and 44 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were enrolled. Comprehensive clinical characteristics were documented for all participants. Two dimensional dynamic images of the apical four-chamber, two chamber, and three-chamber views were collected from all subjects, with three consecutive cardiac cycles recorded for each view. LV myocardial strain parameters, including global longitudinal strain (GLS) and peak strain dispersion (PSD), as well as myocardial work indices, including global work index (GWI), and global constructive work (GCW), global wasted work (GWW), global work efficiency (GWE), were obtained and subsequently analyzed.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with AS had lower absolute GLS (18.46±2.00% vs.19.41±1.91%, p = 0.021), higher PSD ( 47 . 20 ± 13 . 25  vs .  39 . 32 ± 9 . 10  ms ,  p = 0 . 001   ) and GWW ([106.00 (68.75-140.00) vs. 61.00 (49.25-81.25) mmHg%, P < 0.001), along with lower GWI(1679.26±226.70 vs. 1780.84±209.25 mmHg%, P < 0.05) and GWE (94.08±2.68% vs. 96.32±0.93%, P < 0.001). Furthermore, PSD was positively correlated with GWW (r = 0.59, P < 0.001) and negatively correlated with GWE (r = -0.65, P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, systolic blood pressure, LV mass index, and GLS, AS remained associated with higher PSD ( p  = 0 . 007 )   , higher GWW ( P  <  0 . 001 )   , and lower GWE (P < 0.001), whereas the associations with GWI and GCW were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with AS exhibited increased LV mechanical dispersion and wasted myocardial work and reduced myocardial work efficiency. These alterations persisted after adjustment for GLS, suggesting that PSD and myocardial work analysis may provide complement

candidates.title: Identification of Regional Wall Motion Abnormalities by Emergency Physicians in Acute Coronary Syndromes: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
candidates.journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chest pain accounts for approximately six million emergency department (ED) visits annually in the United States. Early detection of acute occlusive myocardial infarction (OMI) is challenging, especially in patients without classic ST-elevation on initial electrocardiography (ECG). Regional wall motion abnormalities (RWMA) often precede ECG changes and can be sensitive indicators of acute coronary occlusion on transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). However, the accuracy of emergency physician-performed TTE for RWMA detection has not been well defined. In this review we aim to determine how accurate emergency physicians are in detecting RWMAs.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review of studies including adult ED patients who underwent cardiac ultrasound performed or interpreted by emergency physicians, with test characteristics compared to cardiology-performed or interpreted echocardiography as the reference standard. Primary outcomes were sensitivity and specificity for RWMA detection. Secondary outcomes included likelihood ratios, and area under the receiver-operator curve (AUC). Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2, and evidence certainty was evaluated using GRADE methodology.
RESULTS: The search identified 2,463 studies, of which 32 underwent full-text review; nine studies including 1,191 participants from the US, Turkey, and Iran are included. Sonographers across studies ranged from medical students and residents to fellowship-trained and senior emergency physicians with varying levels of prior ultrasound and RWMA-specific training. Pooled sensitivity and specificity for RWMA detection were 86% (95% CI, 76-93%) and 85% (95% CI, 70-94%), respectively, with an AUC of 0.918. Pooled positive and negative likelihood ratios were 5.42 (95% CI, 2.51-11.68) and 0.17 (95% CI, 0.09-0.33), respectively. Four of the nine studies were judged to have a high risk of bias in at least one domain. Substantial heterogeneity was observed in the secondary univariat

candidates.title: Characteristics of Wellens syndrome patients in acute coronary syndrome: a retrospective study.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine the prevalence, clinical characteristics, coronary angiographic patterns, and factors associated with acute heart failure among patients with Wellens syndrome in a Vietnamese acute coronary syndrome cohort.
RESULTS: Among 938 patients admitted with acute coronary syndrome, 50 patients (5.3%) fulfilled electrocardiographic criteria for Wellens syndrome. The mean age was 64.0 ± 7.8 years, and 54% were female. Cardiovascular risk factors were highly prevalent, including dyslipidemia (92%), hypertension (88%), diabetes mellitus (64%), and smoking (52%). Type B Wellens morphology was slightly more frequent than type A (52% vs. 48%). Coronary angiography demonstrated predominant involvement of the left anterior descending artery, most commonly affecting the proximal (78%) and mid (66%) segments, with multivessel disease present in 46% of patients. Acute heart failure occurred in 42% of cases. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, elevated troponin T was associated with acute heart failure (adjusted odds ratio 7.91 (95% CI 1.80-34.68), p = 0.006) and may reflect the extent of myocardial injury.

candidates.title: Comparison between angiography or intravascular imaging guided coronary rotational atherectomy.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rotational atherectomy (RA) is a cornerstone technique for the management of severely calcified coronary lesions during percutaneous coronary interventions. Although intravascular imaging (IVI) provides superior anatomical guidance, its long-term prognostic impact in RA remains underexplored.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare 12-month clinical outcomes between IVI-guided and coronary angiography (CAG)-guided RA.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis included 468 patients who underwent RA. Following 1:1 propensity score matching（PSM）, 306 patients (153 per group) were compared: IVI-guided versus angiography (CAG)-guided RA. The primary endpoint was 12-month major adverse cardiac events (MACE). A stratified Cox proportional hazards model, incorporating variables selected via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, was employed for the primary adjusted analysis to mitigate overfitting.
RESULTS: Compared with CAG guidance, IVI-guided RA was associated with the use of larger burrs and stent diameters, as well as greater contrast volume (all P<0.05). At 12 months, IVI-guided RA was associated with significantly lower rates of MACE (7.2% vs. 15.0%; P = 0.033), cardiac death (2.0% vs. 8.5%; P = 0.020), and all-cause mortality (2.6% vs. 11.8%; P<0.005). In the stratified multivariable Cox model adjusting for preoperative renal function, IVI guidance remained independently associated with a lower hazard of MACE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.42, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.20-0.86; P = 0.018).
CONCLUSIONS: In this observational study, IVI-guided RA was associated with reduced 12-month MACE and all-cause mortality compared to CAG-guided RA. These findings generate hypotheses regarding the potential role of IVI guidance in this high-risk setting and underscore the need for validation in prospective, randomised trials.

candidates.title: Low Forward Flow and Early Mortality Despite Preserved Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction After Acute Myocardial Infarction: A MIMIC-IV-Echo Cohort Study.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) guides risk assessment after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), but preserved LVEF does not ensure preserved forward flow. We examined stroke volume index (SVI) and 30-day mortality after AMI with preserved LVEF.
METHODS: Adults with a first AMI-coded hospitalization and echocardiography from 24 h before through 48 h after admission were identified in MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-Echo. Documented type 2 myocardial infarction was excluded. SVI was calculated from left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) diameter, velocity-time integral (VTI), and body surface area (BSA). Preserved LVEF was ≥50%; low flow was SVI <35 mL/m2. Modified Poisson regression estimated risk ratios (RRs); splines assessed nonlinearity.
RESULTS: Among 4,307 patients, 2,142 had preserved LVEF; 864 (40.3%) had low flow. Thirty-day mortality was 7.5% (65/864) with low flow and 4.7% (60/1,278) with normal flow. The adjusted RR was 1.65 (95% confidence interval, 1.19-2.29), but joint adjustment for shock and pre-echocardiography support yielded RR 1.31 (0.95-1.82). The association was nonlinear (P < 0.001). Spline-modeled SVI increased the C-statistic by 0.0147 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.0051-0.0290) beyond clinical variables and LVEF; after adding shock, cardiac arrest, and support to the base model, the increase was 0.0024 (-0.0012-0.0097).
CONCLUSION: Low Doppler-derived SVI identified a higher-risk preserved-LVEF phenotype, but its incremental discrimination was minimal after acute-severity information was included. The finding supports descriptive hemodynamic phenotyping rather than an AMI treatment threshold and requires external validation against Killip class and established risk scores.

candidates.title: Effects of Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair on Right Heart Dimension and Function.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) has developed as a treatment option for patients experiencing severe tricuspid regurgitation. T-TEER consistently reduces tricuspid regurgitation, but data on subsequent right heart remodeling remain limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate changes in right heart dimension and function after T-TEER using extended echocardiographic follow-up.
METHODS: The study was based on the international EuroTR (European Registry of Transcatheter Repair for Tricuspid Regurgitation), including patients undergoing T-TEER between 2016 and 2024 at 18 European centers. Eligible were patients with available baseline and follow-up (≥90 days postprocedure) echocardiographic assessment.
RESULTS: A total of 699 patients (mean age, 78±8 years; 56% women) were included in the analysis. Echocardiographic follow-up was performed at a median of 407 days (interquartile range, 205-801 days). Right heart dimensions significantly decreased: right ventricular (RV) midventricular diameter from 40.2±8.9 to 37.1±8.4 mm (P<0.001) and end-diastolic area from 28.7±9.0 to 26.2±9.6 cm2 (P<0.001). Procedural success was significantly associated with positive RV remodeling (odds ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.07-3.09]). For RV function, a decline of fractional area change from 37.8%±10.2% to 33.3%±10.1% (P<0.001), and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion from 17.4±4.7 to 16.6±4.7 mm (P<0.001) was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: In the subset of surviving patients with available echocardiographic follow-up, treatment with T-TEER led to favorable long-term changes with reduced RV dimension, associated with procedural success. RV function modestly decreased, likely reflecting normalization after volume unloading.

candidates.title: Prognostic Value of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Artery Coupling in Mitral Valve Surgery and Impact of Concomitant Tricuspid Valve Repair.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling on clinical outcomes following mitral valve surgery with specific consideration of concomitant tricuspid valve repair remains uncertain.
METHODS: A total of 214 patients who underwent mitral valve surgery and presented with moderate tricuspid regurgitation at the index procedure were included. Patients were classified after baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling (impaired versus normal). The primary study end point was a composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary study end points included all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization.
RESULTS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was observed in 112 patients (52%), while 102 patients (48%) had normal right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling. The rate of concomitant tricuspid valve repair was similar between study groups (50.0% versus 49.0%, P=0.886). Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was associated with a higher hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 2.60, 95% CI 1.32-5.14, P=0.006), heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio 3.29, 95% CI 1.27-8.54, P=0.014), and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 2.25, 95% CI 1.11-4.59, P=0.025) during follow-up. Additionally, concomitant tricuspid valve repair in patients with moderate tricuspid regurgitation was associated with a lower hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.26-0.80, P=0.007).
CONCLUSIONS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling is a predictor of adverse outcomes after mitral valve surgery. Concomitant tricuspid valve repair for moderate tricuspid regurgitation seems to be associated with improved outcomes.

candidates.title: Risk Stratification and Outcomes of Right Atrial Phasic Function in Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy: A Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Study.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy is associated with a high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (HF). However, the prognostic role of right atrial (RA) mechanics, as quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), remains largely unexplored.
METHODS: Consecutive patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy undergoing CMR between 2014 and 2021 were retrospectively included. Demographics, clinical history, and strain parameters were collected. The primary clinical end points were end-stage HF and MVA.
RESULTS: A total of 316 patients (mean age 38±15 years; 66.1% men) were included. Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years, 49 developed end-stage HF and 103 experienced MVA outcomes. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Gray models showed that impaired RA reservoir strain was an independent predictor of end-stage HF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, P<0.001) and MVA outcomes (subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99, P=0.025), with added prognostic value beyond clinical and imaging variables, improving the C-statistic to 0.84 and 0.70, respectively. Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that RA reservoir strain <18.6% was associated with higher end-stage HF risk, consistent across subgroups regardless of left ventricular involvement (both log-rank P<0.05). The association between RA reservoir strain <23.0% and MVA was significant in the overall cohort (P<0.001) and in patients without left ventricular involvement (P=0.002), but not in those with left ventricular involvement (P=0.08).
CONCLUSIONS: Lower cardiac magnetic resonance-derived RA reservoir strain was independently associated with end-stage HF and MVA in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional risk markers. These findings support RA mechanics as a potential complementary component of multichamber CMR risk assessment, pending extern

candidates.title: Comparison of Prosthetic Valve Deformation and Hemodynamic Performance Between Bicuspid and Tricuspid Aortic Valve Anatomy After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study compared prosthetic valve deformation and postprocedural hemodynamic performance between bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valve anatomy after transcatheter aortic valve replacement with the Venus-A prosthesis.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak. Computed tomography measurements included expansion ratio, ellipticity, implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening. The leaflet inflow and valve waist were collectively defined as the functional valve portion.
RESULTS: Among 212 patients (106 bicuspid and 106 tricuspid), the mean age was 74.2±7.6 years, and 43.9% were women. Patients with bicuspid anatomy had a significantly lower oversizing ratio and underwent balloon predilation and postdilation more frequently than those with tricuspid anatomy. Residual transvalvular gradients were higher with bicuspid than tricuspid anatomy (12.0 [interquartile range, 8.2-17.0] versus 10.0 [7.2-14.0] mm Hg; P=0.014), whereas moderate to severe paravalvular leak did not differ significantly. Prosthetic ellipticity was greater in bicuspid anatomy, but expansion ratios, including those within the functional valve portion, did not differ significantly. Implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening incidence also did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSIONS: Following Venus-A implantation, bicuspid anatomy was associated with greater prosthetic ellipticity and higher residual gradients, despite no significant difference in prosthetic expansion.

candidates.title: Benchmarking metabolic surrogate indices against body mass index for left atrial diameter in atrial fibrillation: a two-cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic surrogate indices are increasingly used in atrial fibrillation (AF), but several algebraically incorporate body mass index (BMI). We examined whether their associations with left atrial diameter (LAD) provide information beyond a simple anthropometric benchmark.
METHODS: We analyzed 788 patients in a primary AF cohort and 813 in a replication cohort. Seven prespecified metabolic surrogate indices were compared with BMI using harmonized linear models. We evaluated adjusted associations and incremental R² (ΔR²), partitioned shared and unique ΔR² by commonality analysis, and quantified BMI-index ΔR² differences by paired bootstrap resampling. Sensitivity analyses addressed body-size indexing, additional height/BSA covariate adjustment, AF-phenotype stratification, and covariate specification.
RESULTS: Indices without BMI in their formulas-TyG, TG/HDL-C, TG/G, and CHG-added little ΔR² in either cohort (all <0.4 percentage points). SPISE, TyG-BMI, and METS-IR contributed 5.66, 4.79, and 4.45 percentage points in the primary cohort and 3.57, 3.51, and 3.35 percentage points in the replication cohort, versus 6.23 and 4.29 percentage points for BMI. Most ΔR² of the BMI-containing indices was shared with BMI, whereas index-unique components were small. Bootstrap comparisons supported numerically similar or greater ΔR² for BMI, although confidence intervals did not uniformly exclude zero. Height-adjusted raw-LAD models preserved the comparative pattern, whereas additional BSA adjustment substantially attenuated BMI-related associations, supporting a body-size/allometric component.
CONCLUSIONS: Indices without BMI in their formulas added little ΔR² for contemporaneous LAD, whereas BMI-containing composites derived most of their ΔR² from variance shared with BMI. candidates.title: Percutaneous transvenous mitral commissurotomy during pregnancy: a contemporary Southeast Asian experience.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis during pregnancy is associated with substantial maternal and fetal morbidity because physiological hemodynamic changes may precipitate heart failure and pulmonary hypertension. Percutaneous transvenous mitral commissurotomy (PTMC) is the recommended intervention for carefully selected symptomatic patients who remain refractory to medical therapy. Although PTMC during pregnancy has been widely reported, contemporary data describing procedural characteristics, radiation exposure, and maternal-fetal outcomes from Southeast Asia remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the procedural, hemodynamic, radiation, maternal, and neonatal outcomes of PTMC performed during pregnancy.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of consecutive pregnant women with rheumatic mitral stenosis who underwent PTMC at a tertiary referral center in Thailand between 2002 and 2022 according to the institutional eligibility criteria used during the study period. Given the limited sample size, all analyses were considered exploratory. Hemodynamic, echocardiographic, procedural, radiation, maternal, and neonatal outcomes were evaluated.
RESULTS: Eighteen pregnant women underwent PTMC at a mean gestational age of 24.6 ± 5.7 weeks. Procedural success was achieved in 94% of patients. Mitral valve area significantly increased from 0.98 ± 0.23 cm² to 1.50 ± 0.34 cm² (p < 0.001), while mean transmitral gradient decreased from 15.98 ± 5.97 mmHg to 7.26 ± 3.92 mmHg (p = 0.001). Mean left atrial pressure also significantly decreased from 31.94 ± 5.95 mmHg to 17.41 ± 4.29 mmHg (p < 0.001), and most patients improved from New York Heart Association functional class III-IV to class I-II (p < 0.001). Among the 12 patients with available radiation data, the median fluoroscopy time was 3.76 min and the median cumulative air Kerma was 21 mGy. candidates.title: Cardiac monitoring and incidence of cardiotoxicity cardiomyopathy among breast cancer patients undergoing anthracycline regimen chemotherapy: insight from a single centre study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anthracyclines remain a cornerstone of breast cancer therapy but carry a significant risk of cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD). This study evaluates the incidence of CTRCD in an Indonesian setting using the latest 2022 ESC Cardio-Oncology guidelines, focusing on subclinical markers such as high-sensitivity Troponin I (hs-cTnI), Global Longitudinal Strain (GLS) and Mechanical Dispersion (MD).
METHODS: This retrospective analytical cohort study involved 98 breast cancer patients treated with anthracyclines at a national referral hospital in Indonesia from July 2018 to February 2020. Clinical assessments, hs-cTnI, and echocardiography (LVEF, GLS, and MD) were performed at baseline, 1, 3, and 6 months. CTRCD was defined per the 2022 ESC criteria.
RESULTS: CTRCD occurred in 74.5% of patients, predominantly as asymptomatic mild cases (63.26%). While symptomatic CTRCD was relatively low (7.14%), asymptomatic dysfunction was detected as early as one-month post-chemotherapy. A significant progressive decline was observed in LVEF (68.2 ± 6.2% to 61.3 ± 8.8%, p < 0.001) and GLS (-19.7 ± 2.9% to -17.1 ± 3.5%, p < 0.001). Notably, mechanical dispersion significantly increased over time (p = 0.029), and median hs-cTnI surged from 1.6 ng/L to 82.2 ng/L (p < 0.001) by month 6.
CONCLUSION: The high incidence of asymptomatic CTRCD underscores the inadequacy of relying on clinical symptoms alone. Integration of hs-cTnI, GLS, and mechanical dispersion monitoring is may be essential for early detection and enables timely cardioprotective intervention.

candidates.title: Importance of Angina Pectoris by Coronary Artery Disease Severity.
candidates.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Angina pectoris remains a common clinical manifestation, but contemporary population-based data on its long-term prognostic significance are limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term importance of angina pectoris in association with coronary artery disease (CAD) severity determined by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) in a general population.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This population-based cohort study included participants from the Swedish Cardiopulmonary Bioimage Study who had completed the Rose Questionnaire and underwent valid CCTA from November 2013 to October 2018, excluding participants with prior myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure, or coronary revascularization. Follow-up continued through September 2024. Data analyses were conducted between August 2025 and January 2026.
EXPOSURES: Angina (defined by the Rose Questionnaire) and CAD (categorized as no findings, nonobstructive CAD [<50% stenosis], or obstructive CAD [≥50% stenosis]) according to CCTA findings.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was MI or coronary death. The secondary outcome was major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as MI, coronary revascularization, heart failure hospitalization, or death from coronary disease or heart failure. Associations were evaluated using Cox regression with sequential multivariable adjustment and stratification by CAD category and presented as hazard ratios (HRs).
RESULTS: This study included 24 176 individuals (median [IQR] age, 57 [54-61] years; 12 225 female [50.6%]; 1615 with hyperlipidemia [6.8%]; 4374 with hypertension [18.3%]; 703 with diabetes [2.9%]). Angina was present in 720 participants (3.0%). During a median (IQR) follow-up of 7.7 (6.9-8.6) years, 293 primary events occurred. Angina was associated with a higher incidence of MI or coronary death compared with no angina (21 participants [2.9%] vs 272 participants [1.2%]; HR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.60-3.90).
