candidates.title: Pulmonary thromboembolism with prolonged pulmonary infarction during intensive decongestion for severe heart failure: A case report.
candidates.abstract:
RATIONALE: Pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) may be overlooked in acute decompensated heart failure because dyspnea, hypoxemia, pleural effusion, and pulmonary infiltrates can mimic refractory congestion. Extensive PTE with pulmonary infarction during intensive decongestion in severe heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is rarely described.
PATIENT CONCERNS: A 50-year-old woman without prior cardiovascular disease presented with several weeks of progressive dyspnea, severe orthopnea, pulmonary edema, pleural effusions, and an oxygen requirement of 5 L/min.
DIAGNOSES: Echocardiography showed a severely dilated left ventricle and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25%, consistent with nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy. After a cumulative negative fluid balance of 12 L over 48 hours, hypoxemia worsened despite improved congestion. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography confirmed extensive acute PTE with pulmonary infarction.
INTERVENTIONS: Systemic thrombolysis with alteplase was administered, followed by unfractionated heparin and transition to a non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant. Guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF was initiated.
OUTCOMES: Hemodynamics stabilized, but parenchymal recovery was delayed. Pulmonary infarction showed minimal radiographic improvement at 2 weeks, partial improvement at 1 month, and complete resolution at 2 months. Oxygen therapy was discontinued, dyspnea improved markedly, and left ventricular ejection fraction increased to 37%.
LESSONS: PTE should be suspected when oxygenation worsens despite effective decongestion in severe HFrEF. Pulmonary infarction may require up to 2 months for complete radiographic resolution despite prompt thrombolysis and anticoagulation.

candidates.title: Relationship between coronary flow reserve and coronary calcium burden in patients with suspected coronary artery disease: A retrospective analysis.
candidates.abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) measures atherosclerotic burden, while coronary flow reserve (CFR) measures coronary vasodilator function. The study aimed to assess the relationship between CAC burden and CFR and to define clinical and imaging factors independently associated with compromised CFR. This retrospective observational study included 467 patients aged 16 to 93 years who underwent clinically indicated CAC assessment and quantitative ^82Rb PET/computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging with pharmacological vasodilator stress between January 2024 and June 2026. CAC was categorized as 0, 1 to 99, 100 to 399, or ≥400 Agatston units. CFR was calculated as stress-to-rest myocardial blood flow, with CFR < 2.0 defined as impaired. Correlation, multivariable linear regression, and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Mean age was 61.8 ± 13.7 years, with 59.1% male participants; 39.6% had impaired CFR. Mean CFR decreased progressively from 2.43 ± 0.62 in patients with CAC = 0 to 1.57 ± 0.47 with CAC ≥ 400 (P for trend < .001), while impaired CFR increased from 25.9% to 67.1%. CFR was inversely correlated with CAC (Spearman r = -0.43, P < .001). After adjustment, CAC 100 to 399 and ≥400 remained independently associated with impaired CFR (adjusted OR 2.41, 95% confidence interval 1.35 to 4.30 and OR 3.28, 95% confidence interval 1.72 to 6.25, respectively). Age, diabetes, and abnormal myocardial perfusion were also independently associated with impaired CFR. CAC was independently associated with lower CFR and a higher prevalence of impaired CFR. This association remained after multivariable adjustment, and also on sensitivity analysis, indicating that these 2 approaches to coronary assessment complement each other. The results of this study are presented as associations, due to its retrospective cross sectional design.

candidates.title: Association of the Neutrophil-to-HDL-C Ratio With Coronary Artery Disease and Coronary Stenosis Severity in Patients Undergoing Coronary Angiography: Results From the Iranian-CARDIO Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Inflammation plays a central role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis, with neutrophils and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) being key components. The neutrophil-to-HDL-C ratio (NHR) has recently been proposed as a potential biomarker of CAD. This study is aimed at evaluating the association of NHR with the presence and angiographic severity of CAD.
METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional study was conducted on 250 patients who were referred for suspected CAD and underwent coronary angiography at Afshar Hospital, Yazd, Iran. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected, and the severity of CAD was assessed using the Gensini score. NHR was calculated as the neutrophil count (×103/μL) divided by HDL-C (mmol/L). Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed; the model adjusted for age, sex, smoking, body mass index, and blood pressure (Model III) was designated as the primary model, and a fully adjusted model (Model IV) served as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: The findings showed that patients with CAD had a significantly higher NHR than patients without CAD (3.9 ± 1.8 vs. 3.1 ± 1.28, p = 0.001). NHR increased across Gensini score tertiles (p = 0.04). In the primary adjusted model, each 1-SD increase in NHR was independently associated with CAD (OR = 2.01, 95% CI 1.28-3.14; p = 0.002) and a high Gensini score (OR = 1.56, 95% CI 1.14-2.12; p = 0.005). Bootstrap resampling (1000 replicates) confirmed the stability of these estimates. These findings were consistent in the fully adjusted model (OR = 2.31 and 1.62, respectively). NHR showed only modest discriminative ability for CAD (AUC = 0.638) and a high Gensini score (AUC = 0.620).
CONCLUSION: NHR was independently associated with the presence and severity of CAD in patients referred for coronary angiography. However, its discriminativ

candidates.title: Postoperative complications from alcohol use disorder in an adult congenital heart disease patient: a case report emphasizing the role of high-complexity congenital centers.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Superior sinus venous atrial septal defect (SVASD) associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return (PAPVR) is a rare congenital heart disease that is predominantly diagnosed and surgically treated in childhood; however, sometimes the diagnosis is delayed and requires intervention in adulthood.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 69-year-old patient presented to the adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) clinic due to shortness of breath and recurrent syncopal episodes and was found to have significant right ventricular enlargement by echocardiogram of undetermined cause. Cardiac CT detected a large SVASD with PAPVR that required surgical intervention. The postoperative course was complicated by delirium tremens.
CONCLUSIONS: ACHD patients often have many comorbidities that are not commonly seen in the pediatric population. Because of this, it is of utmost importance that pediatric surgical centers offering procedures for ACHD patients have established protocols to manage these comorbidities postoperatively, including substance withdrawal symptoms.

candidates.title: Single-stage repair of tetralogy of Fallot with partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection in an adult: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) with partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection (PAPVC) is rare and may be missed preoperatively, which may produce persistent right heart volume overload and contribute to right ventricular dilatation and dysfunction after TOF repair. Reports of this combination in adults with unrepaired TOF remain limited.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 24-year-old woman with congenital heart disease diagnosed in childhood presented with exertional fatigue and dyspnea relieved by squatting. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated TOF, a superior sinus venosus atrial septal defect, and incomplete visualization of the pulmonary veins. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) with three-dimensional reconstruction confirmed anomalous drainage of the right upper pulmonary vein into the superior vena cava (SVC). Single-stage repair was successfully performed, comprising TOF repair, a modified Warden procedure, and tricuspid valvuloplasty. Central venous pressure was 9 mmHg postoperatively, with no rhythm disturbance. Short-term follow-up indicated unobstructed venous pathways, with no residual intracardiac shunting, normal left ventricular systolic function, and no rhythm abnormalities.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of careful preoperative assessment of pulmonary venous anatomy in TOF. Single-stage repair was feasible and can achieve a favorable short-term outcome.

candidates.title: Prognostic impact of the right-to-left atrial volume index ratio on mortality and length of stay in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial remodeling is a key mechanism influencing prognosis in cardiovascular diseases [1]. This study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of the right-to-left atrial volume index ratio (RAVI/LAVI) for 2-month all-cause mortality and length of hospital stay in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective observational study, a total of 267 hospitalized patients were included. Patients were stratified into two groups according to the median RAVI/LAVI ratio (median value = 0.78) (below-median vs. above-median). Clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic variables were compared between groups. The primary endpoint was 2-month all-cause mortality after CABG, and the secondary endpoint was length of hospital stay. Predictors of mortality were evaluated using logistic regression analysis.
RESULTS: Mortality was significantly higher in the high RAVI/LAVI group (35.2% vs. 12.8%, p < 0.001), and the length of hospital stay was markedly longer (24.9 days vs. 11.4 days, p < 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, the RAVI/LAVI ratio remained an independent predictor of mortality (OR 6.67; 95% CI 1.96-22.73; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: The RAVI/LAVI ratio demonstrates a strong and independent association with mortality and length of hospital stay. This ratio may represent a practical and robust echocardiographic marker for risk stratification in vascular and cardiac patients.

candidates.title: Beyond the Stethoscope: Artificial Intelligence for Heart Failure Diagnosis and Phenotyping.
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping cardiovascular medicine by transforming routinely collected clinical data into tools for earlier disease detection and more precise phenotyping. Heart failure (HF) represents a particularly compelling opportunity for AI-driven innovation, as many patients with structural heart disease remain unrecognized and traditional diagnostic frameworks often fail to capture disease heterogeneity. AI-enabled electrocardiogram (ECG) models, including EchoNext and PRESENT-SHD, highlight the potential for scalable opportunistic screening strategies for structural heart disease. Multimodal approaches, using ECGs and echocardiograms, are enabling earlier recognition of specific HF phenotypes, such as transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Successful implementation of these technologies will require prospective evaluation, thoughtful workflow integration, and responsible deployment. Early-career cardiologists are uniquely positioned to lead this transformation of AI in clinical medicine, ensuring that AI serves as a tool to augment clinical reasoning and ultimately advances more personalized, patient-centered cardiovascular care.

candidates.title: Automated Deep Learning Pipeline for Characterizing Left Ventricular Diastolic Function.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD) is most commonly evaluated by echocardiography. However, without a sole identifying metric, LVDD is assessed by a diagnostic algorithm relying on secondary characteristics that is laborious and has the potential for interobserver variability.
METHODS: To characterize concordance in clinical evaluations of LVDD, we evaluated historical echocardiogram studies at 2 academic medical centers for variability between clinical diastology reported by clinicians and the 2016 and 2025 American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) guidelines. We developed a workflow of 8 deep learning (DL) models trained on over 155,000 studies to automate LVDD assessment. Model performance was evaluated on held-out test sets from 3 academic centers.
RESULTS: In 592 studies from Cedars-Sinai Medical Center (CSMC), DL demonstrated 80.4% agreement and a weighted Cohen kappa of 0.62 with the 2016 ASE guideline assessment. In contrast, the CSMC clinician evaluation had 52.2% agreement and a kappa of 0.46 with the 2016 guidelines. In the Stanford Healthcare (SHC) cohort of 1572 studies, DL had 66.7% agreement and a kappa of 0.33 with the 2016 guidelines vs clinical diastology, with 32.7% agreement and a kappa of 0.14. Our DL workflow showed strong concordance with the 2025 guidelines, with agreements of 81.8% in CSMC and 68.1% in SHC. In a third validation cohort of 204 studies from the University of Chicago, DL had 34.3% agreement with the 2025 guidelines.
CONCLUSIONS: Evaluating LVDD has high heterogeneity. We developed DL measurement-driven diastolic dysfunction, a pipeline of models that automates the clinical workflow of grading LVDD and can contribute to improved diagnosis of heart failure.

candidates.title: Volumetric Quantification of Retinal Ischemic Perivascular Lesions (RIPLs) in Coronary Artery Disease.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPLs) have been reported as correlates of several systemic conditions. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, number, area, and volume of RIPLs and to evaluate their association with coronary artery disease (CAD) using a contemporary imaged coronary angiography (CA) cohort.
METHODS: CA patients were imaged using an SS-OCTA device during the same visit. Structural volumes comprising 500 B-scans were pixel-wise annotated by three graders. RIPLs were quantified by presence, count, area and volume for the first time. CAD severity was assessed using the Gensini score (GS). Associations between RIPL metrics and CAD were analyzed using generalized estimating equation models. Multivariable and age and sex adjusted models were calculated. Multiple testing corrections were applied to primary analyses.
RESULTS: RIPLs were detected in 38.0% of eyes. In models with the Gensini score (GS) as outcome, RIPL metrics showed weak and inconsistent trends and were not statistically significant, especially after adjustment. The GS showed no significant associations with RIPL presence (β = 0.132, P = 0.102), area (β = 0.173, P = 0.093), count (β = 0.023, P = 0.165), or volume (β = 0.240, P = 0.085) either. Cardiovascular risk factors were not independently associated with RIPL metrics. Those negative findings remained consistent in sensitivity analyses using the SYNTAX II and SCORE2.
CONCLUSIONS: In this contemporary coronary angiography cohort with high-density OCT imaging, RIPL burden was not significantly associated with CAD and no robust or proportional association with CAD severity was found. In this work, no other disease specific associations could be established.

candidates.title: Influence of diabetes mellitus on dapagliflozin response after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR): insights from the DAPA-TAVI trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The DAPA-TAVI trial demonstrated that dapagliflozin reduced the composite of all-cause mortality or worsening heart failure (HF) at 1 year in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with prior HF. Whether the magnitude of this benefit differs according to diabetes mellitus (DM) status remains uncertain.
METHODS: This pre-specified subgroup analysis of the multicenter randomized DAPA-TAVI trial conducted at 39 centers in Spain, which enrolled 1222 patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVR with prior HF and at least one high-risk condition. Patients were stratified by the presence or absence of DM. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or worsening HF at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included the individual components of the primary endpoint, cardiovascular death, and safety outcomes. Cox proportional-hazards models adjusted for age, sex, coronary artery disease, baseline ejection fraction and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate were used to estimate treatment effects.
RESULTS: Among 1222 patients, 537 (43.9%) had DM. In patients with DM, dapagliflozin significantly reduced the primary endpoint compared with standard care (15.2% vs. 22.7%; HR 0.580; 95% CI 0.389-0.866; p = 0.008; number needed to treat [NNT] = 11), driven primarily by fewer worsening HF events. In patients without DM, the reduction was numerically lower and non-significant (15.0% vs. 18.0%; HR 0.814; 95% CI 0.560-1.183; p = 0.280; NNT = 32). Genital infections were more frequent with dapagliflozin in patients with DM, whereas symptomatic hypotension was more common in those without DM. No significant differences in serious adverse events were observed in either subgroup. No statistically significant interactions between DM status and treatment effect were observed for the primary or secondary endpoints.
CONCLUSIONS: In this pre-specified subanalysis of the DAPA-TAVI trial, dapagliflozin significantly reduced the risk of

candidates.title: Incomplete Shone's complex as a rare cardiac manifestation of Coffin-Lowry syndrome: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coffin-Lowry syndrome is a rare X-linked genetic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the RPS6KA3 gene, characterized by distinctive craniofacial features, skeletal abnormalities, and neurodevelopmental impairment. Although cardiac involvement has been reported in Coffin-Lowry syndrome, it most commonly manifests as cardiomyopathy or valvular insufficiency. To the best of our knowledge, Coffin-Lowry syndrome has not been associated with obstructive left-sided congenital heart diseases including an incomplete Shone's complex.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a 2-month-old boy who, on cardiac evaluation, was found to have coarctation of the aorta, a bicuspid aortic valve with severe stenosis, a parachute-like mitral valve with mild subvalvular stenosis, consistent with an incomplete Shone's complex, and marked left ventricular hypertrophy. The patient underwent successful corrective surgery for coarctation of the aorta and aortic valve stenosis, with follow-up revealing moderate residual aortic valve stenosis and mild residual valvular dysfunction. Genetic testing identified a maternally inherited microduplication of the X chromosome p22.12 region, encompassing several 5' exons of the RPS6KA3 gene.
CONCLUSIONS: This case suggests that obstructive left-sided congenital heart diseases including an incomplete Shone's complex may represent a previously unrecognized cardiac manifestations of Coffin-Lowry syndrome, thereby expanding the cardiovascular phenotype of this rare condition. Recognition of this association may have implications for early diagnosis, genetic evaluation, and long-term cardiac surveillance in affected patients.

candidates.title: Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups.
RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

candidates.title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Isolated Native Aortic Regurgitation: National Propensity-Matched Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is well established for aortic stenosis, while its application for isolated native aortic regurgitation (AR) was previously off label and technically challenging. Comparative data between TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are limited.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient characteristics and outcomes of off-label TAVR vs SAVR among patients with isolated native AR.
METHODS: Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Provider Analysis and Review database, patients ≥65 years of age who underwent TAVR or SAVR for isolated native AR (2017-2023) were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to evaluate short- and long-term outcomes. Fine-Gray models accounted for death as a competing risk, reported as subdistribution HRs (SHRs).
RESULTS: Among 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs were included, with balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 75.8 years vs 75.7 years; female sex 517 of 1,742 [29.7%] vs 528 of 1,742 [30.3%]). In the matched cohort, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P < 0.001) and lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-1.00; P = 0.048) but higher 30-day pacemaker implantation (OR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.33-2.25; P < 0.001). Through 5 years (median follow-up 2.58 years), TAVR was associated with increased repeat aortic valve replacement (SHR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.13-3.66) but similar all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.31) and heart failure-related readmission (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.98-1.21) between treatment strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization and comparable 5-year survival as SAVR, although pacemaker and long-term reinterventions rates were higher.

candidates.title: Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses.
METHODS: This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

candidates.title: Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS).
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial.
METHODS: The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed.
RESULTS: Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; Pinteraction = 0.96).

candidates.title: Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch and Patient-Centered Outcomes After TAVR.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement has been widely studied for its association with clinical outcomes, but its effect on patient-reported health status remains less defined.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between PPM severity and health status through 3-year follow-up after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SCOPE I (Safety and Efficacy of the ACURATE Neo/TF Compared to the SAPIEN 3 Bioprosthesis) randomized trial categorized patients according to PPM severity using Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Endpoints included survival and patient-reported health status, with an integrated outcome defined as being alive with good health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score ≥75 without a decline of >10 points from baseline).
RESULTS: Among 662 patients, moderate and severe PPM occurred in 184 (27.8%) and 69 (10.4%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 1 and 3 years was 7.0% and 20.5%, with no differences across PPM categories. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score was similar through 1 year but lower at 3 years in patients with severe vs no PPM (median 71.1 vs 83.9; P = 0.027). Fewer patients with severe PPM were alive with good health status at 3 years (30.6% vs 49.4%; P = 0.021). In multivariable analysis, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of the integrated outcome (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.27-0.96; P = 0.036), but this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for 30-day mitral regurgitation (OR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.30-1.15; P = 0.121).
CONCLUSIONS: Among survivors, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of good health status at 3 years. This association was attenuated after accounting for 30-day residual mitral regurgitation, suggesting a possible contributory role. Given the post hoc design, the findings are hypothesis-generating.

candidates.title: Cardiac Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The extent of cardiac damage in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with worse clinical outcomes.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the clinical impact of cardiac damage using the updated criteria incorporating the echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension.
METHODS: This post hoc subanalysis of LANDMARK trial, which randomized 768 patients with severe AS to the Myval transcatheter heart valve (THV) series or to contemporary THVs (Sapien and Evolut series), used updated cardiac damage classification: stage 0, no cardiac damage; stage 1, left ventricular damage; stage 2, left atrial or mitral valve damage; stage 3, pulmonary artery or tricuspid valve damage; and stage 4, right ventricular damage. The impact of cumulative cardiac damage, defined as meeting all criteria for stages 1 to 4, was also assessed. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Cardiac damage stages were assessed in 596 patients (stage 0, n = 36; stage 1, n = 88; stage 2, n = 284; stage 3, n = 84; stage 4, n = 104), with a mean age of 80.2 (5.7) years and a mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score of 3.3% (2.4%). One-year mortality was 0%, 1.1%, 4.7%, 7.2%, and 20.4% in stages 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (log-rank P < 0.001). The area under the curve for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.739. Patients with cumulative cardiac damage had the highest mortality (23.6%). In the multivariable analysis, stage 4 was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: The updated cardiac damage staging stratified 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, highlighting the importance of comprehensive echocardiographic assessment in severe AS. (LANDMARK Trial: a Randomised Controlled Trial of Myval THV [LANDMARK]; NCT04275726).

candidates.title: Valvular Shock in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit: Perioperative Care for Transcatheter Valve Interventions.
candidates.abstract: Valvular heart disease is an uncommon but high-risk cause of cardiogenic shock requiring rapid, multidisciplinary management aimed at bridging patients to definitive surgical or transcatheter valve intervention. Early comprehensive Doppler echocardiography is essential, as clinical signs may be subtle. Distinguishing decompensated chronic valvular disease from acute unstable lesions guides urgency and treatment strategy. Medical stabilization and mechanical circulatory support vary markedly between stenotic and regurgitant lesions, and standard shock therapies may be harmful in specific contexts. Transcatheter approaches are preferred when feasible, though their expanding use introduces added complexity in cardiac intensive care.

candidates.title: Coronary Artery Revascularization in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
candidates.abstract: Patients with concomitant severe aortic stenosis and significant coronary artery disease present a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge in clinical practice. There are no clear-cut guidelines as to the timing of revascularization in these patients who are referred for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). This article aims to show that in patients without high-grade proximal coronary artery disease, revascularization after TAVR is safe, feasible, and practical. Additionally, the use of preoperative TAVR computed tomographic angiography might be used in both intermediate and high-risk patients rather than invasive coronary angiography to assess for significant proximal coronary artery disease to help guide the timing of revascularization.

candidates.title: Coronary Angiography in the Evaluation of Systolic Heart Failure.
candidates.abstract: The review discusses angiographic and hemodynamic features of invasive and computed tomography coronary angiography, which inform diagnosis, prognosis, and coronary revascularization in patients with systolic heart failure.

candidates.title: Regression patterns of giant coronary artery aneurysms in children with kawasaki disease: a retrospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To characterise post-peak regression of giant coronary artery aneurysms (GCAA) across severity groups in children with Kawasaki disease (KD) and examine factors associated with regression. This retrospective cohort included 146 children with KD-associated GCAA admitted to Beijing Children's Hospital between April 2016 and September 2025. Serial echocardiographic measurements were used to identify the retrospectively observed peak patient-level coronary Z score. Cumulative regression from the observed peak to Z scores < 10, < 5 and < 2.5 was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Cox models examined factors associated with regression to Z < 5. Patients were grouped by peak Z score: 10 to < 20 (n = 104), 20 to < 30 (n = 24) and ≥ 30 (n = 18). The observed peak occurred at a median of 30.0 days after disease onset. Five-year cumulative regression estimates to Z < 10 were 81.2%, 56.5% and 0%, respectively; estimates to Z < 5 were 55.6%, 13.5% and 0%. Older age, higher peak Z score and more affected coronary segments were independently associated with a lower regression hazard to Z < 5.
CONCLUSION: Post-peak regression differed across GCAA severity groups. Older age, higher peak Z scores and greater coronary segment involvement were associated with a lower hazard of regression to Z < 5. No regression was observed during available follow-up in the small subgroup with peak Z scores ≥ 30.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Giant coronary artery aneurysms after Kawasaki disease regress less frequently than smaller aneurysms and require long-term surveillance. • Aneurysm severity is associated with subsequent coronary outcomes.
WHAT IS NEW: • Post-peak regression differed across peak Z-score groups and according to thresholds of  <10, <5 and <2.5. • Greater segment involvement was associated with less frequent regression to Z <5.

candidates.title: The diagnostic value of residual cholesterol inflammatory index for coronary artery disease severity in patients with premature coronary artery disease undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the diagnostic value of the Residual Cholesterol Inflammatory Index (RCII) for assessing coronary artery disease severity in patients with premature coronary artery disease (PCAD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and to provide evidence for clinical risk stratification and individualized treatment.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on 351 patients diagnosed with PCAD who underwent PCI at Nantong First People's Hospital between January 2024 and December 2025. Patients were divided into four groups (low, medium, high, and extremely high RCII) based on RCII quartiles. Baseline characteristics, laboratory parameters, and coronary angiography data were collected. Coronary lesion severity was evaluated using the Gensini score. Associations between RCII and coronary lesion severity were analyzed using the Kruskal‑Wallis H test, χ² test, multiple linear regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.
RESULTS: With the increase in RCII levels, the Gensini score, the rate of three-vessel coronary artery disease, and the incidence of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in PCAD patients undergoing PCI increased significantly (all P < 0.001). Multiple linear regression analysis, after adjustment for traditional cardiovascular risk factors, showed that RCII exhibited a significant non-linear (inverted U-shaped) association with Gensini score (P for nonlinearity < 0.001), with a positive linear relationship predominantly observed in the low-to-moderate RCII range (≤ 40, accounting for 94% of the population) (unstandardized regression coefficient B = 0.52, 95% confidence interval 0.338-0.701, P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis revealed a significant inverted U-shaped nonlinear association between RCII and Gensini score (P for nonlinearity < 0.001), with an inflection point threshold of approximately 40. candidates.title: Lactate-right ventricular discordance patterns and mortality in critical illness.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serum lactate and echocardiographic assessment are both central to hemodynamic evaluation in the ICU, yet their combined phenotypic information remains unexplored. We hypothesized that cross-classifying patients by lactate level and right ventricular (RV) function identifies clinically coherent classification groups with differential outcomes.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using MIMIC-IV v2.2 linked with MIMIC-IV-ECHO v1.0, with supportive external assessment in the eICU Collaborative Research Database. Adult ICU patients with transthoracic echocardiography and lactate measured within ± 6 h were classified by lactate (< 2 vs. ≥ 2 mmol/L) and qualitative RV function. Logistic models used patient-clustered robust standard errors; a sensitivity analysis retained only the earliest eligible observation per patient. Incremental value was assessed by adding RV dysfunction to a clinical model containing continuous lactate.
RESULTS: Among 6,228 observations from 4,965 patients (median age 66 years; 57.8% male; 30.9% hospital mortality), mortality increased from 18.8% in Low-Lactate/Preserved-RV to 47.2% in High-Lactate/RV-Dysfunction. Associations persisted with patient-clustered inference, first-day SOFA adjustment, and restriction to one observation per patient. Adding RV dysfunction to a clinical model containing continuous lactate produced a small improvement in AUC (0.758 to 0.761; ΔAUC 0.003, patient-bootstrap 95% CI 0.001-0.006). RR-based RERI was 0.070 (95% CI - 0.177 to 0.284). In 43,466 eICU stays with observed hospital outcome, diagnosis-coded RV disease reproduced the mortality ordering; aligned adjusted ORs were 2.01, 3.01, and 5.87 across the non-reference groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Lactate-RV cross-classification identifies clinically coherent groups with graded mortality in ICU patients selected for echocardiography. RV assessment adds statistically detectable but modest prognostic information beyond continuous lactate and clinical covariates. The

candidates.title: Cardioprotective Effects of Low-Dose Bisoprolol Against Anthracycline-Induced Subclinical Cardiotoxicity in Breast Cancer: A Triple-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial Using Advanced Echocardiographic Parameters.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anthracyclines are cornerstone agents in breast cancer chemotherapy. However, they can cause dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, potentially impairing long-term cardiac function. Beta-blockers have demonstrated cardioprotective effects. However, evidence regarding bisoprolol, particularly using comprehensive echocardiographic evaluations, remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the cardioprotective effects of low-dose bisoprolol against anthracycline-induced subclinical cardiac dysfunction in patients with breast cancer.
METHODS: This triple-blind, randomized controlled trial was conducted in Isfahan, Iran, between January and December 2023. Eligible women with locally advanced breast cancer receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy were randomized to bisoprolol (2.5 mg/day) or a placebo. Cardiac function was assessed at baseline, mid-treatment, and the end of treatment during a 6-month follow-up period. The evaluated echocardiographic parameters included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular end-diastolic and end-systolic dimensions (LVEDD, LVESD), left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), global longitudinal strain (GLS), and tricuspid annular systolic excursion (TAPSE). Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS software (version 25.0). Continuous variables were analyzed using paired or independent-samples t tests, and categorical variables were analyzed using the Chi square test. Statistical significance was defined as P<0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 50 patients completed the trial (25 in the bisoprolol group and 25 in the placebo group). LVEF remained stable in both groups. Compared with the placebo group, bisoprolol demonstrated significantly more favorable structural and functional changes, including a reduction in LVEDD (mean change=-0.172 cm; 95% CI=-0.343 to -0.001; P=0.049), LVESD (mean change=-0.156 cm; 95% CI=-0.295 to -0.172; P=0.029), and LVEDV (mean change=-7.920 mL; 95% CI=-15.174 to -0.666; P=0.033); improve

candidates.title: The prognostic role of echocardiographic parameters in ischemic stroke patients with atrial fibrillation.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concomitant cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) in stroke patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with an unfavourable outcome, but the additional prognostic value of echocardiographic parameters remains unclear.
METHODS: We included consecutive patients with recent AF-associated ischemic stroke (IS) or transient ischemic attack (TIA) who underwent echocardiography and brain MRI from the prospective Novel Oral Anticoagulants in Ischemic Stroke Patients registry. We examined associations of left atrial and ventricular echocardiographic parameters with a primary composite outcome (recurrent IS; intracranial hemorrhage, all-cause death) and its components as secondary outcomes, using unadjusted and adjusted (age, sex, modified CHA2DS2VASc-Score, hyperlipidemia, oral anticoagulation before/after stroke, MRI markers of cSVD) Cox regression. Associations between echocardiographic parameters and MRI markers of cSVD were analyzed using logistic regression.
RESULTS: We included 690 patients (median age 80, 45% female) with a total follow-up of 1084 patient-years. In unadjusted analyses, left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) was associated with the composite outcome (HR 1.44 [1.05-1.97]) and all-cause death (HR 1.95 [1.33-2.84]), neither association persisted after adjustment (aHR 1.04 [0.74-1.46]; aHR 1.29 [0.85-1.96]) Reduced ejection fraction and concentric/eccentric hypertrophy were associated with all-cause death in unadjusted analysis only. No echocardiographic parameter was associated with recurrent IS. Left atrial dilatation (OR 1.96 [1.32-2.91]) and concentric hypertrophy were associated (OR 1.68 [1.08-2.62]) with white matter hyperintensities extent in unadjusted but not in adjusted analyses.
CONCLUSION: In stroke patients with AF, structural changes of the left ventricle might be considered as indicator but not independent predictor of future cerebrovascular events or death.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT03826927.

candidates.title: Pulmonary-Cardiac Involvement in a Patient with IgA Vasculitis.
candidates.abstract: Immunoglobulin A (IgA) vasculitis (IgAV), formerly known as Henoch-Schönlein purpura, is a systemic small-vessel vasculitis caused by IgA immune-complex deposition; cardiac involvement is exceedingly rare and incompletely characterized. We describe a 41-year-old woman with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy who presented with progressive dyspnea, hemoptysis, and a painful purpuric rash and was found to have severe multisystem IgAV with simultaneous cardiac, pulmonary, renal, and cutaneous involvement. High-sensitivity troponin T peaked at 20,208 ng/L and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide at 49,428 pg/mL. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25%, diffuse mid-wall and epicardial late gadolinium enhancement with abnormal T1 and T2 values, and a 25 × 15 mm apical thrombus. Skin biopsy confirmed leukocytoclastic vasculitis and bronchoscopy confirmed diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, while multimodality imaging and a negative serologic work-up excluded cardiac sarcoidosis, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis, and anti-glomerular basement membrane disease. The patient was treated with pulse methylprednisolone, plasma exchange, rituximab, and cautious anticoagulation, with resolution of alveolar hemorrhage, a progressive decline in cardiac biomarkers, resolution of the left ventricular thrombus, and partial recovery of left ventricular systolic function. This case expands the recognized spectrum of cardiovascular involvement in adult IgAV and highlights the value of multimodality imaging and multidisciplinary management in establishing the diagnosis and guiding therapy.

candidates.title: Association of Baseline Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index with 12-month Change in Arterial Stiffness in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease: An Exploratory Single-Center Longitudinal Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) reflects arterial stiffness and is associated with the severity of coronary artery disease (CAD). Short-term change in CAVI in patients with angiographically documented CAD is poorly described. We explored whether baseline CAVI was associated with its 12-month change.
METHODS: This exploratory secondary analysis used data from a previously published single-center study, extended with 12-month follow-up. Clinically stable patients with at least 50% coronary stenosis on invasive angiography and paired CAVI measurements were included. Change in the mean of right and left CAVI (ΔCAVI-mean) was the 12-month value minus the baseline value; positive values indicate greater stiffness, and ΔCAVI-mean ≥ +0.5 defined worsening. Non-worsening was analyzed by logistic regression; post hoc analyses estimated the change expected from regression to the mean.
RESULTS: Of 157 patients, 33 (21.0%) worsened. CAVI-mean was 9.20 ± 0.80 at baseline and 9.15 ± 0.76 at 12 months (r = 0.43). Baseline CAVI-mean ≥9.0 was associated with non-worsening (odds ratio adjusted for age and sex 8.10, 95% CI 3.35-19.58). ΔCAVI-mean differed by -0.81 (95% CI -1.08 to -0.54) between patients with baseline CAVI-mean ≥9.0 and those below 9.0; regression to the mean alone predicted a difference of -0.74. ΔCAVI-mean was not related to the average of the two measurements (Oldham's method: r = -0.05; p = 0.54).
CONCLUSION: In this selected single-center CAD cohort, baseline CAVI-mean ≥9.0 was associated with lower odds of CAVI worsening over 12 months. The association was of the size expected from regression to the mean and should not be interpreted as a biological effect. The worsening threshold is not clinically validated and no clinical outcomes were assessed. Studies of change in CAVI need repeated measurements, continuous modeling, and validation in larger cohorts with clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Clinical study on feasibility and repeatability of left ventricular systolic function assessment in patients with chronic kidney disease using artificial intelligence-based automatic strain technique.
candidates.journal: Malawi medical journal : the journal of Medical Association of Malawi
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular damage is a common complication in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), and left ventricular longitudinal strain (GLS) is superior to LVEF in evaluating systolic function. However, it has not been widely adopted clinically because it requires proficiency and is time-consuming. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility, reproducibility, and predictive value of automated GLS compared with manual GLS, providing a reference for clinical evaluation and reduction of cardiovascular events in CKD patients.
METHODS: A total of 285 CKD patients (aged 52 ± 12.85) without dialysis were enrolled from Hainan Provincial People's Hospital. GLS was measured using three methods on identical apical three-, two-, and four-chamber views: (1) fully automatic GLS analyzed by machine functions, (2) semi-automatic GLS corrected by researchers, and (3) manual GLS measured by experts. Five cases were excluded due to poor image quality. Clinical outcomes were followed up by telephone and outpatient visits.
RESULTS: About 35% of automatic GLS results required manual correction, with significant differences among the three methods (P < 0.01). The correlation and consistency between semi-automatic and manual GLS were higher than those of automatic GLS (P < 0.01). During 2-year follow-up, 55 patients (19.6%) experienced cardiovascular events. Automated GLS predicted events but with lower accuracy than semi-automatic GLS. The analysis time for automatic (15.23 ± 0.75 s) and semi-automatic GLS (75.06 ± 19.01 s) was markedly shorter than manual analysis (236.81 ± 45.41 s, P < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Automated GLS assessment in CKD patients is feasible and reproducible. As some images still require manual correction, the semi-automated approach currently offers the optimal balance between efficiency and predictive value.

candidates.title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation in bicuspid aortic valve regurgitation: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for pure aortic regurgitation (AR) remains challenging, especially in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) anatomy, which has been excluded from pivotal trials of dedicated AR devices. Whether cusp-engaging devices can be used in type 1 BAV with raphe is unknown.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report two East Asian male patients (aged 72 and 62 years) with severe pure AR and type 1 bicuspid aortic valve, confirmed by transthoracic echocardiography. Pre-procedural multidetector computed tomography (MDCT) demonstrated a raphe between the left and right coronary cusps in both patients, with relatively symmetric cusp sizes and minimal calcification. Self-expanding Taurus-Trio valves (27 mm and 25 mm, respectively) were successfully implanted under monitored anaesthesia care (MAC) with TTE guidance. Post-procedural TTE showed only trivial paravalvular leak (PVL). At 6-month follow-up, MDCT confirmed favourable valve performance, with all three locators appropriately engaged within the corresponding cusps, preserved leaflet morphology and motion, and no evidence of hypo-attenuated leaflet thickening (HALT). Neither patient developed new conduction disturbances requiring permanent pacemaker implantation.
CONCLUSIONS: This case report demonstrates the feasibility of using a dedicated cusp-engaging transcatheter valve in carefully selected patients with type 1 BAV-AR, favourable cusp symmetry, and minimal calcification. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant further investigation; they should not be generalised to all BAV subtypes or to patients with significant calcification.

candidates.title: Visual Harness Scales General VLMs to Medical Images
candidates.abstract: We show that an appropriate visual harness can substantially improve the performance of general vision-language models (VLMs) across diverse medical imaging tasks. We introduce VERA, a medical visual harness that equips general VLMs with interactive visual tools and systematic diagnostic evidence management. With VERA, general VLMs interactively explore medical images and progressively acquire diagnostic evidence, which is preserved in a lossless memory for subsequent retrieval and use. After submitting an initial answer, the VLM receives an assessment of potential omissions and the reliability of identified findings. This assessment guides further image inspection and measurement, followed by answer revision in an iterative agentic loop until sufficient evidence is obtained. Across 11 tasks and four imaging modalities, VERA improves performance on all tasks with Qwen3.8-27B, with notable gains in spleen measurement (63.3% to 98.3%), renal search (57.5% to 71.2%), and pulmonary nodule detection (0.0% to 28.2%). High-capability API-based VLMs achieve even higher performance with VERA. For example, GPT-6.1 Sol improves pulmonary nodule detection from 10.8% to 69.2% with VERA, demonstrating the complementary benefits of stronger model capabilities and an effective medical visual harness. Our results highlight the potential of visual harnesses as a new paradigm for scaling general VLMs to medical imaging tasks.

candidates.title: Cardiac MRI-informed electrocardiography enables biologically grounded cardiomyopathy detection
candidates.abstract: Precise myocardial phenotyping at population scale is limited by the cost and accessibility of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), whereas electrocardiography (ECG) is widely available but reflects electrical rather than structural and functional information. Here we develop MyoECG, a cross-modal representation learning framework that distils myocardial structural and functional knowledge from CMR into standard 12-lead ECGs, enabling imaging-informed cardiomyopathy detection and subtype classification from ECGs alone. MyoECG was pretrained on 45,241 paired ECG-CMR examinations from UK Biobank and a tertiary cardiovascular centre, then developed and validated across more than 1.8 million ECGs from seven independent datasets. Across internal and external datasets spanning prevalences of 0.2-54.7%, MyoECG outperformed five pretrained ECG foundation models, with AUROCs of 0.800-0.974 for cardiomyopathy detection. In a multi-reader study of six cardiologists, MyoECG assistance improved mean sensitivity by 0.109 (95% CI, 0.041-0.175; P = 0.009) and specificity by 0.056 (95% CI, 0.004-0.108; P = 0.040). In 41,128 UK Biobank participants, the MyoECG score showed genetic correlations with cardiomyopathy (rg = 0.409) and dilated cardiomyopathy (rg = 0.371), genome-wide associations at four loci, including regions mapped to NFIA and KCNQ1, and associations with 69 circulating proteins related to myocardial stress, cell adhesion, vascular biology and metabolism. The cardiomyopathy correlation attenuated to non-significance after adjustment for 27 measured CMR traits (rg = 0.131; P = 0.143), indicating that the score captures CMR-derived information rather than dataset-specific shortcuts. MyoECG offers a scalable route to CMR-informed cardiomyopathy assessment and a strategy for transferring knowledge from resource-intensive imaging to widely deployable physiological signals.

candidates.title: Image-Condition-Controlled Diffusion Network with Large-Scale CT Pretraining for CT-Free Attenuation Correction in Dynamic Cardiac PET
candidates.abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) provides quantitative information on myocardial perfusion. In dynamic PET, tracer kinetics are tracked through a series of reconstructed time frames. Reliable attenuation correction is essential for accurate measurements. Clinical attenuation maps ($μ$-maps) are typically derived from computed tomography (CT), which adds radiation exposure and may introduce PET-CT misregistration due to respiratory and cardiac motion. Moreover, supervised CT-free methods rely on paired non-attenuation-corrected (NAC) PET and CT data, which are scarce, whereas large-scale unpaired CT data are more readily available. To address these challenges, we propose Large-scale Unpaired CT-Informed Diffusion (LUCID), a framework that transfers anatomical priors learned from 10,000 chest CT volumes in the public CT-RATE dataset to $μ$-map synthesis for dynamic cardiac $^{82}$Rb PET. First, a convolutional neural network (CNN) predicts an initial $μ$-map from each NAC PET frame. Second, the CT-pretrained diffusion backbone refines a low-noise perturbation of the CNN prediction through a single denoising step, conditioned on the corresponding NAC PET frame via ControlNet. Finally, frame-wise predictions are averaged voxel-wise to obtain the final $μ$-map. We further introduce the voxel-wise temporal standard deviation (TSD) to quantify inter-frame variability without requiring a reference $μ$-map. We evaluated LUCID on an in-house dataset of 102 patients and found that it achieved the best quantitative accuracy while maintaining competitive inter-frame consistency. Ablation studies showed that refinement with a diffusion backbone pretrained on in-house CT data from the training patients was less accurate than the CNN prediction alone, highlighting the importance of large-scale CT pretraining.

candidates.title: Automated Left Ventricle Strain Analysis from DENSE MRI
candidates.abstract: Background: Quantifying myocardial strains from Displacement ENcoding with Stimulated Echoes (DENSE) MRI provides insight into left ventricular performance, but current data processing pipelines remain limited in automation, robustness, and full left ventricle coverage. Methods: We present a fully automated framework for voxel-wise displacement and strain analysis of the left ventricle from DENSE MRI. Our method integrates a multi-channel nnU-Net model trained on both magnitude and phase images for segmentation, an automated phase unwrapping approach, an adaptation of the regularized spatiotemporal least squares (RSTLS) formulation for displacement computation, and strain calculations based on radial basis function interpolation. The proposed framework enables the estimation of displacements and strains across the left ventricle from a full stack of short-axis images. Results: Validation using a computational phantom shows the framework's overall resilience to data noise. Following computational phantom evaluation, the proposed framework is applied to analyze DENSE MRI short-axis slices acquired in forty-seven (N=47) healthy volunteers and covering the full left ventricle. Circumferential, longitudinal, and radial strains are presented throughout the cardiac cycle and at peak systole, showcasing the performance of the proposed framework. Results show that circumferential and longitudinal strains are computed accurately. However, challenges persist when estimating radial strain, especially in the subendocardial layer. A group-wise strain comparison is also performed based on volunteers' sex and age showing a significant effect of sex on circumferential and longitudinal strains. Conclusions: Overall, the proposed framework provides an automated and modular pipeline to compute displacements and strains from DENSE MR images that can be scaled and generalized toward clinical applications.

candidates.title: Foundation Model Fine-Tuning with Attention-based Multi-View Fusion for Multi-Task Cardiac Function Assessment
candidates.abstract: In cardio-oncology, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is the standard biomarker for monitoring cardiac function during cancer therapy. However, its estimation from echocardiography is highly operator dependent, and clinically meaningful declines are often detected only after myocardial injury has progressed, motivating automated methods for standardized assessment and earlier detection of LV dysfunction. To address this need, we propose a multi-task framework integrating cardiac cycle-based temporal standardization, multi-view spatiotemporal feature extraction, and joint optimization for LVEF estimation and LV dysfunction classification. Apical four- and two-chamber echocardiographic sequences are temporally standardized by sampling a clip over an estimated cardiac cycle before being processed by the EchoPrime foundation model, which is fine-tuned end-to-end within the proposed architecture. View-specific features are fused through an attention-based aggregation module to generate a patient-level embedding, from which two task-specific prediction heads estimate continuous LVEF and binary LV dysfunction. To broaden the LVEF distribution encountered during training, samples from the MIMIC-IV-ECHO dataset are incorporated using a balanced sampling strategy. Evaluated on the EchoRisk-MICCAI Challenge, our method achieves an MAE of 4.003 for LVEF estimation (Task 1) and an AUC of 0.764 for LV dysfunction detection (Task 2) on the validation set, demonstrating the effectiveness of foundation model fine-tuning with attention-based multi-view fusion for automated cardiac function assessment in cardio-oncology.

candidates.title: Learning Motion-Appearance Coupling Priors for Solving Video Inverse Problems
candidates.abstract: Reconstructing video from degraded measurements requires priors that capture both frame appearance and temporal dynamics. Many recent approaches combine pretrained image diffusion priors with motion guidance, sidestepping the costs of training large video models. Temporal consistency is often enforced via photometric losses or warping-based constraints, which implicitly assume that motion explains frame-to-frame or latent-to-latent changes up to small deviations, an assumption that fails under occlusions, lighting changes, and non-rigid deformation. In this paper, we propose to learn the coupling between motion and frame appearance as a generative prior. We learn the distribution of motion-induced appearance residuals with a conditional diffusion model and use it to regularize reconstruction in video inverse problems. Our motion-appearance prior acts as a plug-in regularizer for diffusion-based video reconstruction, preserving the benefits of image diffusion models while remaining compatible with existing appearance regularization techniques. Experiments on dynamic video inverse problems show that reconstruction with a learnt motion-appearance coupling prior outperforms photometric-consistency and noise-warping baselines, and that the approach also transfers to cardiac MRI reconstruction.

candidates.title: Mucin VNTR haplogroup associations with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis are not independent of rs35705950
candidates.abstract: BackgroundThe MUC5B promoter variant (rs35705950) is the strongest common genetic risk factor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). MUC5B and MUC5AC contain variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) regions. Long-read sequencing resolves MUC5AC into three SNP-tagged haplogroups (H1, H2, H3) differing in repeat length, and MUC5B into two (H1, H2) differing in lineage but not length. The tags correlate with rs35705950, so whether a haplogroup effect is distinguishable from the promoter variant is unclear. MethodsWe assigned MUC5AC and MUC5B haplogroups from imputed chromosome 11 array data in 771 European-ancestry IPF Job Exposures Study participants (385 cases, 386 controls). Logistic regression adjusted for age, smoking, principal components and centre, with and without rs35705950. The same models were fitted in TOPMed (1,961 cases, 3,816 controls). ResultsMUC5AC H3 and MUC5B H1 were each associated with IPF (H3 OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.26-2.09, p=1.8x10-4; MUC5B H1 OR 0.71, 0.52-0.98, p=0.038). Both attenuated on adjustment for rs35705950 (H3 OR 1.10, 0.83-1.45, p=0.52; MUC5B H1 OR 0.82, 0.58-1.15, p=0.25). A MUC5AC H2 association persisted after adjustment (OR 0.69, 0.51-0.94, p=0.017). In TOPMed the H3 findings replicated (unadjusted OR 1.62, 1.47-1.78, p<10-15; adjusted 0.94, 0.84-1.05, p=0.26), but the rs35705950-adjusted H2 association did not: the estimate was null overall (OR 0.99, 0.88-1.11, p=0.87) and in men and women separately (1.00, 0.87-1.16; 0.97, 0.79-1.19). The MUC5B tag failed quality control in TOPMed. ConclusionsThe MUC5AC H3 and MUC5B H1 associations are not independent of rs35705950. The MUC5AC H2 association seen here did not replicate. VNTR haplogroup does not appear to contribute to IPF risk independently of rs35705950.

candidates.title: Automated Gland MRI Radiomics for Predicting Time to Pathologic Progression during Prostate Cancer Active Surveillance
candidates.abstract: Background: Repeated biopsies burden patients during prostate cancer active surveillance (AS). Existing MRI risk stratification tools avoiding biopsy remain limited by the difficulty of automated lesion segmentation. Purpose: To develop a model integrating gland MRI radiomics and clinicopathologic variables for predicting time to pathologic progression during prostate cancer AS. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-institution study included men with grade group 1 or favorable grade group 2 prostate cancer undergoing AS with fusion-targeted and systematic biopsy (2010-2025). Gland segmentation used nnU-Net; gland radiomic features were selected by LASSO-penalized survival regression to train an XGBoost accelerated failure time model. Comparator models were assessed by C-index, time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Kaplan-Meier, and decision curve analysis. Results: Of 522 men (median age, 64 years [IQR, 59-68]), 410 were assigned by site to development and 112 to internal testing. Gland segmentation Dice was 0.89 +/- 0.04. The C-index was higher for the gland radiomics model (0.77) than for clinicopathologic (0.68) and lesion radiomics (0.68) models (adjusted P [≤] .017), with the highest time-dependent AUC at 36 months (0.87 [95% CI: 0.78, 0.94]). Progression-free survival was lower in high-risk than low-risk groups (36 months, 63.9% vs 100%; 48 months, 55.4% vs 93.8%; log-rank P < .001). At a 0.25 risk threshold, 49.1% and 31.3% were low risk at 36 and 48 months (negative predictive value, 1.00; positive predictive value, 0.36). Conclusion: An automated gland radiomics model predicted time to pathologic progression during AS better than clinicopathologic and lesion-based models.

candidates.title: Longitudinal Multimodality Imaging of Cardiovascular Abnormalities Following Definitive Chemoradiation for Lung Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cardiovascular complications following definitive chemoradiation therapy (CRT) for lung cancer are well recognized, but their longitudinal imaging manifestations remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to characterize cardiovascular abnormalities across multiple imaging modalities and electrocardiography during lung cancer survivorship. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included patients treated with definitive CRT between 2013 and 2025 who underwent baseline and follow-up cardiovascular assessments. Findings from computed tomography, echocardiography, myocardial perfusion imaging, coronary angiography, and electrocardiography were categorized into exploratory, literature-informed cardiovascular phenotype domains across five follow-up intervals. Longitudinal patterns were evaluated using generalized estimating equations (GEE). and exploratory associations with clinical cardiovascular adverse events (CVAEs) were assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Results: Eighty-six patients were included (mean age, 66, SD=9.1 years; 46 women). Baseline coronary, thoracic aortic, and valvular calcification were common, affecting 72%, 88%, and 50% of patients, respectively. During the first 0-6 months, reduced LV systolic function (53%), valvular dysfunction (35%), and pericardial effusion (19%) were observed. Pericardial effusion was observed in 37% at 1-2 years, while calcification progression and pulmonary vascular abnormalities were identified during later follow-up intervals. Longitudinal analyses suggested positive associations between successive follow-up categories and calcification progression (average OR, 4.30), pulmonary artery enlargement (OR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.10-2.02; P = 0.01), right-heart abnormalities (average OR, 1.65), and arrhythmia (OR, 1.76; 95% CI, 1.30-2.38; P < 0.001). Exploratory associations between imaging abnormalities and clinical CVAEs were also observed. Conclusions: Longitudinal multimodality cardi

candidates.title: LungAI: An AI Biomarker that Refines Lung-RADS v2022 Triage of Screen-Detected Pulmonary Nodules
candidates.abstract: BackgroundThe Lung-RADS algorithm standardizes the management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules, but its risk assessment is driven chiefly by nodule size and attenuation. This misallocates a meaningful fraction of patients: a nontrivial share of small malignancies receive 12-month surveillance while large benign nodules proceed to invasive workup. Artificial intelligence (AI) may supply risk information independent of the imaging features Lung-RADS already uses. MethodsWe validated LungAI, an investigational deep learning nodule malignancy classifier not yet cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), on the held-out NLST test partition of Ardila et al. (2,747 low-dose CT examinations from 1,244 patients with [≥]1 solid or part-solid 4-30 mm nodule; 89 pathologically confirmed cancers, prevalence 3.2%). We compared discrimination against Sybil, mean nodule diameter, and estimated nodule volume. A board-certified radiologist assigned Lung-RADS v2022 categories to a positives-enriched random subset (226 eligible examinations; 78 cancers), projected to the full cohort by contingency weighting. A per-category reclassification algorithm shifted patients along the existing Lung-RADS management ladder using a-priori score cutpoints. We evaluated a separately locked follow-up configuration on examinations with a prior scan. ResultsLungAI achieved AUROC 0.92 (95% CI 0.88-0.95) and AUPRC 0.47 (0.35-0.61), outperforming Sybil ({Delta}AUROC 0.07; {Delta}AUPRC 0.18), diameter ({Delta}AUROC 0.14; {Delta}AUPRC 0.34), and volume ({Delta}AUROC 0.14; {Delta}AUPRC 0.38; all P<0.001). Against Lung-RADS v2022 scored ordinally on the weighted annotated subset, LungAI improved AUPRC ({Delta}AUPRC 0.31, P=0.003) but not AUROC ({Delta}AUROC 0.03, P=0.20). candidates.title: Large Language Models to Label CT Radiology Reports for Incidental Findings Found in Lung Cancer Screening: A Comparative Analysis
candidates.abstract: ObjectiveTo compare LLM and prompting strategies for labeling Specific Incidental Findings (SIFs) occurring during lung cancer screening, in radiology reports. Materials and MethodsIn this retrospective study, 300 CT reports from a Dutch academic hospital were included between 19th March 2003 and 28th December 2020. GPT-5, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-3.1-8B-INST, MedGemma-4B-IT, a keyword-based search method, and a radiologist labelled the reports for the presence or absence of nine SIFs. The radiologists scores were the reference standard. Each LLM was evaluated with four different prompting strategies: two without Chain-of-Thought (CoT), and two with CoT (one zero shot, one few shot). The automated labelling methods were evaluated against the radiologist primarily using Cohens Kappa, and additionally sensitivity, specificity, and F1 scores. ResultsGPT-5 achieved substantial or almost perfect agreement for seven out of nine SIFs: aortic valve disease, bronchiectasis, consolidation, coronary artery calcification, emphysema, abnormality in mediastinal lymph nodes, and thyroid abnormalities, with Cohen {kappa} values of 0.81 (0.70, 0.93), 0.97 (0.93, 1.00), 0.71 (0.62, 0.82), 0.92 (0.87, 0.96), 0.91 (0.84, 0.97), 0.71 (0.62, 0.80), and 0.92 (0.86, 0.98) respectively. For the remaining two SIFs, moderate LLM agreement was obtained with MedGemma-4B-IT and with GPT-4-Turbo with Cohen {kappa} values of 0.48 (0.40, 0.60), 0.42 (0.31, 0.58) for interstitial lung abnormalities and mediastinal mass respectively. The highest agreement was obtained with the non-CoT prompt strategies for most SIFs. ConclusionThis study demonstrated that LLMs can automatically label radiology reports with agreement ranging from almost perfect to moderate, but not one LLM - prompt combination achieved the highest agreement across all SIFs.

candidates.title: MLX-Radiomics: accelerating standardized regional and voxel-wise radiomics for CT, PET and MRI
candidates.abstract: BackgroundDifferences among radiomics implementations complicate cross-study comparisons, while voxel-wise feature extraction remains computationally demanding. We developed MLX-Radiomics to accelerate regional feature extraction and voxel-wise mapping while preserving agreement with standardized reference measurements. MethodsMLX-Radiomics implements 172 feature definitions from the Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative (IBSI), 16 extensions and the IBSI 2 image filters. We assessed agreement with IBSI reference data and evaluated numerical accuracy against independent double-precision and analytic calculations. In matched comparisons on Apple M1 Max and M5 Max systems, we used the IBSI reference CT to compare feature values, extraction time and memory use with PyRadiomics, MIRP and Flash-Radiomics, and feature values with FastRad. Separately, we compared the time required to generate voxel-wise feature maps for regions of up to 10.1 million voxels with published GPU results obtained on different hardware and images. We evaluated agreement with MIRP under published settings in a 51-patient cohort with CT, FDG PET and T1-weighted MRI. ResultsMLX-Radiomics agreed with all 2,160 IBSI reference measurements within the specified tolerances. With matching outputs, MLX-Radiomics was 2.66 to 7.27 times faster than PyRadiomics and MIRP for regional feature extraction and 198 to 218 times faster than PyRadiomics for voxel-wise mapping on a 243-voxel crop. It also outperformed the fastest Flash-Radiomics CPU configurations tested. On the M5 Max, generating 93 maps over 10.1 million voxels took 23.8 s. In the patient cohort, MLX-Radiomics and MIRP agreed on 98.0% of requested values. For tumors at the image edge, matching the libraries resampling rules substantially improved agreement. candidates.title: Effects of Sacred Dances versus Conventional Physical Training on Functional Capacity and Quality of Life in Women with Heart Failure: Protocol for a Randomized Active-Controlled Crossover Non-Inferiority Trial (RED-WHF)
candidates.abstract: This protocol describes the RED-WHF trial, a randomized, active-controlled, two-period crossover clinical trial designed to evaluate whether Sacred Dances (SD)--as a mind-body intervention--are non-inferior to conventional physical training (PT) regarding functional capacity and quality of life in women with heart failure (HF). Sedentary behavior and emotional stress significantly worsen HF prognosis, yet conventional exercise programs face barriers in patient adherence and variable motivation. Sacred Dances, a form of low-to-moderate-intensity moving meditation, may enhance physical fitness while promoting emotional well-being and spiritual connection (flourishing). We will recruit 30 sedentary women aged 18 to 70 with stable HF (NYHA class I-III) and a documented left ventricular ejection fraction. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to one of two treatment sequences: SD followed by PT, or vice versa. Each 12-week intervention phase consists of two weekly sessions, lasting 90 minutes for SD (with 60 minutes of active dancing to allow choreography instruction) and 60 minutes for PT, separated by a 3-week washout period. Primary outcomes are functional capacity (6-minute walk test [6MWT]) and health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5L Index and VAS). Secondary outcomes include adherence rates, spiritual attitudes (ARES scale), symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress (DASS-21), and perceived subjective impact (EUPI-12). Statistical planning incorporates linear mixed models (LMM) with treatment, period, and sequence fixed effects, and an intention-to-treat approach with multiple imputation for missing data. To establish non-inferiority, a 30-meter margin for the 6MWT difference will be applied. The study was approved by the local Ethics Committee (CEP/EBMSP opinion 7.443.180, CAAE: 86133125.0.0000.5544) and prospectively registered in the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC ID: RBR-85tkdz5).

candidates.title: Cytokine Signatures of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis and the Modifying Role of Clonal Hematopoiesis: A Machine-Learning and Multi-Omics Study
candidates.abstract: BackgroundImmune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) myocarditis affects up to 2% of patients on ICI and has up to a 50% mortality. Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) is a risk factor for ICI myocarditis. ObjectivesTo leverage a multi-omics approach to evaluate cytokines associated with ICI myocarditis, immunosuppression resistance, CHIP in ICI myocarditis and implicated pathways and cell type contributions. Methods236 cardio-oncology patients were enrolled, including 88 who were on ICI. Cytokine profiling from patients on ICI were sampled and analyzed using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence. Single-cell multi-omics of peripheral blood from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63) evaluated cell-type contributions of cytokines and implicated pathways. Validation of Yale proteomic analyses was done using the Stanford CYTOF dataset. ResultsTop features associated with ICI myocarditis included IL13, CXCL10, PDGF-A, CCL13, CCL17 and KITlg. Top KEGG pathways associated with ICI myocarditis and immunosuppression resistant ICI myocarditis included JAK-STAT signaling, IL17 signaling and lipid/atherosclerosis pathways. At the single-cell level, the consensus signals distinguishing myocarditis from non-myocarditis across cohorts was predominantly driven by module-level JAK-STAT, T-cell, and Toll-like receptor activation. Similar transcription gene programs were activated in CHIP carriers including modules implicated in the pro-inflammatory immune response, such as NF-kappa B, IL17, MAPK, and TNF pathways within CHIP cells spanning lymphoid (cytotoxic CD8+ NKT, and natural killer cells) and myeloid lineages. ConclusionsAcross cohorts, JAK-STAT signaling emerges as a convergent and potentially actionable axis in ICI myocarditis that is further amplified in CHIP carriers, supporting cytokine-guided risk stratification and JAK-STAT-directed immunosuppression as testable strategies.
